# Lumiose

> Lumiose is a web framework for everything from static sites and SPAs to full-stack apps: TSX with scoped CSS built in, signals, and 0 kB of JavaScript until a page needs it.

These docs match lumiose 0.2.0. Installed projects have them in `node_modules/lumiose/docs`;
`lumiose docs <topic>` prints one and `lumiose explain <code>` explains a diagnostic.

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Lumiose docs

> Lumiose is a web framework for everything from static sites and SPAs to full-stack apps: TSX with scoped CSS built in, signals, and 0 kB of JavaScript until a page needs it.

**Feels like React. Runs like vanilla JS.** Components live in `.stsx` files (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks), are set up once and
update through signals, and every route picks its rendering mode: static, server, islands or SPA.

These docs ship inside the package, so they always match the installed version. Read them from
`node_modules/lumiose/docs`, or from the terminal:

```sh
lumiose docs                    # this index
lumiose docs signals            # a topic, by name or path (concepts/signals)
lumiose docs "bind:value"       # search, when no topic matches
lumiose explain LUM2001         # the long-form explanation of a diagnostic
lumiose docs signals --format json
```

Every concept page has the same sections, in order: **Concept**, **API**, **Example**, **Common
mistakes** and **Related diagnostics**. Reference pages list every export with its signature.

## Start here

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): Create a project, configure TypeScript and Vite, and render a first component.
- [Coming from React](coming-from-react.md): Hooks mapped to signals, what goes away (the rules of hooks, dependency arrays, stale closures, memoization) and the mistakes React habits cause.
- [Upgrading from 0.1](upgrading.md): The renamed APIs (`useContext`, `<Ctx value>`, `render`, `isPending`, …) and how to migrate.

## Concepts

- [Components](concepts/components.md): Setup-once function components, props, children, refs and the `.stsx`/`.tsx`/`.ts` file types.
- [Signals and reactivity](concepts/signals.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `store`, owners, context and scheduling.
- [Sharing state](concepts/state.md): Component, context and module-scope state; recipes for stores with actions, families, persisted signals, external stores and state shared by islands.
- [JSX](concepts/jsx.md): Bindings, compiled idioms (`.map`, ternaries), `class`, `style`, events, `bind:`, `attach` and `ref`.
- [Styles](concepts/styles.md): Raw-CSS `<style>` blocks scoped by placement, `<style global>`, JS values in styles (`$name`), build-time math and runtime values.
- [Async components](concepts/async.md): `async` components on server and client, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`, re-runs and in-flight state.
- [Islands](concepts/islands.md): `client:*` directives, serializable props, slots and server-only boundaries.
- [Routing](concepts/routing.md): File routes, layouts, params, typed `href()`, error pages and the SPA router.
- [Data and actions](concepts/data-and-actions.md): Read data with async components, serve endpoints, mutate with form actions and `submit()`.
- [Server](concepts/server.md): Request context, middleware, cookies, env, redirects and error helpers.
- [Rendering modes](concepts/rendering-modes.md): `static`, `server` and `spa` routes, prerendered SPA pages, shell-first streaming, hydration and the build.
- [SVG imports](concepts/svg.md): `import Icon from "./icon.svg"` as an inline, optimised component; `title`, `currentColor`, `?url` and `?raw`.
- [Markdown and HTML imports](concepts/content.md): `.md` and `.html` files as static components; GFM, heading ids, frontmatter and its hook, scoped `<style>`, client `<script>`.
- [Head and document](concepts/head.md): `<Title>`, `<Meta>`, `<Head>` and a custom `document.stsx`.
- [Compiler and diagnostics](concepts/compiler.md): What the compiler does with `.stsx`/`.tsx`, and how `LUMxxxx` diagnostics work.
- [Testing](concepts/testing.md): Test components with Vitest and the Lumiose Vite plugin.
- [Security](concepts/security.md): A strict Content Security Policy with nonces and hashes (`lumiose({ csp: "strict" })`, `cspNonce()`), and the cross-site form check.

## Deploy

- [Overview](deploy/README.md): What `lumiose build` writes, the production settings (`PORT`, `HOST`, `ORIGIN`, `LUMIOSE_SECRET`) and how far each target's guide was verified.
- [Docker](deploy/docker.md): A multi-stage Dockerfile: `node:24-alpine`, production dependencies only, a non-root user and a health check.
- [VPS](deploy/vps.md): `@lumiose/adapter-node` under systemd or pm2, behind Caddy or nginx; what the adapter already does for compression and caching.
- [Coolify](deploy/coolify.md): Deploy from the Dockerfile with Coolify's Dockerfile build pack.

## Reference

- [`lumiose`: reactivity](reference/reactivity.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `batch`, `flush`, `untrack`, `store`, owners, context (`createContext`, `useContext`), `useId`, `getAbortSignal`, `isPending`, `isBusy`, `resource`.
- [`lumiose`: components](reference/components.md): `Suspense`, `ErrorBoundary`, `Portal`, `Dynamic`, `ref`, `Head`, `Title`, `Meta`.
- [`lumiose`: app layer](reference/app.md): `fetchJSON`, `submit`, `isSubmitting`, `actionData`, `invalidate`, `fail`, `redirect`, `notFound`, `error`, `href`, request APIs and types.
- [`lumiose`: server rendering](reference/server.md): `renderToStream`, `renderToString` and the `lumiose/server` subpath.
- [`lumiose/dom`](reference/dom.md): `render`, the compiler-runtime contract, `hydrate` (`lumiose/dom/hydrate`) and the island loader (`lumiose/dom/loader`).
- [`lumiose/router`](reference/router.md): The SPA router: `Link`, `navigate`, `isNavigating`, `searchParams` and reactive route state.
- [`@lumiose/vite`](reference/vite.md): The Vite plugin and its options.
- [JSX types and tsconfig](reference/jsx.md): `lumiose/jsx-runtime`, `lumiose/env` and the required `tsconfig.json`.
- [CLI](reference/cli.md): `lumiose dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `typegen`, `routes`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, `agents init` and `mcp`; `--format json` and exit codes.
- [MCP server](reference/mcp.md): `lumiose mcp` for coding agents: docs, `check` with fixes, routes, components, compiler output, rendered HTML and dev logs.
- [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](reference/adapter-node.md): `createServer`, `createHandler` and `createStaticHandler`: serve a build with Node.
- [Server build](reference/server-entry.md): `dist/server/entry.js`: `export default { fetch(request, platform?) }`, `ctx.platform`, `createHandler` and `config`; run it with Bun or Deno.
- [`@lumiose/query`](reference/query.md): TanStack Query for Lumiose (`useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useQueryClient`, `QueryClientProvider`), and when to use it instead of `fetchJSON`.

## Diagnostics

- [All diagnostics](errors/README.md): Every `LUMxxxx` code with its explanation and fix.

## Status of this version

Lumiose is pre-release (`0.0.0`). The docs describe the designed API; where this version does not
implement something yet, the page says so in a **Status** note. In short:

| Area                                                                                  | Status                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Signals, components, JSX compilation, client rendering (`lumiose/dom`)                | Available                                                                  |
| Async components, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`                                     | Available                                                                  |
| Server rendering (`renderToStream`), shell-first streaming, head                      | Available                                                                  |
| File routes, typegen, request handler, middleware, actions, `fetchJSON`               | Available, with `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and `@lumiose/adapter-node` |
| `<style>` blocks                                                                      | Available                                                                  |
| Islands hydration and the island loader                                               | Available                                                                  |
| SPA mode and the SPA router (`lumiose/router`)                                        | Available, with `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build`                          |
| `lumiose check`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, language server, VS Code extension | Available                                                                  |
| `lumiose mcp`                                                                         | Available                                                                  |
| `create-lumiose` (templates `minimal`, `static`, `ssr`, `spa`), `lumiose agents init` | Available                                                                  |
| `@lumiose/testing`                                                                    | Planned                                                                    |

<!-- source: getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

> Set up a Lumiose project with TypeScript and Vite 8, write a first `.stsx` component and check it with `lumiose check`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 or later.
- TypeScript (`typescript@^7`). Lumiose uses stock `tsc`, with no TypeScript plugins.
- Vite 8.

## Create a project

```sh
pnpm create lumiose my-app --template ssr   # or: minimal, static, spa
cd my-app && pnpm install && pnpm dev
```

| Template  | `lumiose({ mode })` | What you get                                                 |
| --------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `minimal` | `static`            | One page.                                                    |
| `static`  | `static`            | A layout, pages, a blog with `staticPaths()` and a 404 page. |
| `ssr`     | `server`            | Streaming, a form action, a JSON endpoint and a Node server. |
| `spa`     | `spa`               | Pages and a persistent layout rendered in the browser.       |

Every project starts agent-ready: `AGENTS.md` (with a Lumiose section pointing at these docs),
`CLAUDE.md` referencing it, the `lumiose` skill in `.claude/skills/lumiose`, and `.gitattributes`
highlighting `.stsx` as TSX. In an existing project, `lumiose agents init` writes the same files
(re-run it after upgrading Lumiose; it only touches its own parts). With `--mcp`, both also register
the [Lumiose MCP server](reference/mcp.md) for Claude Code (`.mcp.json`) and Codex
(`.codex/config.toml`). Run `create-lumiose --help` for the options (`--yes`, `--force`, `--mcp`,
`--format json`).

The rest of this page sets a project up by hand, step by step.

## 1. Install

```sh
pnpm add lumiose
pnpm add -D @lumiose/vite @lumiose/cli vite typescript
```

Lumiose ships as three packages that share one version:

- `lumiose`: the runtime your app imports (signals, the DOM and server renderers, the router, the
  app runtime). It has no dependencies.
- `@lumiose/vite`: the Vite plugin, plus the dev server and the production build behind
  `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build`.
- `@lumiose/cli`: the `lumiose` command (`dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`,
  `mcp`, …).

`@lumiose/compiler` (the native compiler) comes with them. Add
[`@lumiose/adapter-node`](reference/adapter-node.md) to preview a build (`lumiose preview`) and to
serve it on Node in production.

## 2. Configure TypeScript

`tsconfig.json` extends the tsconfig that Lumiose generates (`lumiose check` prints this file when it
is missing, and `lumiose agents init` writes it):

```jsonc
{
  // Lumiose's compiler options, shadow TSX and route types. lumiose dev, build, check and typegen
  // write the generated file; add your own options below.
  "extends": "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json",
}
```

- `.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json` sets `jsx: "preserve"` (the Lumiose compiler transforms JSX, not
  TypeScript), `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"`, bundler module resolution, `strict`, `types:
  ["lumiose/env"]`, and the `rootDirs` and `include` entries below. Lumiose keeps it current.
- `.lumiose/shadow`: TypeScript cannot read `.stsx`, so Lumiose writes a masked copy of each one (a
  _shadow file_, same line and column offsets) and `import "./X.stsx"` resolves to it.
- `.lumiose/types`: generated route types (`lumiose typegen`, run by `lumiose check`).
- `lumiose dev`, `build`, `check` and `typegen` write `.lumiose/`. Before a bare `tsc` in a fresh
  clone, run `lumiose typegen`. See [tsconfig](./reference/jsx.md#tsconfigjson).

Add `.lumiose/` to `.gitignore`, and `*.stsx linguist-language=TSX` to `.gitattributes` so GitHub
highlights `.stsx` files.

## 3. Configure Vite

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumiose()],
});
```

## 4. Write a component

```stsx check file=Counter.stsx
// src/Counter.stsx
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Counter({ start = 0 }: { start?: number }) {
  const count = signal(start);

  return (
    <button class={{ hot: count() > 5 }} onClick={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>
      Clicked {count()} times
    </button>
  );
}

<style>
  button { font: inherit; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; }
  .hot { color: crimson; }
</style>
```

- The function body runs **once**. `count()` reads the signal; JSX that reads it updates on its own.
- The `<style>` block at the end of the file is scoped to this file: it styles the components
  defined here, and nothing else. One block per file, after the components, is the convention;
  [Styles](./concepts/styles.md) covers blocks nested in JSX.

## 5. Mount it

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<div id="app"></div>
<script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
```

```tsx check file=main.tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { render } from "lumiose/dom";
import { Counter } from "./Counter.stsx";

render(() => <Counter start={1} />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

Run `pnpm vite` and open the printed URL.

## 6. Check the project

```sh
pnpm lumiose check        # typegen + shadow files + tsc + Lumiose diagnostics
pnpm lumiose lint         # oxlint, .stsx included
pnpm lumiose fmt          # oxfmt for the TSX, plus each <style> block
```

`lumiose check` maps every TypeScript error in a shadow file back to the `.stsx` line and column.
`--format json` prints machine-readable diagnostics; every Lumiose diagnostic has a stable code that
`lumiose explain <code>` explains.

## Editor

Install the Lumiose VS Code extension (`lumiose-vscode`). It adds the `stsx` language and runs the
Lumiose language server, which proxies TypeScript for `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.stsx` files and adds:

- CSS features inside `<style>` blocks;
- class completion, definitions and rename that follow placement: the blocks enclosing the
  cursor (never a sibling subtree's), the file's, and the project's global classes (`<style global>`
  blocks and imported global `.css` files);
- `var(--…)` completion of every custom property declared in the project, with its value;
- descriptions of `<style global>` and of Lumiose attributes (`client:*`, `bind:*`, `on:*`, `attach`,
  `ref`, `key`), and the snippets `comp`, `acomp`, `route` and `island`;
- the compiler's diagnostics, with the project-wide ones (`LUM4003` server-only imports in the
  client graph, `LUM3012` unread custom properties) that follow the other files' edits;
- hovers on JSX expressions with their execution contract: tracked (re-runs when the signals it
  reads change, which it lists), once, untracked or deferred, and the runtime helper that runs it.

The extension bundles the server (it runs on VS Code's own Node.js) and uses the project's
`typescript`; install `@lumiose/language-server` as a dev dependency only to pin the server to your
`lumiose` version. See [Compiler and diagnostics](concepts/compiler.md).

## Next

- [Components](concepts/components.md) and [Signals](concepts/signals.md): the component model.
- [Styles](concepts/styles.md): scoping by placement, JS values in styles and build-time math.
- [Rendering modes](concepts/rendering-modes.md): server-first pages with islands.

<!-- source: coming-from-react.md -->

# Coming from React

> Lumiose JSX reads like React, but a component's body runs once, as setup, and never re-renders. The rules of hooks, dependency arrays, stale closures and memoization go away. A few new mistakes take their place, and the compiler flags most of them.

This page maps React habits to Lumiose. The linked pages have the full rules.

## Mental model

In React, a state change re-runs the component function. Hooks keep their state between runs
by call order, and effects list their dependencies so React knows when to re-run them.

In Lumiose, the component body runs **once per instance**: it creates signals, effects and
handlers, then returns JSX. JSX expressions that read signals compile to bindings that update
their part of the DOM in place. When a signal changes, only the bindings, computeds and effects
that read it run again. Local variables are ordinary variables, and a closure reads the current
value because it calls `count()` when it runs ([Components](concepts/components.md),
[Signals](concepts/signals.md)).

The exception is an **async component**: when a prop or signal read in its body changes, the body
runs again, and signals created in the body start fresh ([Async components](concepts/async.md)).

## From React to Lumiose

| React                                                 | Lumiose                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `const [count, setCount] = useState(0)`               | `const count = signal(0)`: read `count()`, write `count.set(1)` or `count.update((n) => n + 1)`.                                                |
| `useReducer(reducer, init)`                           | A `store()` plus the functions that change it ([a store with actions](concepts/state.md#a-store-with-actions-zustand-style)).                   |
| `useMemo(() => a * b, [a, b])`                        | `computed(() => a() * b())`, or a plain function `() => a() * b()` for cheap derivations.                                                       |
| `useCallback(fn, deps)`, `React.memo(Component)`      | Not needed: functions are created once and components don't re-render.                                                                          |
| `useEffect(fn, [deps])`                               | `effect(fn)`: it tracks what it reads. Return a cleanup, as in React.                                                                           |
| `useEffect(fn, [])`                                   | `onMount(fn)`: runs once, untracked, after mount. It may return a cleanup.                                                                      |
| `useLayoutEffect(fn, deps)`                           | `effect(fn)` or `onMount(fn)`: there is one kind of effect, and it runs after the DOM writes of the same flush.                                 |
| Cleanup returned from `useEffect`, `AbortController`  | `onCleanup(fn)`, and `getAbortSignal()`, aborted when the owner is disposed or the effect re-runs.                                              |
| `useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)`                      | `const input = ref<HTMLInputElement>()`, then `<input ref={input} />` and `input()?.focus()`.                                                   |
| `useRef(value)` for a mutable value                   | A `let` variable in the component body: the body runs once.                                                                                     |
| `<Ctx.Provider value={v}>`, `useContext(Ctx)`         | `<Ctx value={v}>`, `useContext(Ctx)`. The provider reads `value` once: provide a signal or a store for state that changes.                      |
| `useId()`, `identifierPrefix`                         | `useId()`, and `idPrefix` on `render()` and `renderToStream()` ([useId](reference/reactivity.md#useid)).                                        |
| `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, get)`                | A signal set from the store's `subscribe` ([an external store](concepts/state.md#an-external-store-zustandvanilla-a-jotai-store-redux)).        |
| Fetching in `useEffect`, TanStack Query               | An `async` component that awaits `fetchJSON()` or `query()` ([Async components](concepts/async.md)), or [`@lumiose/query`](reference/query.md). |
| `useTransition`, `isPending`                          | `isPending()` inside an async component, and `isBusy()` for anything in flight.                                                                 |
| `useOptimistic(state, update)`                        | `optimistic(source)` ([Data and actions](concepts/data-and-actions.md)).                                                                        |
| `<Suspense>`, error boundary classes                  | `<Suspense fallback={…}>` and `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>`.                                                                 |
| `createPortal(children, node)`                        | `<Portal mount={node}>`.                                                                                                                        |
| `{items.map((item) => <Row key={item.id} />)}`        | The same, with `items()`. It compiles to a keyed list; `key` is optional ([JSX](concepts/jsx.md)).                                              |
| `className`, `htmlFor`, `style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}` | `class`, `for`, `style={{ "font-weight": 600 }}` (kebab-case keys).                                                                             |
| `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }}`          | `innerHTML={html}`.                                                                                                                             |
| `onChange` on a text input (fires on every keystroke) | `onInput`, or `bind:value={signal}`. Handlers get native events, so `onChange` fires when the value is committed.                               |

## What goes away

- **The rules of hooks.** `signal`, `computed`, `effect` and `onCleanup` are ordinary functions:
  call them in conditions, loops and helper functions. Nothing depends on call order.
- **Dependency arrays.** Effects and computeds subscribe to the signals they read, and collect them
  again on every run, so a dependency cannot be missing, and a branch that stops reading a signal
  stops depending on it.
- **Stale closures.** A handler or a timer callback calls `count()` when it runs, so it gets the
  current value. There is no closure from an older render to capture.
- **Memoization.** `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `React.memo` exist to limit re-renders, and there
  are none. Use `computed` only to cache an expensive derivation.
- **Context re-renders.** A context change does not re-render its consumers: provide a signal or a
  store, and only the code that reads it updates.

## Mistakes that replace them

| React habit                                                 | What happens in Lumiose                                 | Instead                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `const doubled = count() * 2` in the body                   | Computed once, never updates.                           | `const doubled = () => count() * 2`, or `computed` ([LUM2001](errors/LUM2001.md)).         |
| `if (!user()) return <Login />`                             | Checked once, at setup.                                 | `{user() ? <Profile /> : <Login />}` in the JSX ([LUM2003](errors/LUM2003.md)).            |
| `count.set(…)` in the body                                  | A write during render.                                  | Write in handlers and effects ([LUM2002](errors/LUM2002.md)).                              |
| `effect(() => b.set(a() * 2))` to sync state                | A frame of staleness and an extra flush.                | `const b = computed(() => a() * 2)`.                                                       |
| Reading a signal in an effect only to use its current value | The effect re-runs whenever that signal changes.        | `untrack(() => s())` or `s.peek()` reads without subscribing.                              |
| Asserting right after a write in a test                     | Effects run after the DOM updates, not synchronously.   | Call `flush()` before asserting.                                                           |
| `{Card({ title })}`                                         | Skips the component's owner and props handling.         | `<Card title={title} />` ([LUM2004](errors/LUM2004.md)).                                   |
| `{children}` inserted twice                                 | The second insert moves or re-creates the nodes.        | Take a render prop such as `renderItem: () => JSX.Element` ([LUM2005](errors/LUM2005.md)). |
| A signal created and read in an async component's body      | The read re-runs the body, which re-creates the signal. | Read it in JSX, handlers or effects ([LUM2007](errors/LUM2007.md)).                        |
| A module-scope signal written on the server                 | Shared by every request.                                | Component state, context or `defineState` ([LUM4008](errors/LUM4008.md)).                  |

Destructuring props is fine: `({ title })` compiles to reads of `props.title`, which stay reactive.
Copying a signal's value into a variable is what freezes it.

## Example

A clock that pauses, in React:

```tsx
function Clock({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(Date.now());
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (paused) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [paused]);

  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = `${label}: ${new Date(now).toLocaleTimeString()}`;
  }, [label, now]);

  const toggle = useCallback(() => setPaused((p) => !p), []);
  return <button onClick={toggle}>{paused ? "Resume" : "Pause"}</button>;
}
```

The same clock in Lumiose. The effects list no dependencies, and the handler needs no
`useCallback`:

```tsx check
import { effect, signal } from "lumiose";

export function Clock({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const now = signal(Date.now());
  const paused = signal(false);

  // Reads paused(): re-runs, after clearing the interval, when it flips.
  effect(() => {
    if (paused()) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => now.set(Date.now()), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  });

  // Reads label (props.label) and now(): re-runs when either changes.
  effect(() => {
    document.title = `${label}: ${new Date(now()).toLocaleTimeString()}`;
  });

  return <button onClick={() => paused.update((p) => !p)}>{paused() ? "Resume" : "Pause"}</button>;
}
```

- [JSX](concepts/jsx.md): bindings, compiled `.map()` and ternaries, and the React prop names that differ.
- [Sharing state](concepts/state.md): context, `defineState`, and what replaces Jotai, Zustand and Valtio.
- [Async components](concepts/async.md): data loading, re-runs, `<Suspense>` and `isPending()`.

<!-- source: upgrading.md -->

# Upgrading from 0.1

> The next release renames several APIs to the names React, Solid and Svelte use for the same behavior. The old names are removed, with no aliases: this page lists every rename and how to migrate.

The renames change names only, except context, where `provide()` becomes a provider component.
Type errors point at every place to update: `lumiose check` (or `tsc`) reports each old import as a
missing export.

## Migration table

| 0.1                                                | Now                                                                        | Entry            |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `inject(Ctx)`                                      | `useContext(Ctx)`                                                          | `lumiose`        |
| `provide(Ctx, value)`                              | `<Ctx value={value}>…</Ctx>`                                               | `lumiose`        |
| `lifetime()`                                       | `getAbortSignal()`                                                         | `lumiose`        |
| `pending()`                                        | `isPending()`                                                              | `lumiose`        |
| `busy()`                                           | `isBusy()`                                                                 | `lumiose`        |
| `submitting(name?)`                                | `isSubmitting(name?)`                                                      | `lumiose`        |
| `flushSync()`                                      | `flush()`                                                                  | `lumiose`        |
| `navigating()`                                     | `isNavigating()`                                                           | `lumiose/router` |
| `search()`, `search.set()`, `Search`, `SearchInit` | `searchParams()`, `searchParams.set()`, `SearchParams`, `SearchParamsInit` | `lumiose/router` |
| `mount(code, container)`                           | `render(code, container)`                                                  | `lumiose/dom`    |

Signatures and behavior are unchanged, apart from context.

## Context: `provide()` becomes `<Ctx value>`

`createContext()` returns a provider component, as in React 19 and Solid 2. Instead of calling
`provide()` in a component body, wrap the subtree that should see the value:

```tsx
// 0.1
export function Shop() {
  provide(CartContext, createCart());
  return <Products />;
}

// Now
export function Shop() {
  return (
    <CartContext value={createCart()}>
      <Products />
    </CartContext>
  );
}
```

Differences to keep in mind:

- The value reaches the provider's children only. A component that called `provide()` and then
  read the context itself with `inject()` now reads it in a component inside the provider.
- The provider reads `value` once, when it renders, as before: to share changing state, provide a
  signal, a store or an object with getters.
- Islands still start a new context root: a provider in the page does not reach an island
  ([LUM4010](errors/LUM4010.md)).

## Other changes

- **App entries and HMR.** With `@lumiose/vite`, an app entry is detected by its `render` import
  from `lumiose/dom` (it was `mount`). Rename the import and the entry keeps re-rendering on hot
  updates.
- **`ErrorBoundary`.** The docs call the fallback's second argument `reset` (it was `retry`), as
  Solid and react-error-boundary do. It is only a parameter name: existing code keeps working.
- **`url()`, `params()`, `route()`.** Unchanged. Those of `lumiose` read the request and are
  server-only (`LUM4003` in the browser); those of `lumiose/router` are reactive and work in the
  browser too.

See also: [Signals and reactivity](concepts/signals.md), [Sharing state](concepts/state.md),
[`lumiose`: reactivity](reference/reactivity.md).

<!-- source: concepts/components.md -->

# Components

> A component is a PascalCase function that returns JSX. Its body runs once, as setup; signals make the JSX update in place.

## Concept

**Files.** Components live in `.stsx` files (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks) or plain `.tsx`
files. A file may export many components. Logic, tokens, endpoints and server code live in `.ts`.

| Extension | Contents                                                              |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.stsx`   | TSX plus `<style>` blocks. Use it for components with styles.         |
| `.tsx`    | Plain TSX. A `<style>` block here is `LUM1006` ("rename to `.stsx`"). |
| `.ts`     | Everything else.                                                      |

**Setup once.** The body of a component runs once per instance. There is no re-render: JSX
expressions that read signals become fine-grained bindings, and only those update. Local variables
are ordinary variables; state that changes lives in [signals](signals.md).

**Props.** Props are the single parameter. The compiler keeps them reactive, even when you
destructure them: `({ title, count = 0 })` is rewritten to reads of `props.title` and
`props.count`, so a parent passing a signal value keeps the child up to date. `...rest` stays
reactive too.

On the server, where nothing is reactive, a prop expression is evaluated **lazily and at most once
per component instance** (decision-28): the first read runs it, later reads reuse the value, and a
prop the component never reads never runs. `<Filters labels={listLabels()} />` queries the labels
once per render however often `Filters` reads `props.labels`. In the browser props stay live: each
read re-evaluates the expression, so keep prop expressions free of side effects.

**Children** are lazy: `children` is evaluated where you insert it. Insert it once; to render
something several times, take a render function as a prop. Named slots are ordinary props that hold
JSX.

**Refs.** `ref` takes a callback `(el) => void`. `ref<T>()` returns such a callback that can also be
read like a signal.

**Async.** Any component may be `async` and `await` data in its body; see
[Async components](async.md).

## API

| API                                     | Use                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `function Name(props) { return <… /> }` | A component. PascalCase, returns JSX.                                           |
| `children` prop                         | Lazy content passed between the tags. Insert once.                              |
| `ref<T>()`                              | A ref callback that reads like a signal (`input()`), `undefined` until mounted. |
| `useId()`                               | A unique id for `id`/`for` and `aria-*` pairs, the same after hydration.        |
| `onMount(fn)`, `onCleanup(fn)`          | Run after mount; run when the component is disposed.                            |
| `<Dynamic component={X} … />`           | Render a component (or tag name) chosen at runtime.                             |
| `<Portal mount={node}>`                 | Render children elsewhere in the document.                                      |

Types: a component's return type is `JSX.Element`. Props are a plain interface; `children?:
JSX.Element` for content.

## Example

```stsx check
import { onMount, ref, signal } from "lumiose";

interface Props {
  label: string;
  initial?: string;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}

export function SearchBox({ label, initial = "", children }: Props) {
  const query = signal(initial);
  const input = ref<HTMLInputElement>();

  onMount(() => input()?.focus());

  return (
    <form class="search" onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
      <label>
        {label}
        <input ref={input} bind:value={query} />
      </label>
      <p>Searching for “{query()}”</p>
      {children}
    </form>
  );
}

export function Page() {
  return (
    <SearchBox label="Books">
      <small>Try “Dune”.</small>
    </SearchBox>
  );
}

<style>
  .search { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; }
</style>
```

Both components share the `<style>` block at the end of the file: by convention, each `.stsx`
file has one, after its components ([Styles](styles.md)).

## Common mistakes

- **Reading a signal once in setup and expecting it to update.** `const doubled = count() * 2`
  is computed once. Use a function or `computed`: `const doubled = () => count() * 2`. The compiler
  warns with `LUM2001`.
- **Returning early on reactive state.** `if (!user()) return <Login />` runs once. Put the
  condition in the JSX: `{user() ? <Profile /> : <Login />}` (`LUM2003`).
- **Calling a component as a function.** `{Card({ title })}` skips the component's owner and
  props handling. Write `<Card title={title} />` (`LUM2004`).
- **Inserting `children` twice.** The second insert moves or re-creates the nodes. Take a render
  prop such as `renderItem: () => JSX.Element` instead (`LUM2005`).
- **Writing a signal in the component body.** Setup runs during render; a write there
  (`count.set(…)`) re-triggers bindings mid-render. Write in handlers or effects (`LUM2002`).
- **Expecting React re-renders.** There are no hooks rules and no dependency arrays: nothing
  re-runs except bindings and effects that read signals.
- **`className`, `htmlFor`.** Use `class` and `for`; the React names are type errors.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1006](../errors/LUM1006.md): raw CSS in a `.tsx` file.
- [LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md): stale derived value.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.
- [LUM2003](../errors/LUM2003.md): reactive early return.
- [LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md): component called as a function.
- [LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md): children inserted twice.

See also: [JSX](jsx.md), [Signals](signals.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/signals.md -->

# Signals and reactivity

> State lives in signals: read with `count()`, write with `count.set(v)`. Computeds derive, effects react, and only the code that read a signal re-runs.

## Concept

Lumiose's reactive core is a push-pull signal graph (the alien-signals algorithm). Reading a signal
inside a tracked scope (a JSX binding, a `computed`, an `effect`) subscribes that scope; writing
the signal marks it dirty and re-runs only what depends on it.

- **Reads are synchronous.** `count()` always returns the current value, even right after a write.
- **Writes are batched.** Writes inside a delegated event handler are batched for the duration of
  the handler. Any other write schedules a microtask flush. `flush()` flushes immediately.
- **Flush order:** computeds are pulled, then DOM bindings run (parents before children), then user
  effects.
- **Owners.** Every component, effect and root is an _owner_. Owners scope cleanups
  (`onCleanup`), context (`<Ctx value>`/`useContext`), error handling and `getAbortSignal()`. Disposing an owner
  disposes everything created under it.
- **Equality.** A write that is `Object.is`-equal to the current value is not a change. Pass
  `{ equals }` to customize, or `{ equals: false }` to treat every write as a change.
- **On the server** signals are plain cells, computeds run once, and effects never run.

## API

| API                                                             | Shape                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal(value, { equals? })`                                    | `s()` reads, `s.set(v)` and `s.update(fn)` write, `s.peek()` reads untracked.                                                               |
| `computed(fn, { equals? })`                                     | `c()` reads. Lazy, cached and glitch-free; `fn` receives the previous value.                                                                |
| `effect(fn)`                                                    | Runs after the DOM updates and again when what it read changes. `fn` may return a cleanup. Returns a disposer.                              |
| `onMount(fn)`                                                   | Runs `fn` once, untracked, after the owner's DOM is mounted. May return a cleanup.                                                          |
| `onCleanup(fn)`                                                 | Runs `fn` when the current owner is disposed or re-runs.                                                                                    |
| `store(obj)`                                                    | Deep, mutable reactive proxy over a plain object or array (like Valtio's `proxy` or Solid's `createMutable`): mutate it directly.           |
| `snapshot(value)`                                               | A deep plain copy of a store, for `structuredClone`, `postMessage` and saving.                                                              |
| `untrack(fn)`                                                   | Runs `fn` without subscribing to what it reads.                                                                                             |
| `batch(fn)`                                                     | Groups writes; dependents run once at the end.                                                                                              |
| `flush()`                                                       | Runs pending bindings and effects now.                                                                                                      |
| `getAbortSignal()`                                              | An `AbortSignal` aborted when the owner is disposed, an effect re-runs, or an async run is superseded. On the server, the request's signal. |
| `createContext(default?)`, `<Ctx value={v}>`, `useContext(ctx)` | Values passed down the owner tree; they survive `await`. The provider reads `value` once: provide a signal or store for changing state.     |
| `resource(fetcher)`                                             | Low-level on-demand loading with `loading()`, `error()`, `refetch()`. Prefer [async components](async.md).                                  |

In-flight state (`isPending()`, `isBusy()`, `isSubmitting()`, `isNavigating()`) is covered in
[Async components](async.md) and [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).

## Example

```tsx check
import { computed, createContext, effect, signal, store, useContext } from "lumiose";

const Theme = createContext<"light" | "dark">("light");

export function Cart() {
  const items = store([{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 1 }]);
  const discount = signal(0);
  const total = computed(
    () => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.qty, 0) * (1 - discount()),
  );

  effect(() => {
    document.title = `Cart: ${total().toFixed(2)}`;
  });

  return (
    <Theme value="dark">
      <section>
        <button onClick={() => items.push({ name: "Ink", price: 5, qty: 1 })}>Add ink</button>
        <button onClick={() => (items[0]!.qty += 1)}>One more pen</button>
        <button onClick={() => discount.set(0.1)}>Apply 10%</button>
        <p>Total: {total().toFixed(2)}</p>
        <ThemeLabel />
      </section>
    </Theme>
  );
}

function ThemeLabel() {
  const theme = useContext(Theme);
  return <small>Theme: {theme}</small>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Destructuring or copying a signal's value in setup.** `const n = count()` freezes the value.
  Read `count()` where you need it, or derive: `const double = () => count() * 2` (`LUM2001`).
- **Calling `set` with the same object after mutating it.** `list().push(x); list.set(list())` is
  not a change (`Object.is`). Write a new value (`list.update((l) => [...l, x])`), use `store()`,
  or create the signal with `{ equals: false }`.
- **Writing signals in the component body or in a `computed`.** That is a write during render
  (`LUM2002`). Computeds must be pure; write in handlers and effects.
- **Using `effect` to derive state.** `effect(() => b.set(a() * 2))` adds a frame of staleness and
  an extra flush. Use `computed(() => a() * 2)`.
- **Expecting an effect to run synchronously.** Effects run after the DOM updates. In tests, call
  `flush()` after a write before asserting.
- **Module-scope signals in server code.** On the server, a signal at module scope is shared by
  every request. Keep request data in components or context (`LUM4008`).
- **Posting a store to a worker.** `postMessage()` and `structuredClone()` throw on proxies: send
  `snapshot(state)`.
- **Expecting `store()` to wrap class instances, `Map`s or `Set`s.** Only plain objects and arrays
  become reactive; other values are returned as is.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md): stale derived value.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.
- [LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md): own signal read in an async body.
- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.

See also: [reference: reactivity](../reference/reactivity.md), [JSX bindings](jsx.md), [Sharing state](state.md).

<!-- source: concepts/state.md -->

# Sharing state

> Signals already do what Jotai, Zustand and Valtio do: keep state in a component, pass it down with context, or share it with `defineState`: one instance per page in the browser, one per request on the server, sent to the islands. This page shows where state should live, with recipes for stores with actions, families, persistence, external stores and state shared by islands.

## Concept

**Pick the narrowest place that works.**

| Where                                            | Lives as long as          | Shared with                                 | On the server                              |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| A component (`signal`, `store` in setup)         | the component             | its children, through props                 | one per request: safe                      |
| Context (`<Ctx value>` / `useContext`)           | the provider              | everything rendered inside it               | one per request: safe                      |
| Scoped state (`export const s = defineState(…)`) | the page (in the browser) | every component and island that calls `s()` | one per request, sent to the islands: safe |
| Module scope (`export const s = signal()`)       | the page (in the browser) | every component and island that imports it  | one per process: never write it during SSR |

**No state library needed.** Only the code that reads a signal (or a store property) re-runs, so
selectors and re-render tuning are not needed. What the popular libraries offer maps to:

| Library feature                                      | In Lumiose                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Jotai `atom(v)`, derived atoms                       | `signal(v)`, `computed(fn)`                                                       |
| Jotai `atomFamily`                                   | a `store` keyed by id, or the family recipe below                                 |
| Jotai `atomWithStorage`, Zustand `persist`           | the persisted signal recipe below                                                 |
| Jotai `Provider`, Zustand `createStore` with context | a store with actions, provided through context (recipe below)                     |
| Zustand selectors, `subscribeWithSelector`           | not needed: `computed` for the slice, `effect` to react to it                     |
| Zustand `immer` middleware                           | `store()`: a mutable proxy, mutate it directly                                    |
| Zustand `devtools`                                   | `effect(() => console.debug(JSON.stringify(state)))` (tracks every property read) |
| Valtio `proxy`, `snapshot`                           | `store`, `snapshot`                                                               |
| Solid `reconcile`, TanStack structural sharing       | `reconcile(store, data)`: patch fresh data in, keeping unchanged items            |
| `zustand/vanilla`, a Jotai store, Redux              | the external store recipe below                                                   |

**Islands.** Each [island](islands.md) hydrates as its own root, so context provided by the page
does not reach an island, and one island cannot provide to another. The server renders islands
the same way, so their HTML matches. Islands share the Lumiose runtime and the modules they import,
so islands share state through **scoped state**: `defineState(factory)` returns an accessor whose
factory runs on first use, once per page in the browser and once per request on the server.

**Scoped state on the server.** The factory runs per request, so it can seed itself from the
request (`cookies()`, `locals()`, …); there is no separate seed API. When islands (or SPA routes)
import a state, the page sends its server values: the signals and stores the factory returned,
once per page, in the chunk where the state was first used. In the browser the factory runs again
(rebuilding computeds and functions) and the server values replace its signals and stores before
any island reads them, so hydration matches. A state that only server code imports is never sent.
Sent values must be plain data, like island props (`LUM4011`), and they are **public**: everyone
who can load the page can read them in its source. Never put secrets in a state that islands use.

**Scoped state in tests.** Under Vitest, `@lumiose/vite` resets scoped state before each test: each
test starts with fresh instances, in DOM tests and in server tests (where calls outside a render
share one instance per test).

## API

| API                                                        | Use it for                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal(v)`, `computed(fn)`, `store(obj)`                  | The state itself and what derives from it.                           |
| `createContext<T>()`, `<Ctx value={v}>`, `useContext(ctx)` | One instance per subtree (and per request on the server).            |
| `defineState(factory)`                                     | One instance per page, per request on the server; shared by islands. |
| `effect(fn)`, `onMount(fn)`                                | Syncing with the outside world (storage, logging); browser only.     |
| `onCleanup(fn)`                                            | Ending a subscription when its owner is disposed.                    |
| `snapshot(value)`                                          | A plain copy of a store, to save or send. Its reads are not tracked. |
| `reconcile(store, data, { key })`                          | Patching fresh data into a store, keeping unchanged items as is.     |

See [Signals and reactivity](signals.md) for each API.

## Example

### A store with actions (Zustand-style)

A function creates the state and returns it with the functions that change it. Provide one
instance through context: every component below shares it, each request on the server gets its
own, and tests call `createCart()` directly.

```tsx check
import { computed, createContext, store, useContext } from "lumiose";

export function createCart() {
  const state = store({ items: [] as { id: string; qty: number }[] });
  return {
    state,
    count: computed(() => state.items.reduce((n, item) => n + item.qty, 0)),
    add(id: string) {
      const item = state.items.find((item) => item.id === id);
      if (item) item.qty += 1;
      else state.items.push({ id, qty: 1 });
    },
    clear() {
      state.items = [];
    },
  };
}

export type Cart = ReturnType<typeof createCart>;

const CartContext = createContext<Cart>();

export function getCart(): Cart {
  const cart = useContext(CartContext);
  if (cart === undefined) throw new Error("getCart() needs a <Shop> above it.");
  return cart;
}

export function Shop() {
  return (
    <CartContext value={createCart()}>
      <main>
        <AddButton id="pen" />
        <CartCount />
      </main>
    </CartContext>
  );
}

function AddButton({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const cart = getCart();
  return <button onClick={() => cart.add(id)}>Add {id}</button>;
}

function CartCount() {
  const cart = getCart();
  return <p>{cart.count()} items</p>;
}
```

### State shared by islands (defineState)

Define the state at module scope with `defineState` and call its accessor wherever it is used. The
server seeds it from the request; the islands start from the server's values and share one
instance in the browser.

```ts check file=lib/cart.ts
import { computed, cookies, defineState, isServer, store } from "lumiose";

export interface CartItem {
  id: string;
  qty: number;
}

export const cart = defineState(() => {
  // Request APIs exist only on the server; the browser gets the server's values instead.
  const saved = isServer ? cookies().get("cart") : undefined;
  const state = store({ items: saved ? (JSON.parse(saved) as CartItem[]) : [] });
  return {
    state, // sent to the browser (a store)
    count: computed(() => state.items.reduce((n, item) => n + item.qty, 0)), // derived again
    add(id: string) {
      const item = state.items.find((item) => item.id === id);
      if (item) item.qty += 1;
      else state.items.push({ id, qty: 1 });
    },
  };
});
```

```stsx check file=components/CartIslands.stsx
import { cart } from "../lib/cart.ts";

export function AddToCart(props: { id: string }) {
  const { add } = cart();
  return <button onClick={() => add(props.id)}>Add to cart</button>;
}

export function CartBadge() {
  const { count } = cart();
  return <span class="badge">{count()}</span>;
}
```

```stsx check file=routes/shop-islands.stsx
import { AddToCart, CartBadge } from "../components/CartIslands.stsx";
import { cart } from "../lib/cart.ts";

export const mode = "server";

export default function ShopPage() {
  return (
    <main>
      <header>
        Cart <CartBadge client:idle />
      </header>
      <p>{cart().count()} items, rendered on the server for this request</p>
      <AddToCart client:visible id="pen" />
    </main>
  );
}
```

What the page sends is `cart`'s store (`{ items: [...] }`): `count` and `add` are created again in
the browser. `@lumiose/vite` names each state after its module and export
(`/src/lib/cart.ts#cart`), the way it names islands, so define states at module scope and export
them (or the binding). For state that lives only in the browser, a module-scope `signal` works too,
as long as it is written only in handlers and effects, which never run on the server.

### Families (atomFamily)

A `store` tracks each key separately, so a record keyed by id is already a family: setting
`selected[id]` re-runs only what read that id.

```ts check
import { store } from "lumiose";

export const selected = store<Record<string, boolean>>({});
// selected["todo-1"] = true; re-runs only the bindings that read selected["todo-1"]
```

When each entry must be a signal of its own (to pass it to a component, or to derive from it),
create them on first use:

```ts check
import { signal, type Signal } from "lumiose";

export function family<K, T>(initial: (key: K) => T) {
  const signals = new Map<K, Signal<T>>();
  return {
    get(key: K): Signal<T> {
      let entry = signals.get(key);
      if (entry === undefined) signals.set(key, (entry = signal(initial(key))));
      return entry;
    },
    delete(key: K): void {
      signals.delete(key);
    },
  };
}

export const drafts = family((_postId: string) => "");
// drafts.get("post-1").set("Hello"); drafts.get("post-1")()
```

### Fresh data into a store (reconcile)

Replacing a store's array with a new fetch result (`state.books = fresh`) gives every row a new
object, so a list re-renders every row and loses its local state. `reconcile` patches the data in
instead: rows are matched by `id` (or by `{ key }`), unchanged rows keep their identity, and only
the fields that changed notify.

```ts check
import { reconcile, store } from "lumiose";

interface Book {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

export const books = store<Book[]>([]);

export async function refresh(): Promise<void> {
  const fresh = (await (await fetch("/api/books")).json()) as Book[];
  reconcile(books, fresh); // only changed titles and added or removed rows update the page
}
```

It works on a part of a store too: `reconcile(state.books, fresh)`. Keys missing from the new
data are deleted, nested objects are merged, and other values are replaced.

### A persisted signal (atomWithStorage, persist)

Call it in a component. The saved value loads in `onMount`, after hydration, so the server HTML
and the first browser render agree; other tabs stay in sync through the `storage` event.

```tsx check
import { effect, onMount, signal, type Signal } from "lumiose";

export function persisted<T>(key: string, initial: T): Signal<T> {
  const value = signal(initial);
  let loaded = false;
  onMount(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(key);
    if (saved !== null) value.set(JSON.parse(saved) as T);
    loaded = true;
    const sync = (event: StorageEvent) => {
      if (event.key === key && event.newValue !== null) value.set(JSON.parse(event.newValue) as T);
    };
    window.addEventListener("storage", sync);
    return () => window.removeEventListener("storage", sync);
  });
  effect(() => {
    const current = value();
    if (loaded) localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(current));
  });
  return value;
}

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const theme = persisted<"light" | "dark">("theme", "light");
  return (
    <button onClick={() => theme.update((t) => (t === "light" ? "dark" : "light"))}>
      Theme: {theme()}
    </button>
  );
}
```

In a `client:only` island or an SPA, which render nothing on the server, you can read
`localStorage` directly in `signal(…)` instead.

### An external store (zustand/vanilla, a Jotai store, Redux)

Mirror any store with `getState()` and `subscribe()` into a signal. Call it in a component (or
under another owner) so the subscription ends with it.

```ts check
import { onCleanup, signal } from "lumiose";

export interface ExternalStore<T> {
  getState(): T;
  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
}

export function fromStore<T>(source: ExternalStore<T>): () => T {
  const state = signal(source.getState());
  onCleanup(source.subscribe(() => state.set(source.getState())));
  return state;
}
```

A `zustand/vanilla` store fits as it is: `fromStore(bearStore)`. For a Jotai store, adapt one
atom: `fromStore({ getState: () => jotai.get(countAtom), subscribe: (fn) => jotai.sub(countAtom, fn) })`.
Derive slices with `computed(() => state().bears)`.

## Common mistakes

- **Writing module-scope state during SSR.** A module-scope signal written in a component body or
  a server path leaks one request's state into the next (`LUM4008`). Use `defineState`, whose
  factory runs once per request, or keep it in context.
- **Reading page context inside an island.** Each island starts a new context root, on the
  server as in the browser, so `useContext()` inside it does not see what the page provided outside
  it and returns the context's default (`LUM4010` warns in dev). Pass the value as an island prop,
  provide the context inside the island, or share scoped state (`defineState`).
- **Calling request APIs in a state's factory without a guard.** The factory also runs in the
  browser, where `cookies()` and `locals()` throw `LUM4003`. Read them only on the server
  (`isServer ? cookies().get("cart") : undefined`); the server's values arrive anyway.
- **Putting secrets or class instances in a state that islands use.** Its signals and stores are
  sent with the page, readable by anyone, and must hold plain data (`LUM4011`). Keep secrets in
  server-only modules; keep other values in computeds or functions, which are not sent.
- **Calling a state's accessor at module scope on the server.** There is no request there, so it
  throws. Call it in components, middleware, endpoints or actions.
- **Creating a state inside a function.** Only module-scope states get an id, so a state created
  in a component or helper is never sent and the browser starts from the factory's values.
- **Reading `localStorage` in setup in a server-rendered component.** The server cannot read it,
  so the first browser render differs from the HTML (`LUM4006`). Load it in `onMount`, as the
  persisted recipe does.
- **Copying state between stores with `effect`.** `effect(() => b.set(a()))` adds a frame of
  staleness. Derive with `computed`, or keep one source of truth.
- **Expecting `snapshot()` in an effect to track.** Its reads are not tracked. To log every change,
  read through the store (`JSON.stringify(state)`).
- **Assigning a fresh fetch result over a store's array.** `state.rows = await res.json()` replaces
  every row, so lists re-create their rows and lose row state. Use `reconcile(state.rows, data)`.
- **Wrapping a class instance, `Map` or `Set` in `store()`.** Only plain objects and arrays become
  reactive. Use a record keyed by id, or the family recipe.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.
- [LUM4011](../errors/LUM4011.md): non-serializable scoped state value.
- [LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md): island reads context provided by the page.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.

See also: [Signals and reactivity](signals.md), [Islands](islands.md), [Async components](async.md).

<!-- source: concepts/jsx.md -->

# JSX

> JSX reads like React (`.map()`, ternaries, `onClick`) but compiles to cloned templates with fine-grained bindings. Only expressions that read signals update.

## Concept

**Bindings.** The compiler looks at each JSX expression:

- Literals and plain identifiers are **static**: written once.
- Calls and member access (`count()`, `user.name`, `props.title`) become **bindings** that re-run
  when a signal they read changes, and write only the part of the DOM they own.
- `untrack(() => …)` opts an expression out.

**Compiled idioms.** There are no `<For>` or `<Show>` components; ordinary JavaScript compiles to
the efficient form:

| Source                                              | Compiled to                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{items().map((item, i) => <Row key={item.id} />)}` | A keyed list. `key` is optional (items are keyed by reference otherwise). `i` becomes a reactive index only if you use it.                                                                                                            |
| `item.id === selected()` inside `.map`              | An O(1) selector: a selection change touches two rows.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `{c() ? <A /> : <B />}`, `{c() && <A />}`           | A memoised branch: switches only when the condition flips.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `{count() * 2}`, ``{`#${id}`}``, `{String(x)}`      | Provably text: a text node of the template, updated with `setText` (written once when nothing reactive is read). Applies to sole children and to children between elements; a `const` initialised with such an expression counts too. |
| `{row.label()}`, `{id}`, `{props.title}`            | Maybe text, alone between nodes (or the only child): also a text node of the template, written by `insertText`. Text values update the node in place; nodes, arrays and other values render in a region before it.                    |
| `{fn()}` next to text or another `{…}`              | A dynamic insert (a region), since adjacent text nodes would merge when the HTML is parsed.                                                                                                                                           |

**Elements.**

| Prop                         | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `class`                      | A string, an array, or a `{ name: boolean }` record (nested arrays allowed). `className` is a type error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `style`                      | A string, or an object with **kebab-case** keys, including `--custom` properties. Each key updates on its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `aria-*`, `spellcheck`, …    | Booleans are written as `"true"`/`"false"` (`aria-pressed={false}` renders `aria-pressed="false"`): `aria-*`, `contenteditable`, `draggable`, `spellcheck` and the other enumerated attributes, static or not. Other attributes: `true` adds the attribute empty (`hidden`); `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out. |
| `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, …    | camelCase handlers. Bubbling events are delegated (one listener per type at `document`); non-bubbling ones (`onFocus`, `onMouseEnter`, `onScroll`) get a direct listener.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `on:click`, `on:my-event`    | A native `addEventListener` listener with the exact event name. Use it for custom and web-component events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `bind:value`, `bind:checked` | Two-way binding to a writable signal, on `input`, `select` and `textarea`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `attach={[fn]}`              | Runs `fn(el)` with the element in a tracked scope; it may return a cleanup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ref={fn}`                   | Called with the element. `ref<T>()` makes a callback you can read like a signal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `innerHTML`                  | Sets unescaped HTML. The lint rule `no-unsafe-html` warns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `key`                        | Allowed on intrinsic elements and components (list identity).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `client:*`                   | Island directives, on components only. See [Islands](islands.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Handlers receive the **native** event, with `currentTarget` typed as the element. There are no
synthetic events.

## API

JSX types come from `lumiose/jsx-runtime` (via `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"`) and the global `JSX`
namespace from `lumiose/env`:

| Type                     | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `JSX.Element`            | Anything JSX can render: nodes, strings, numbers, arrays, functions, `null`. |
| `JSX.ClassValue`         | The `class` prop value.                                                      |
| `JSX.CSSProperties`      | The `style` object (kebab-case keys and `--custom` properties).              |
| `JSX.EventHandler<E, T>` | A handler: the native event `E` with `currentTarget: T`.                     |
| `JSX.Ref<T>`             | The value of `ref<T>()`.                                                     |
| `JSX.HTMLProps<T>`       | Props of an HTML element, for wrappers and custom elements.                  |

See [JSX types and tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md) for custom elements and the full rules.

## Example

```tsx check
import { signal } from "lumiose";

interface Todo {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

export function TodoList() {
  const todos = signal<Todo[]>([
    { id: 1, title: "Write docs" },
    { id: 2, title: "Ship" },
  ]);
  const selected = signal(1);
  const draft = signal("");
  const progress = signal(40);

  const add = (event: SubmitEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    todos.update((list) => [...list, { id: Date.now(), title: draft() }]);
    draft.set("");
  };

  return (
    <section style={{ "--progress": `${progress()}%`, "max-inline-size": "40rem" }}>
      <form onSubmit={add}>
        <input bind:value={draft} on:focus={(event) => event.currentTarget.select()} />
        <button disabled={draft() === ""}>Add</button>
      </form>
      {todos().length === 0 ? (
        <p>Nothing to do.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul>
          {todos().map((todo) => (
            <li
              key={todo.id}
              class={["todo", { active: todo.id === selected() }]}
              onClick={() => selected.set(todo.id)}
            >
              {todo.title}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **React prop names.** `className` → `class`, `htmlFor` → `for`, `onclick`/`onKeydown` →
  `onClick`/`onKeyDown` (camelCase after `on`). The wrong forms are type errors.
- **camelCase style keys.** `style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}` is a type error; write
  `{ "font-weight": 600 }`, as in CSS. Numbers get no units: write `"12px"`.
- **Passing a value to `bind:value`.** It needs the signal itself: `bind:value={draft}`, not
  `bind:value={draft()}`.
- **Custom events with `onX`.** `onMyEvent` is not an event prop; write `on:my-event`.
- **Using the index outside the row.** The `i` of `.map((item, i) => …)` is a reactive index that
  belongs to its row; storing it in an outer variable or closure that outlives the row is
  `LUM2006`.
- **Wrapping lists in helper components.** `{items().map(…)}` already compiles to a keyed list;
  there is no `<For>`.
- **`innerHTML` with user input.** It is not escaped. Prefer text children.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md): component called as a function.
- [LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md): children inserted twice.
- [LUM2006](../errors/LUM2006.md): reactive index escapes its callback.
- [LUM1001](../errors/LUM1001.md): syntax error.

See also: [Components](components.md), [Styles](styles.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/styles.md -->

# Styles

> Write plain CSS in `<style>` blocks in `.stsx` files. By convention, one block at the end of the file styles every component in it. Where a block sits decides its scope: the file, the element that encloses it, or the whole app with `<style global>`. CSS reads JS constants as `$name`, inlined at build time, and constant math is precomputed.

## Concept

**One block per file, at the end.** The default is a single top-level `<style>` after the
components. It styles every template in the file, so several components share it, and it reads
any top-level `const` declared above it. The JSX stays free of CSS, and the file reads like a
component file with its stylesheet:

```stsx check
import { signal } from "lumiose";

const accent = "#5546ff";
const radius = "10px";

export function Counter() {
  const count = signal(0);

  return (
    <div class="counter">
      <button onClick={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>{count()}</button>
      <Reset onReset={() => count.set(0)} />
    </div>
  );
}

export function Reset(props: { onReset: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button class="reset" onClick={props.onReset}>
      Reset
    </button>
  );
}

<style>
  .counter { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; }
  button {
    padding: 0.5rem 1rem;
    border: 0;
    border-radius: $radius;
    background: $accent;
    color: white;
  }
  .reset { background: transparent; color: $accent; }
</style>
```

`Counter` and `Reset` share the block: `button` matches the buttons of both, and of no other file.

**Placement decides scope.**

| Placement                                                                            | Scope                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| File top level (by convention, one block at the end of the file)                     | Every template in the file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Inside a component's JSX, as a child of an intrinsic element or fragment (any depth) | Its **enclosing element and everything written inside it** in that component, including `.map` callbacks and JSX passed as children there. A block directly under the component's root element therefore covers the whole component. Sibling subtrees are not affected, and it never reaches other components' own templates. |
| `<style global>` (anywhere a block is valid)                                         | The whole app, unscoped. Usually at the end of the root `_layout.stsx`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Nested blocks, for two jobs.** A block inside a component's JSX is still valid. Reach for one
when the file-level block cannot do the job:

- **Scoping one element's subtree,** so a selector such as `p` or `.note` cannot match anything
  else in the file.
- **Reading a constant declared inside a component** (`const gap = 12` in its body). A file-level
  block only sees top-level constants.

```stsx
export function Panel() {
  const gap = 12;

  return (
    <div class="panel">
      <aside class="side">…</aside>                 {/* not styled by the <style> below */}
      <section class="body">
        <p class="note">…</p>
        <style> p { color: tomato; } </style>      {/* only the <p> of this <section> */}
      </section>
      <style> .panel { gap: calc($gap * 1px); } </style>   {/* reads the component's `gap` */}
    </div>
  );
}

<style>
  .panel { display: grid; }
</style>
```

Everything else goes in the file-level block. Moving a block from a component's root to the end
of the file widens its scope to every component in the file: check that its selectors (bare
element selectors in particular) do not start matching another component's elements.

**How scoping works.** Each scope with styles gets a token `data-l-<hash>`, a stable hash of the
file path plus the component name, with one token per style-bearing element. Every element in the
scope carries the token: the whole file for top-level blocks, and the enclosing element's lexical
subtree for blocks inside a component. The last compound of each selector gets `[data-l-<hash>]`,
a +0,1,0 specificity bump. Dynamic classes always work, because no element is pruned.

- `:global(.sel)` leaves a selector unscoped; `:deep(.sel)` scopes only the part before it.
- `@keyframes` names are scoped, and `animation` references are rewritten. A block sees its own
  keyframes, then those of the blocks of enclosing elements (innermost first), then the file's, so
  a nested block can animate with keyframes defined under the component's root. Custom properties
  are not scoped.
- **Class passthrough.** When a parent passes `class` to a child component, the parent's scope
  tokens at that call site travel with it: the file token plus every enclosing style subtree. So
  `.cta { … }` in the parent styles `<Button class="cta" />` wherever `Button` applies
