  `props.class`. The child applies it on every element whose `class` value may contain it:
  `class={["btn", props.class]}`, a destructured `class` prop or `...rest`, a helper that gets
  `props` (`class={variantClass(props)}`), or a local value or function built from them
  (`const classes = () => ["btn", props.class]`). A class that reaches the element any other way
  (a module-level variable, a context) loses the parent's scope, so read `props.class` in the
  component. Forwarding works through intermediate components: when `Field` passes its own
  `class` prop on (`<Input class={["field", props.class]} />`), `Input`'s element gets `Field`'s
  tokens and those of `Field`'s caller.
- Within a file, file-level CSS comes first, then component blocks in source order.
- **In the editor**, class completion follows the same scopes: in a `class` attribute it offers
  the classes of the blocks that apply there (innermost first), then the project's global classes
  (`<style global>` blocks and imported global `.css` files), never a sibling subtree's.
  `var(--…)` offers every custom property declared in the project, with its value.

**Blocks are plain CSS:** no Sass, no `lang`, `media` or other attributes (only `global`). CSS
imports, CSS Modules, Tailwind v4 and `.scss` imports still work through Vite.

> **Status:** available. `@lumiose/vite` serves each file's CSS as a CSS module, and style-only or
> constant-only edits hot-update the CSS without remounting. `LUM3012` (a custom property set in a
> `style` prop that no stylesheet reads) is reported by `lumiose build` only.

**In builds**, a page needs few render-blocking stylesheets. `lumiose build` merges the stylesheets
every page starts with (the document's, the root layouts', shared components') into one file that
all pages link and browsers cache, then puts each page's own stylesheets after it: inline in one
`<style>` when they total 4 kB or less, else merged into one file for that page. The cascade
order is the same as in dev, where each file's CSS stays a separate stylesheet for HMR. In the
sample apps a first view went from 6–8 stylesheet requests to one, with about 30% fewer CSS bytes (brotli).
Each tag lists the stylesheets it holds in `data-l-css`, so an island or an SPA route that imports
one does not load it again.

### JS values in styles

`$name` and `$obj.key` put a JS value into CSS. The compiler evaluates the reference at build time
and inlines the result, so the output is plain CSS: no runtime lookup and no JS inside CSS.
TypeScript checks each reference like any other expression. Imports used only by `$` references
are removed from the JS output, and editing them hot-reloads the CSS only.

**What a reference can name:** a `const` whose value the compiler can work out without running the
app.

| Declared as                                                                                  | Readable from                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A top-level `const` of the file                                                              | Every block of the file. A top-level block must come after it.                                                   |
| A `const` of the enclosing component                                                         | Blocks inside that component, `<style global>` included.                                                         |
| An `export const` (or `export default`) of an imported `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.stsx` or JSON module | Every block of the importing file: named, default or namespace imports (`$theme.space.md`), re-exports included. |

Imports are resolved the way the rest of the toolchain resolves them: by Vite in `lumiose dev` and
builds (aliases included), and like TypeScript in `lumiose check` and the editor (relative paths,
tsconfig `paths`, package `exports` and `imports`). An import that cannot be resolved, or that has
no such export, is reported as [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) at each reference.

The value may be built from literals, template literals, arithmetic (`+ - * / % **`, unary `-`),
other constants, and object literals with their members at any depth (`$theme.color.brand`),
including spreads, destructuring, `as const` and `satisfies`. Mark token objects `as const`: a plain
object literal folds too, as written, but only `as const` keeps the JS read-only like the CSS.

**How values are written.** Strings are inserted verbatim, without quotes (`"12px"` becomes
`12px`; for a CSS string, put the quotes inside: `'"→"'`). Numbers are inserted as plain numbers
(`const gap = 8` gives `8`), so give them a unit with `calc($gap * 1px)` (which ships as `8px`, see below) or keep the unit in the
constant (`"8px"`, `` `${gap}px` ``). A bare number where a length, angle or time is required
(`gap: $gap`, `rotate: $angle`) is [LUM3018](../errors/LUM3018.md), with `calc($gap * 1px)` as the
fix: Lightning CSS happens to read a bare length as pixels, but angles and times are dropped, and in
custom properties or math functions the number stays unitless. A unit written after the reference
(`$gap px`) does not attach to it ([LUM3019](../errors/LUM3019.md)).

**What cannot be referenced.** The compiler reports it; the CSS keeps the `$` text, which browsers
ignore.

| Reference                                                                                                   | Diagnostic                      | Fix                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `$space(2)`: a function call, or a `const` holding a function or a call's result (`Date.now()`, `signal()`) | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Compute it as a constant: `calc($space * 2px)` with `const space = 4`, or name the steps: `$space.md`. |
| `$count` where `count` is a `let` (or `var`)                                                                | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Make it a `const`, or pass it at runtime (below).                                                      |
| `$open`, `$props.width`: signals, props, parameters                                                         | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Pass it at runtime (below).                                                                            |
| `$sizes.0`: an array item (`sizes.0` is not JS)                                                             | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | An `as const` object with named keys: `$sizes.sm`.                                                     |
| `$brand-primary`: a hyphen, read as `$brand` minus `primary`                                                | [LUM3009](../errors/LUM3009.md) | `$brand.primary`, or a camelCase constant: `$brandPrimary`.                                            |
| A component's `const` in a block outside it (file level, or another component)                              | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Move the `const` to the top level, or the block into the component.                                    |
| A top-level block above the `const` it reads                                                                | [LUM3013](../errors/LUM3013.md) | Move the block below it; by convention, to the end of the file.                                        |

`LUM3008`'s message says which case it is (a `let` binding, computed by a call at runtime, an array,
not declared in scope, an import that does not export the name, …).

**Where `$` is read:** in property values (`gap: calc($gap * 1px)`) and in `@media`, `@container`
and `@supports` preludes (`@media (width < $narrow)`). Everywhere else `$` is left to CSS:

- In selectors, `$` keeps its CSS meaning: `[href$=".pdf"]` is "ends with". `.size-$md` is not a
  reference but an invalid selector, which Lightning CSS drops (`LUM3015`).
- Property names, strings (`content: "$gap"`), comments and `url($file)` are not substituted. Put
  the whole value in the constant instead: `const hero = 'url("/hero.png")'` and
  `background-image: $hero`.

**Runtime values.** A `$` reference is fixed at build time. For a value that changes (a signal, a
prop, a measurement), set a custom property with the `style` prop and read it with `var()`. Custom
properties are not scoped and inherit, so descendants can read them too.

```stsx
<div class="bar" style={{ "--fill": `${pct()}%` }}>
  <style>
    .bar { inline-size: var(--fill); }
  </style>
</div>
```

Tokens usually live in their own module:

```ts check file=theme.ts
// src/theme.ts
export const space = { sm: 4, md: 8, lg: 16 } as const;
export const radius = "6px";
export const narrow = "40rem";
```

```stsx check file=components/Meter.stsx
// src/components/Meter.stsx
import * as theme from "../theme.ts";

const track = theme.space.sm * 2;
const shadow = `0 1px ${track / 4}px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)`;

export function Meter(props: { label: string; value: number }) {
  const border = 1;

  return (
    <div class="meter" style={{ "--value": `${props.value}%` }}>
      <span>{props.label}</span>
      <div class="track">
        <div class="fill" />
      </div>

      <style>
        .meter {
          --pad: calc($theme.space.md * 2px);
          display: grid;
          gap: calc($theme.space.sm * 1px);
          padding: var(--pad);
          border: calc($border * 1px) solid;
          border-radius: $theme.radius;
        }
        .track { block-size: calc($track * 1px); border-radius: calc($track * 1px / 2); box-shadow: $shadow; }
        .fill { inline-size: var(--value); block-size: 100%; background: currentColor; }
        @media (width < $theme.narrow) {
          .meter { max-inline-size: calc(100% - $theme.space.lg * 2px); }
        }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The compiler's CSS output for that file (`data-l-lw1tegds` is the component's scope token). Every
`$` reference and every constant `calc()` is gone; only the runtime `var(--value)` and the
`%`-relative width are left to the browser:

```css
.meter[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  --pad: 16px;
  padding: var(--pad);
  border: 1px solid;
  border-radius: 6px;
  gap: 4px;
  display: grid;
}

.track[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  border-radius: 4px;
  block-size: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 2px #0003;
}

.fill[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  inline-size: var(--value);
  background: currentColor;
  block-size: 100%;
}

@media (width < 40rem) {
  .meter[data-l-lw1tegds] {
    max-inline-size: calc(100% - 32px);
  }
}
```

Lightning CSS also minifies values (`rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)` becomes `#0003`) and may reorder or merge
declarations, so the output is equivalent to the source, not identical.

#### Build-time math

Constant math never reaches the browser. It is computed in two steps:

1. **JS math, by the Lumiose compiler.** Arithmetic in constants and template literals is evaluated
   before the value is inserted: `const track = theme.space.sm * 2` inlines `8`.
2. **CSS math, by Lightning CSS.** After substitution, Lightning CSS reduces `calc()`, `min()`,
   `max()`, `clamp()`, `round()`, `abs()`, the trigonometric functions and the other CSS math
   functions whenever the operands are concrete values in compatible units. `calc($gap * 2px)`
   becomes `calc(8 * 2px)`, which ships as `16px`.

| Source (`$gap` is `8`)                    | Output                                | Why                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `padding: calc($gap * 2px)`               | `padding: 16px`                       | `calc(8 * 2px)` reduces.                       |
| `inline-size: min(10px, 20px)`            | `inline-size: 10px`                   |                                                |
| `block-size: clamp(4px, 8px, 12px)`       | `block-size: 8px`                     |                                                |
| `transform: rotate(calc(45deg * 2))`      | `transform: rotate(90deg)`            | Math inside other functions reduces too.       |
| `inset: calc(2px + 3px) calc(1rem + 4px)` | `inset: 5px calc(1rem + 4px)`         | Each value on its own: `rem` plus `px` stays.  |
| `width: calc(100% - $gap * 2px)`          | `width: calc(100% - 16px)`            | The constant part reduces; `%` stays.          |
| `font-size: calc(2 * 1rem)`               | `font-size: 2rem`                     | One unit: nothing to convert.                  |
| `font-size: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 3rem)`       | unchanged                             | `rem` and `vw` are only known in the browser.  |
| `max-width: calc(var(--w) + $gap * 2px)`  | `max-width: calc(var(--w) + 8 * 2px)` | A declaration with `var()` is kept as written. |
| `--space: calc($gap * 2px)`               | `--space: 16px`                       | A custom property, folded by Lumiose (below).  |
| `padding-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)`   | `padding-left: 0`                     | Negative in a non-negative property (below).   |
| `margin-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)`    | `margin-left: -4px`                   | Margins can be negative.                       |

**What cannot fold.** A math function is replaced only by a value that means the same thing
wherever it is used. Absolute units convert into each other (`calc(1in + 4px)` is `100px`) and a
unit combines with itself (`calc(2 * 1rem)` is `2rem`), but context-dependent units mixed with
others need the browser: `%` resolves against the containing block (or the font size, depending on
the property), `vw` and `vh` against the viewport, `em` against the element's font size and `rem`
against the root's. A `var()` is only known when the browser computes styles, so Lightning CSS keeps
any declaration containing one exactly as written, constant parts included. To precompute those,
do the arithmetic in JS: with `` const extra = `${gap * 2}px` ``, `calc(var(--w) + $extra)` ships as
`calc(var(--w) + 16px)`.

**Custom properties.** Lightning CSS keeps custom property values as written, because it cannot
know where they will be used. Lumiose folds each math function in them that reduces to a single value
in compatible units: `--space: calc($gap * 2px)` becomes `16px`, `--turn: rotate(calc(45deg * 2))`
becomes `rotate(90deg)`, and `var(--x, calc($gap * 3px))` becomes `var(--x, 24px)`. Anything with
`var()`, `env()` or context-dependent units mixed with other units stays whole, without the partial
reduction regular properties get (`--inset: calc(100% - $gap * 2px)` stays `calc(100% - 8 * 2px)`).
Negative results and fractional numbers stay inside `calc()` (`calc(-3px)`, `calc(.333333)`),
because a bare value can behave differently where the property is read: `calc()` clamps to the
property's range and rounds where an integer is expected.

**Negative results.** Some properties cannot be negative: padding, sizes (`width`, `min-height`,
…), border widths, `gap`, `font-size`, `line-height` and others. In the browser, a `calc()` that
comes out negative there is clamped to 0, while a negative value written out is invalid and the
whole declaration is dropped. So that folding does not change the meaning, a negative result in such
a property ships as `0`: `padding-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)` gives `padding-left: 0`, and
`font-size: calc(1rem - 2rem)` gives `font-size: 0`. This mirrors the upstream Lightning CSS fix
([lightningcss#1329](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/lightningcss/pull/1329)), which Lumiose
applies until a release includes it. Properties that accept negative values, such as margins and
`inset`, keep them.

Folding regular properties, minification and browser targets come from
[Lightning CSS](https://lightningcss.dev), the CSS parser, transformer and minifier from the Parcel
project, which Lumiose's CSS compiler is built on. Lumiose adds `$` constants, scoping and the
custom-property folding.

## API

| Syntax                                   | Meaning                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<style>…</style>` at module top level   | File-scoped CSS, shared by every component of the file. By convention one block, at the end of the file. |
| `<style>…</style>` in component JSX      | CSS scoped to its enclosing element's subtree (the whole component when placed under the root element).  |
| `<style global>…</style>`                | Unscoped, app-wide CSS.                                                                                  |
| `$name`, `$obj.key`                      | A JS constant, inlined at build time, in property values and `@media`/`@container`/`@supports` preludes. |
| `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()`, … | Folded at build time when every operand is a concrete value in compatible units.                         |
| `:global(sel)`, `:deep(sel)`             | Escape or extend the scope.                                                                              |
| `style={{ "--x": value }}` + `var(--x)`  | Runtime values.                                                                                          |

## Example

```stsx check
// tokens are usually in their own module: `export const radius = { sm: "4px", lg: "12px" } as const;`
const radius = { sm: "4px", lg: "12px" } as const;
const BREAKPOINT = "40rem";

export function Card(props: { title: string; progress: number; class?: string }) {
  return (
    <article class={["card", props.class]} style={{ "--progress": `${props.progress}%` }}>
      <h2>{props.title}</h2>
      <div class="bar" />
    </article>
  );
}

export function Dashboard(props: { columns: number }) {
  const gap = 12;

  return (
    <main class="dashboard" style={{ "--columns": props.columns }}>
      <Card class="featured" title="Uploads" progress={40} />
      <Card title="Downloads" progress={75} />

      <style>
        .dashboard { gap: calc($gap * 1px); }
      </style>
    </main>
  );
}

<style>
  .dashboard { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--columns), 1fr); }
  .card { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; border-radius: $radius.lg; }
  .card h2 { margin: 0; }
  .bar { inline-size: var(--progress); block-size: 4px; background: currentColor; }
  .featured { outline: 2px solid gold; }
  @media (width < $BREAKPOINT) { .card { border-radius: $radius.sm; } }
</style>
```

`Card` and `Dashboard` share the file-level block, which reads the top-level constants. `.featured`
is set by `Dashboard` and styles the `<article>` inside `Card`: both are in the file's scope (from
another file, the class would get there through class passthrough). The nested block in
`Dashboard` is there because it reads `gap`, a constant of the component.

## Common mistakes

- **A block inside `{…}`, a conditional, a `.map` callback, or a component element** such as
  `<Suspense>` or `<Card>`. Move it into an intrinsic element of the component (`LUM3010`).
- **Returning a block, or using it as an expression** (`return <style>…`, `=> <style>`). Put it
  inside the returned element (`LUM3011`).
- **Hyphenated references.** `$brand-primary` reads `$brand` minus `primary`. Use an object
  member: `$brand.primary` (`LUM3009`).
- **Non-constant references.** `$count` where `count` is a signal, a prop or a `let`, or a call
  such as `$space(2)`, is `LUM3008`. Pass runtime values with `style={{ "--count": count() }}` and
  `var(--count)`; replace calls with constant math (`calc($space * 2px)`).
- **Array items.** `$sizes.0` is not JS (`LUM3008`). Use an `as const` object: `$sizes.sm`.
- **A unit after a reference.** `margin: $gap px` ships as `8 px`, which browsers ignore
  (`LUM3019`). Write `calc($gap * 1px)` or keep the unit in the constant.
- **A unitless number in a length, angle or time.** `gap: $gap` with `const gap = 8` relies on
  Lightning CSS reading `8` as pixels, and `rotate: $angle` is dropped (`LUM3018`). Multiply by the
  unit (`calc($angle * 1deg)`) or keep the unit in the constant.
- **`$` in selectors, strings or `url()`.** It is not substituted there (`[href$=".pdf"]` is CSS's
  "ends with"). Put the whole value in a constant, `url()` included.
- **A top-level block before the `const`s it reads.** Move the block to the end of the file
  (`LUM3013`).
- **`<style>` in a `.tsx` file.** It is a type error in `.tsx` (and `LUM1006` for raw CSS); rename the file to `.stsx`.
- **Attributes on `<style>`.** Only `global` is allowed (`LUM1005`).
- **Expecting a parent's styles to reach into children from another file.** A file's blocks
  never style the templates of components defined in other files; pass `class` (passthrough) or
  use `:deep()`.
- **Expecting a nested block to style sibling subtrees.** A `<style>` inside an element only
  styles that element's subtree. Move its rules to the file-level block at the end of the file,
  or the block up to the common ancestor.
- **Styling JSX returned by a helper function.** In `const field = () => <label class="field">…`
  inside a component, the helper's JSX is not inside the element that holds a nested `<style>`, so
  `.field` matches nothing there (`LUM3005`). Move the block to the top level of the file (it
  styles every element of the file), or render that JSX inside the styled element.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1004](../errors/LUM1004.md), [LUM1005](../errors/LUM1005.md), [LUM1006](../errors/LUM1006.md): unclosed block, unknown attribute, raw CSS in `.tsx`.
- [LUM3005](../errors/LUM3005.md): unused scoped selector.
- [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md), [LUM3009](../errors/LUM3009.md), [LUM3013](../errors/LUM3013.md): `$` reference problems.
- [LUM3010](../errors/LUM3010.md), [LUM3011](../errors/LUM3011.md): misplaced blocks.
- [LUM3012](../errors/LUM3012.md): custom property set but never read.
- [LUM3014](../errors/LUM3014.md), [LUM3015](../errors/LUM3015.md): CSS syntax error, invalid CSS dropped (such as `$` in a selector).
- [LUM3017](../errors/LUM3017.md): a declaration value browsers would ignore, or no value.
- [LUM3020](../errors/LUM3020.md): an unknown property name, with a fix for close typos.
- [LUM3018](../errors/LUM3018.md), [LUM3019](../errors/LUM3019.md): a unitless `$` number, a unit separated from a reference.

See also: [Components](components.md), [JSX `style` and `class`](jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/async.md -->

# Async components

> Any component may be `async` and `await` data in its body, on the server and the client. `<Suspense>` shows a fallback while new content loads; `<ErrorBoundary>` catches failures.

## Concept

Async components are **the** way to read data in Lumiose (there are no route loaders). The same
component works in every rendering mode.

**The await rewrite.** The compiler rewrites `await` only where the nearest enclosing function is
the component itself; awaits inside handlers and callbacks are ordinary awaits. Around each
component-level `await`, the runtime restores the owner, context and tracking, so `useContext()`,
`getAbortSignal()` and signal reads keep working after it.

**Re-runs.** Props and signals read in the body (before or after an `await`) are tracked. When one
changes, the component **re-runs**:

- the previous run's `getAbortSignal()` signal aborts (cancel your fetches with it);
- the old UI stays on screen until the new run resolves, then swaps atomically;
- signals created in the body start fresh on each run;
- `isPending()` is true while the re-run is in flight.

**Boundaries.**

- `<Suspense fallback={…}>` shows its fallback for **new** pending content: the first load, and
  branches mounted later. Re-runs of content already shown keep the stale UI instead (use
  `isPending()` to dim it).
- `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>` catches rejections and render errors below it.
- With no boundary: on the server the component becomes part of the page shell (the response waits
  for it); on the client nothing renders until it resolves; errors go to the `_error` page.

**In-flight state** (all are reactive and safe to read anywhere):

| Helper                | True while                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `isPending()`         | this async component's own re-run is in flight (inside the component or its UI).                       |
| `isSubmitting(name?)` | a form action submission is in flight. See [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).                    |
| `isNavigating()`      | an SPA navigation is in flight. See [Routing](routing.md).                                             |
| `isBusy()`            | anything above is in flight, or any `<Suspense>` shows its fallback. Use it for a global progress bar. |

**Caching.** Component-level awaits of `fetchJSON` and `query` go through a keyed cache:

- A GET `await fetchJSON(url)` is keyed by its absolute URL, so it needs no key.
- `await query(key, fn)` caches anything else (a database call, an SDK) under a TanStack-style
  array key such as `["stats", "books"]`: JSON-serializable values, hashed stably. `fn` receives
  `{ signal, queryKey }` (TanStack's query function context); pass `signal` on to cancel the work
  once no component waits for it.
- Components awaiting the same entry share one request: per request on the server, per page in the
  browser (every island and the SPA tree, kept across client navigations).
- In the browser, a cached entry shows at once (no `<Suspense>` fallback for a new component) and
  refetches in the background (stale-while-revalidate, TanStack defaults: `staleTime` 0, `gcTime`
  5 minutes). If the data changed, the components that awaited it re-run.
- `invalidate("/api/books/1")` refetches that URL's entry and `invalidate(["stats"])` the entries
  whose key starts with `["stats"]`. Only the components that awaited them re-run, keeping their
  UI until the new data arrives. `invalidate()` with no target refreshes the whole page.
- Only awaits in async component bodies are cached. `fetchJSON` in event handlers, middleware,
  endpoints and actions is a plain request, and so are non-GET requests and
  `fetchJSON(url, { cache: "no-store" })`, the opt-out for data that must always be fresh: never
  deduped, kept or sent with the page payload.
- Errors are never cached: the next await tries again. Aborting one component's wait (a superseded
  run) never cancels a request another component still awaits.

**Islands.** Inside an [island](islands.md), each awaited value is recorded during SSR and
replayed during hydration, so the client does not fetch it again. Cached values (`fetchJSON`,
`query`) are sent once per page instead, however many islands await them, and fill the browser
cache. Those values must be plain data (`LUM4007`), and **everything awaited inside an island is
sent to the browser**.

> **Status:** async components, the `await` rewrite, re-runs, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`,
> `isPending()`, `isBusy()`, server streaming and the keyed cache (`fetchJSON`, `query`,
> `invalidate(...targets)`) are available, and so is replaying awaited values when an island
> hydrates (see [Islands](islands.md)).

## API

| API                                                              | Shape                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `async function Name(props) { const x = await …; return <… /> }` | An async component.                                                                                        |
| `<Suspense fallback={…}>`                                        | Fallback for new pending content below.                                                                    |
| `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => …}>`                 | Fallback after an error below; `reset()` renders the children again. `fallback` may also be plain content. |
| `isPending()`                                                    | Whether this component's re-run is in flight.                                                              |
| `isBusy()`                                                       | Whether anything in the app is in flight.                                                                  |
| `getAbortSignal()`                                               | `AbortSignal` of the current run; aborted when superseded or disposed.                                     |
| `fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`                                       | Isomorphic JSON fetch that returns plain data; cached by URL when awaited in a component.                  |
| `query(key, fn)`                                                 | Awaited in a component, caches what `fn` resolves to under `key` (an array).                               |
| `invalidate(...targets)`                                         | Refetches the entries of URLs and key prefixes, re-running their components; no target: the whole page.    |

## Example

```tsx check
import { ErrorBoundary, Suspense, fetchJSON, getAbortSignal, isPending, signal } from "lumiose";

interface Book {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  summary: string;
}

export async function BookDetails({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const book = await fetchJSON<Book>(`/api/books/${id}`, { signal: getAbortSignal() });
  const expanded = signal(false);

  return (
    <article class={{ stale: isPending() }}>
      <h2>{book.title}</h2>
      <button onClick={() => expanded.update((open) => !open)}>Details</button>
      {expanded() && <p>{book.summary}</p>}
    </article>
  );
}

export function BookPage({ ids }: { ids: string[] }) {
  const current = signal(ids[0] ?? "");

  return (
    <main>
      <nav>
        {ids.map((id) => (
          <button onClick={() => current.set(id)}>{id}</button>
        ))}
      </nav>
      <ErrorBoundary
        fallback={(error, reset) => (
          <p>
            Could not load the book ({String(error)}). <button onClick={reset}>Retry</button>
          </p>
        )}
      >
        <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
          <BookDetails id={current()} />
        </Suspense>
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </main>
  );
}
```

Clicking another id re-runs `BookDetails`: the old book stays (dimmed through `isPending()`) until
the new one arrives; `<Suspense>` only showed its fallback for the first load. Going back to a book
already seen shows it at once from the cache, then revalidates it.

Data that does not come from `fetchJSON` goes through `query`, and a mutation refreshes only what it
changed:

```tsx check
import { invalidate, query } from "lumiose";

declare const db: { stats(): Promise<{ total: number }>; addBook(title: string): Promise<void> };

export async function Stats() {
  const stats = await query(["stats", "books"], () => db.stats());
  return <p>{stats.total} books</p>;
}

export function AddBook() {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        await db.addBook("Dune");
        await invalidate(["stats"], "/api/books"); // re-runs Stats and the components of /api/books
      }}
    >
      Add
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading the component's own signals in its body.** A signal created in the body and read in
  the body re-runs the component, which re-creates the signal. Read it in JSX or handlers instead
  (`LUM2007`).
- **Not passing `getAbortSignal()` to fetches.** Without it, a superseded run's request keeps going. Pass
  `{ signal: getAbortSignal() }`.
- **Passing a key as a string to `invalidate()`.** A string is a URL: `invalidate("stats")` matches
  no `query()` entry (development builds warn). Pass the key array: `invalidate(["stats"])`.
- **Mutating cached data.** Every component that awaited an entry gets the same object. Copy it
  before changing it, or keep editable state in a signal or `store`.
- **Expecting `fetchJSON` in an event handler to use the cache.** Only component-level awaits are
  cached; a handler's call is a plain request (call `invalidate(url)` after a mutation instead).
- **Awaiting a `Response` inside an island.** `await fetch(url)` gives a non-serializable value.
  Use `await fetchJSON(url)` (`LUM4007`).
- **Putting secrets in awaited values inside islands.** They are serialized into the HTML. Fetch
  only what the browser may see.
- **Wrapping a re-run in `<Suspense>` and expecting the fallback again.** Revealed content keeps
  its stale UI; show progress with `isPending()` or `isBusy()`.
- **`await using` in a component body.** Not supported in v1 (`LUM1007`).
- **Expecting `resource()` on the server.** It never runs there; use an async component.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1007](../errors/LUM1007.md): `await using` in a component.
- [LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md): own signal read in an async body.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch (including replay key mismatches).
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.

See also: [Islands](islands.md), [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/islands.md -->

# Islands

> Pages render on the server and ship no JS by default. Add a `client:*` directive where a component is used, and only that component (an island) hydrates in the browser.

## Concept

An **island** is a component instance that runs in the browser. You declare it at the **usage
site**, so the same component can be static on one page and interactive on another:

```tsx
<TeamPanel client:visible ids={ids} />
```

On the server, the call compiles to an island record: the component's module and export name, its
props, its slots and the hydration strategy. The page HTML contains the server-rendered island
between comment markers (`<!--l:ID-->…<!--/l:ID-->`) plus a JSON record; a small loader (about 1
kB) reads the records, arms the triggers and imports the island's module when one fires. Clicks,
input, submits and key presses that happen before hydration are replayed.

**Directives** (components only):

| Directive                                   | Hydrates                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `client:load`                               | Immediately.                                        |
| `client:idle`                               | When the browser is idle (at the latest after 2 s). |
| `client:visible` / `client:visible="200px"` | When it enters the viewport (optional root margin). |
| `client:media="(max-width: 600px)"`         | When the media query matches.                       |
| `client:only`                               | Client-rendered only: no server HTML.               |

**Props must be serializable**: JSON values plus `undefined`, `NaN`/`Infinity`, `BigInt`, `Date`,
`URL`, `Map` and `Set`. Functions, symbols, class instances (a `Response` too), promises and cycles
are `LUM4002`.

**Children and JSX props are slots.** They are rendered on the server and stay server components:
they never ship their own JS. A slot the island rendered on the server is adopted in place when it
hydrates; one it did not render yet (behind a condition) is sent as `<template data-l-slot="name">`
and inserted when the island renders it.

**What hydration does.** The island's component runs again in the browser, with the props the
server serialized, and its compiled code claims the server's nodes instead of creating new ones:
the DOM, focus and text selections stay. Awaits replay the values recorded during SSR instead of
fetching again, while still tracking what they read, so a later change re-runs the component and
fetches. Everything outside islands stays server HTML that never hydrates. `client:only` renders on
the client without server HTML. An island inside a streamed `<Suspense>` waits for its content
before hydrating.

**Nested directives.** A `client:*` inside an island's own render is just a component: it is
already client-side.

**Context starts at the island.** An island hydrates as its own root, so context the page provided
outside it (a `<Ctx value>` provider in a layout or page) does not reach it, and the server renders it the same
way: `useContext()` inside an island returns the context's default, unless the island or a component
inside it provides the value. Contexts provided inside the island work on both sides. To hand page
data to an island, pass it as a prop; to share state between islands, use scoped state
(`defineState`, [Sharing state](state.md)): one instance per page, seeded on the server and sent
with the page. In dev, an island that reads a context the page provided warns
`LUM4010`. Slots are page content, so they keep seeing the page's context. `<Suspense>`,
`<ErrorBoundary>`, request APIs (`locals()`, `cookies()`, …) and `getAbortSignal()` work inside islands
during SSR as everywhere else.

**Server-only boundaries.** `*.server.ts` files and everything under `src/server/` may not be
imported from code that reaches the browser (`LUM4003`): keep database access, secrets and
`env()` there. `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` fail with the chain of importers when the client graph
reaches one, and `lumiose check` reports the import. Server-only APIs (`request()`, `cookies()`,
`env()`, …) throw `LUM4003` in the browser build.

**Awaited data** inside an island is recorded during SSR and replayed during hydration, so the
browser does not fetch it again; it must be plain data (`LUM4007`), and it is visible in the page
source. Cached awaits (`fetchJSON`, `query`) are sent once per page however many islands await
them, and fill the browser cache, so later awaits and `invalidate(url)` start from them. So are the values of scoped state that islands import (`defineState`, `LUM4011`): the page
sends them once, before the islands that read them hydrate. The loader and `hydrate()` are described in [`lumiose/dom`](../reference/dom.md).

**The loader script.** `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` add the loader to every page that renders an
island, once, as `<script type="module" async>`: in the `<head>` when the shell has islands,
otherwise with the first streamed chunk that does. In a build, pages without islands load no
JavaScript; the loader is the client entry, and each island is a chunk it imports when the island's
trigger fires. The loader's chunk also holds the Lumiose runtime the islands share (signals, DOM,
hydration), so a page loads one runtime file before its islands: about 8 to 10 kB min+brotli in
the sample apps (`pnpm --filter lumiose size:apps` reports them; the runtime's 10 kB cap is checked by
`pnpm --filter lumiose size`). With your own server, pass its URL as
`renderToStream(root, { loaderUrl })`.

**Build output.** `lumiose build` puts the Lumiose runtime in one chunk: the island loader's, the SPA
entry's when the app has no islands, or a shared `lumiose-[hash].js` when it has both. The router's
History API fallback is a separate chunk, loaded only by browsers without the Navigation API.

Which runtime goes where follows one rule: the runtime chunk holds what the loader (or the SPA
entry) imports, plus the runtime that two or more islands (or SPA pages) import; runtime that only
one island imports goes into that island's chunk. A page's JavaScript then depends on its own
islands, not on every island of the app: the keyed selector the compiler emits for one island's
list, or `submit()` used by one form island, loads only on the pages that render that island. The trade-off: runtime shared
by several islands stays in the runtime chunk, so a page with none of them still loads it, but no
page loads more files than it has islands (a chunk per group of islands would cost one more request
each). Imports through `lumiose` and `lumiose/dom` count only the modules that declare what they
import. `fetchJSON` follows the same rule. One exception stays in the runtime chunk: a few bytes
that guard `fetchJSON`'s cache, so the minifier can drop the cache in apps without async components
or resources, which it can only do within one chunk.

Dynamic imports go through a smaller preload helper than Vite's: it still adds the imported chunk's
stylesheets (and waits for them, skipping those the page already holds in its merged or inline
styles), module preloads and the CSP nonce of `<meta property="csp-nonce">`, but dispatches no `vite:preloadError` event (the router loads the
URL with a document navigation when a page's module does not load).

**Islands from other packages.** Components of a linked workspace package (`"@acme/ui": "workspace:*"`)
can be or render islands too. Island records name modules without build-machine paths:
root-relative inside the project (`/src/components/LikeButton.stsx#LikeButton`), package-relative
outside it (`@acme/ui/src/Nav.stsx#Nav`), or by the import's bare name
(`import { Nav } from "@acme/ui"` gives `@acme/ui#Nav`). Either way, the `modulepreload` hint of a
`client:load` island points at its chunk in a build and at Vite's URL of the module in dev. Builds
also look for island call sites in the linked packages that depend on `lumiose`, so each of their
islands gets its chunk even when only server code renders it. Folders inside such a package that
are projects of their own (with a `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or `vite.config.*`, such as a
showcase app) are left out.

> **Status:** available: island calls and records (`LUM4001`, `LUM4002`), the loader with its
> triggers and event replay, and hydration (`LUM4006` on a mismatch), in `lumiose dev` and builds.

## API

| API                                                                           | Use                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible`, `client:media`, `client:only` | Make a component instance an island.                                  |
| `export function X`                                                           | Islands must be exported, so the browser can import them (`LUM4001`). |
| `*.server.ts`, `src/server/**`                                                | Server-only modules.                                                  |
| `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*`                                                    | Env values that may reach islands.                                    |

## Example

```stsx check file=components/LikeButton.stsx
// src/components/LikeButton.stsx: an island; exported so the browser can import it
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function LikeButton({ initial, children }: { initial: number; children?: JSX.Element }) {
  const likes = signal(initial);

  return (
    <button class="like" onClick={() => likes.update((n) => n + 1)}>
      {children} {likes()}
    </button>
  );
}

<style>
  .like { border-radius: 999px; }
</style>
```

```stsx check file=routes/posts/[id].stsx
// src/routes/posts/[id].stsx: a server component; only LikeButton ships JS
import { params } from "lumiose";
import { LikeButton } from "../../components/LikeButton.stsx";

export default function Post() {
  const { id } = params<"/posts/[id]">();

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Post {id}</h1>
      <LikeButton client:visible initial={3}>
        <strong>Like</strong>
      </LikeButton>
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **A non-exported island.** `function Counter` used with `client:load` cannot be imported by the
  browser. Export it (`LUM4001`).
- **Passing functions or class instances as island props.** `onSave={() => …}` cannot be
  serialized. Pass data, and do the work inside the island, or post a form (`LUM4002`).
- **Importing server code into an island.** `import { db } from "../server/db.server.ts"` in an
  island's graph is `LUM4003`. Call an endpoint with `fetchJSON` instead.
- **Touching `window` or `document` at module scope** in a module that also runs on the server.
  Move it into `onMount` or an effect (`LUM4004`).
- **Reading page context inside an island.** An island hydrates as its own root, so it does not
  see values the page provided outside it with a `<Ctx value>` provider, and it renders the same way on the
  server: `useContext()` returns the context's default unless the island (or a component inside it)
  provides the value. Pass the value as a prop, or share scoped state (`defineState`,
  [Sharing state](state.md)); dev warns with `LUM4010` when the page did provide it.
- **Different output on server and client**, for example from `Math.random()` or `Date.now()` in
  render. Hydration reports `LUM4006` in dev and client-renders the range in production.
- **Expecting `submit()` to refresh the page.** On MPA pages a successful `submit()` does not
  reload: the island owns its state and updates itself from the result. Call `invalidate()` when
  the page needs fresh server HTML ([Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)).
- **Making a whole page an island to get interactivity.** Mark only the interactive parts, or use
  an `spa` route ([Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md)).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4001](../errors/LUM4001.md): island component is not exported.
- [LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md): non-serializable island prop.
- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4004](../errors/LUM4004.md): browser API at module scope.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.
- [LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md): island reads context provided by the page.
- [LUM4011](../errors/LUM4011.md): non-serializable scoped state value.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Async components](async.md), [Sharing state](state.md) (state shared by islands).

<!-- source: concepts/routing.md -->

# Routing

> Routes are files under `src/routes`: pages (`.stsx`/`.tsx`), endpoints (`.ts`), nested `_layout` files and `_404`/`_error` pages. Route patterns and params are typed by `lumiose typegen`.

## Concept

```
src/
  routes/
    _layout.stsx            root layout; nested _layout.stsx per folder
    index.stsx              /
    about.stsx              /about
    blog/index.stsx         /blog
    blog/[slug].stsx        /blog/:slug
    docs/[...path].stsx     /docs/*  (rest param, may be empty)
    (marketing)/pricing.stsx  /pricing  (a group folder adds no URL segment)
    api/posts.ts            endpoint: export GET / POST / … = (ctx) => Response
    sitemap.xml.ts          endpoint at /sitemap.xml
    _404.stsx  _error.stsx  error pages, nearest one wins
  document.stsx             optional: owns <html>, <head> and <body>
  middleware.ts             optional: export default (ctx, next) => Promise<Response>
```

- **Matching priority:** static segments beat `[param]`, which beats `[...rest]`. Two files for
  the same pattern are `LUM5003`.
- Only `_layout`, `_404` and `_error` may start with `_`; keep shared modules out of `src/routes`
  (`LUM5002`).
- **Layouts** wrap every page below their folder and receive `{ params, children }`. `children`
  is the page (the outlet).
- **Pages** export a `default` component (it may be `async`), which receives `{ params }`. Other
  page exports: `mode`, `ssr`, `staticPaths`, `action`/`actions`, `headers` and `limits` (see
  [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md) and
  [Security](security.md)). Endpoints may export `limits` too.
- **Error pages:** `_404` renders unmatched URLs and `notFound()`; `_error` renders thrown errors
  and `error(status)`. Both receive `{ status, error }`. Outside dev, unexpected errors are masked
  as 500. An error page renders inside the layouts of its folder, like a page there: the root
  `_404` gets the root `_layout` (header, navigation), so it only renders its own content. If a
  layout itself fails, the error page renders without layouts. To give errors a different frame,
  move the regular pages into a group with their own layout (`(app)/_layout.stsx`) and keep the
  error page outside it.

**Typed routes.** `lumiose typegen` (run by `lumiose check` and the dev server) writes
`.lumiose/types/routes.d.ts`, which augments `RouteMap` (pages and endpoints) and `LayoutMap`
(layouts). Every route-bound type then takes the route pattern as a string literal, checked
against that table: an unknown or stale pattern is a type error, and editors complete it.

- `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug })` builds a URL and type-checks the pattern and params; the URL
  includes Vite's `base` and follows `trailingSlash` ([reference](../reference/app.md#href));
- `PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">` types a page's props, `LayoutProps<"/blog">` a layout's
  (`{ params, children }`, with the params of the layout's URL scope; route groups such as `(app)`
  add nothing to it), and `params<"/blog/[slug]">()` the params anywhere on the server;
- `RequestContext<P>`, `ActionContext<P>` and `Endpoint<P>` type `ctx.params` of middleware
  helpers, actions and endpoints (see [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)).

**Navigation.** Routes are MPA by default: links load the next document. Two `lumiose()` options in
`vite.config.ts` make these navigations smooth ([reference](../reference/vite.md#lumiose)); both are
progressive, so browsers without support navigate normally:

- **Prefetch** (`prefetch`, default `"hover"`). Pages get `<script type="speculationrules">` that
  prefetches same-origin links: when the pointer rests on a link (`"hover"`), early, as the browser
  sees fit (`"viewport"`), or never (`"none"`). Links to endpoints are never prefetched, since a GET
  endpoint may act (`/logout`). `spa` pages get no rules: there `<Link prefetch>` decides per link.
- **Per link**, `<Link prefetch>` from `lumiose/router` overrides the default on MPA pages too. There
  it renders a plain `<a>` (no JavaScript, no router) with a `data-l-prefetch` marker, and the
  rules prefetch it at its own level: `"none"` opts the link out, `"viewport"` prefetches it early,
  `"hover"` on hover. `<Link>` without `prefetch`, like a plain `<a>`, follows the default. The
  server `<Link>` tells the page it rendered a marker as it renders; a hand-written
  `data-l-prefetch` attribute on a plain `<a>` does not change the page's rules.
- **View Transitions** (`viewTransitions: true`, off by default). Every page opts into
  cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`), except for readers who
  prefer reduced motion: the old page cross-fades into the new one. An element morphs into its
  counterpart on the next page when both have the same CSS `view-transition-name`, unique on each
  page: in a style block (`.site-header { view-transition-name: site-header; }`) or per item with
  ``style={{ "view-transition-name": `cover-${post.slug}` }}``. Style the animation with the
  `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements in a global style block.

```ts
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [lumiose({ viewTransitions: true })] });
```

```tsx
import { Link } from "lumiose/router";

// In any page or component: the next page prefetches early, the archive never.
<Link href="/page/2" prefetch="viewport">Older →</Link>
<Link href="/archive" prefetch="none">Archive</Link>
```

Routes with `mode = "spa"` use the client router `lumiose/router` ([reference](../reference/router.md)):

- The SPA starts at the outermost `spa` layout (or the page itself) and covers every `spa` page
  below it; links between them navigate on the client, other links load the document.
- `<Link href prefetch>` (plain `<a>` links work too), `navigate(href, { replace })`, reactive
  `params()`, `route()` (the matched pattern), `url()`, `searchParams()` (`searchParams.set()` changes the
  query) and `isNavigating()`.
- Layouts persist: a layout's `children` is the outlet, and layouts shared by the old and the new
  page keep their state. A page with other param values (`songs/[id]`) is a new page.
- A navigation holds the old page until the new page's async content is ready, then swaps.
- Scroll restoration, focus reset, `_404` for unknown URLs and `notFound()`, `_error` for errors.

> **Status:** file routes, the manifest, matching, typegen, `href()`, the request handler, MPA
> prefetch and View Transitions, and the SPA router (`lumiose/router`) are available, served by
> `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and `lumiose preview`.

## API

| API                                                                                                   | Use                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export default function Page(props: PageProps<"/x/[id]">)`                                           | A page component.                                             |
| `export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/x">)`                                            | A layout: `{ params, children }`.                             |
| `params<"/x/[id]">()`                                                                                 | The matched route's params, typed by pattern (server).        |
| `href(pattern, params?)`                                                                              | Build a URL from a typed route pattern.                       |
| `Routes`, `RouteParams<P>`, `RouteMap`, `LayoutMap`                                                   | Route types.                                                  |
| `ErrorPageProps`                                                                                      | Props of `_404` and `_error`.                                 |
| `notFound()`, `error(status, message?)`, `redirect(to, status?)`                                      | Stop rendering; see [Server](server.md).                      |
| `lumiose/router`: `Link`, `navigate`, `isNavigating`, `searchParams`, reactive `url`/`params`/`route` | SPA routes and islands ([reference](../reference/router.md)). |

## Example

```stsx check file=routes/_layout.stsx
// src/routes/_layout.stsx
import { href, type LayoutProps } from "lumiose";

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/">) {
  return (
    <div class="app">
      <nav>
        <a href={href("/")}>Home</a>
        <a href={href("/blog/[slug]", { slug: "hello-world" })}>First post</a>
      </nav>
      {props.children}
    </div>
  );
}

<style global>
  body { margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
</style>
```

```stsx check file=routes/blog/[slug].stsx
// src/routes/blog/[slug].stsx
import { Title, notFound, type PageProps } from "lumiose";

const posts: Record<string, string> = { "hello-world": "Hello, world" };

export const mode = "server";

export default function Post({ params }: PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">) {
  // A function, so the JSX re-reads it when the params change (a plain const would be LUM2001).
  const title = () => posts[params.slug] ?? notFound();

  return (
    <article>
      <Title>{title()}</Title>
      <h1>{title()}</h1>
    </article>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/_404.tsx
// src/routes/_404.tsx: renders inside routes/_layout.stsx above (its nav and styles), so only
// the page content goes here
import type { ErrorPageProps } from "lumiose";

export default function NotFound({ status, error }: ErrorPageProps) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{status}</h1>
      <p>{error.message}</p>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/index.tsx
// src/routes/index.tsx
export default function Home() {
  return <h1>Home</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Helpers inside `src/routes`.** `src/routes/_utils.ts` or `src/routes/(x).stsx` are not routes
  (`LUM5002`). Put shared modules in `src/lib` or `src/components`.
- **Two files for one URL.** `blog.stsx` and `blog/index.stsx` both match `/blog` (`LUM5003`).
- **Hard-coded URLs.** `"/blog/" + slug` breaks silently when a route moves; `href("/blog/[slug]",
  { slug })` fails type-checking instead.
- **Reading params from `window.location` in a server component.** Use `props.params` or
  `params()`.
- **Matching `url().pathname` to know which route is showing.** `route() === "/songs/[id]"`
  compares the matched pattern, type-checked against the app's routes.
- **Route loaders.** There are none: load data in the async page component itself (decision-18).
- **`mode` that is not a string literal.** `export const mode = getMode()` cannot be read at build
  time (`LUM5002`).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): invalid route file.
- [LUM5003](../errors/LUM5003.md): duplicate route.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Server](server.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md), [`lumiose/router`](../reference/router.md).

<!-- source: concepts/data-and-actions.md -->

# Data and actions

> One way to read data (async components), one way to serve an API (endpoints), one way to mutate (form actions, enhanced with `submit()`). No route loaders, no RPC server functions.

## Concept

**Reading: async components.** Await data in the component that needs it. Server-only data
access (databases, secrets) lives in `*.server.ts` modules or `src/server/`. See
[Async components](async.md).

**HTTP APIs: endpoints.** A `.ts` file under `src/routes` exports handlers named after HTTP
methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` (and `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`), each
`(ctx) => Response`. Islands, SPA code and other clients call them with `fetch` or `fetchJSON`.

**`fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`** fetches JSON and returns plain data, so awaited results stay
serializable inside islands. Non-2xx responses throw a `FetchError` (an `HttpError` with `status`,
`url` and the parsed body as `data`); if a server component lets it escape, the page renders
`_error` (or `_404`) with that status. **During SSR, same-origin URLs are served in-process**, with
the page request's cookies, without a network round-trip. **Awaited in an async component, a GET
is cached by URL**: components awaiting the same URL share one request, and in the browser cached
data shows at once and revalidates in the background; `{ cache: "no-store" }` opts a request out.
`query(key, fn)` caches other data under an array key, and passes `fn` TanStack's
`{ signal, queryKey }`. See [Async components](async.md) and [reference: query](../reference/app.md#query).

**Mutations: form actions.** A page exports `action(ctx)` or named `actions = { name(ctx) }`. A
`<form method="post">` posts to the page (or to `?/name` for a named action) and works without
JavaScript. A named action's URL may keep the page's other query parameters: the action is the
parameter that starts with `/`, wherever it is, so `?status=open&/close` runs `close`, and
`ctx.url` still has `status=open` (useful to redirect back to a filtered list). An action receives
`ctx.formData()` and returns:

| Return                         | Result                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `redirect(to)` or a `Response` | Sent as is (303 after a POST).                                                                  |
| plain data                     | The page re-renders (200) and `actionData()` returns the data.                                  |
| `fail(status, data)`           | The page re-renders with `status`; `actionData()` returns `data`. Use it for validation errors. |

An Origin check protects page POSTs and form-encoded endpoint requests by default (403 for
cross-site requests).

**Enhancing forms.** Inside an island, `onSubmit={submit}` posts the form without a page load.
`submit()` resolves to `{ type: "success", status, data }`, `{ type: "failure", status, data }` or
follows a redirect, and sets `actionData()`. It rejects only for unexpected errors, with a
`FetchError`. `isSubmitting(name?)` is true while a submission is in flight.

**Refreshing.** `invalidate()` re-runs the current page's async components (SPA; the stale UI stays
until the new data arrives), or reloads the page (MPA). On client-routed (SPA) pages a successful
`submit()` runs it for you, so the page shows the mutation without extra code; pass
`submit(form, { invalidate: false })` to keep the page as it is. On MPA pages a successful
`submit()` never reloads: an island owns only its own state, so it updates itself from the result
(`result.data`, `actionData()`). Call `invalidate()` yourself when the page needs fresh
server-rendered content; on MPA pages that reloads and resets `actionData()`.

**Refreshing only what changed.** `invalidate(...targets)` refetches cache entries and re-runs only
the async components that awaited them, on SPA and MPA pages alike (islands included, no reload):
a string is a URL (the `fetchJSON` entry of that URL), an array a `query()` key prefix.
`submit(form, { invalidate: ["/api/books/1", ["stats"]] })` does the same after a successful
submission, instead of refreshing the whole page. Components rendered only on the server (outside
islands) are not re-run by a target: use `invalidate()` for those.

**Optimistic updates.** `optimistic(source)` follows `source` (a getter such as `() => props.likes`,
or a signal) and shows an overlay while a promise is pending: `likes.update((n) => n + 1,
submit(event))` or `likes.set(value, promise)`. When the promise settles the overlay drops:
on success the source already holds the new value, on failure (a `fail()` result or a rejection)
the value rolls back. On SPA pages `submit()` resolves after its `invalidate()`, so the refreshed
data replaces the overlay in the same task, with no flicker back. On MPA pages read the new value
from the result (`actionData()?.likes ?? props.likes` as the source), or pass
`submit(event).then(() => invalidate())`: the MPA `invalidate()` reloads and never settles, so the
overlay holds until the page unloads. Overlays apply in call order and drop independently, and an
`update` re-applies over the latest source. `optimistic` does not re-throw a rejection: await
`submit()` yourself to handle errors.

**Typed results.** Type an action's parameter with its page pattern,
`(ctx: ActionContext<"/books/new">)`, and let TypeScript infer what it returns:
`actionData<typeof actions>()` (or `typeof action`) is the union of the data the actions return
and the data they pass to `fail()`, or `undefined` before a submission. `submit<typeof actions.create>(form)`
resolves with `{ type: "success", data }` or `{ type: "failure", data }` typed from that action,
so the two are told apart by `type`; `actionData()` data is told apart by its shape.
`ActionData<typeof actions>` names that type for a child component's props. An island that posts to another page's action imports the
type only: `import type { actions } from "../routes/reading-list.stsx"`.

## API

| API                                                                  | Shape                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/x"> = (ctx) => Response`           | An endpoint method; `ctx.params` typed by the pattern.                 |
| `export const action = async (ctx: ActionContext<"/x">) => …`        | The default form action of a page.                                     |
| `export const actions = { name: (ctx: ActionContext<"/x">) => … }`   | Named actions, posted to `?/name`.                                     |
| `ctx.formData()`                                                     | The request body as `FormData` (400 if it is not a form).              |
| `fail(status, data?)`                                                | A failed action result.                                                |
| `actionData<typeof actions>()`                                       | The last action's data or `fail` data, typed by the actions. Reactive. |
| `submit(target, { action?, method?, signal?, invalidate? })`         | Post a form, submit event, `FormData`, `URLSearchParams` or a record.  |
| `submit(target, { invalidate: [url, key] })`                         | The same, refetching only those cache entries after a success.         |
| `submit<typeof actions.name>(…)`                                     | The same, resolving with that action's typed success and failure data. |
| `isSubmitting(name?)`                                                | Whether a submission (to `?/name`) is in flight.                       |
| `invalidate()`                                                       | Refresh the current page's server data.                                |
| `invalidate(...targets)`                                             | Refetch the entries of URLs and `query()` key prefixes.                |
| `query(key, fn)`                                                     | Awaited in a component, cache what `fn` resolves to under `key`.       |
| `optimistic(source)`, `.set(value, promise)`, `.update(fn, promise)` | A value with overlays held while their promises are pending.           |
| `fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`, `isFetchError(e)`                        | JSON fetch with typed errors; cached by URL in components.             |

## Example

```ts check file=routes/api/books.ts
// src/routes/api/books.ts: GET /api/books?q=…
import type { Endpoint } from "lumiose";

const books = [{ id: "1", title: "Dune" }];

export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/books"> = ({ url }) => {
  const q = url.searchParams.get("q")?.toLowerCase() ?? "";
  return Response.json(books.filter((book) => book.title.toLowerCase().includes(q)));
};
```

```stsx check file=routes/books/new.stsx
// src/routes/books/new.stsx: a form that works without JS, enhanced when it hydrates
import { actionData, fail, redirect, submit, isSubmitting, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

interface Errors {
  title?: string;
}

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async create(ctx: ActionContext<"/books/new">) {
    const form = await ctx.formData();
    const title = String(form.get("title") ?? "").trim();
    if (title === "") return fail(400, { title: "A title is required." } satisfies Errors);
    // await db.books.insert({ title });
    redirect("/books");
  },
};

export function NewBookForm() {
  return (
    <form method="post" action="?/create" onSubmit={submit}>
      <input name="title" />
      <p class="error">{actionData<typeof actions>()?.title}</p>
      <button disabled={isSubmitting("create")}>Add book</button>
    </form>
  );
}

export default function NewBook() {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>New book</h1>
      <NewBookForm client:load />
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check
import { fetchJSON, isFetchError } from "lumiose";

export async function BookSearch({ q }: { q: string }) {
  try {
    const books = await fetchJSON<{ id: string; title: string }[]>(
      `/api/books?q=${encodeURIComponent(q)}`,
    );
    return (
      <ul>
        {books.map((book) => (
          <li key={book.id}>{book.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if (isFetchError(error) && error.status === 404) return <p>No books.</p>;
    throw error;
  }
}
```

A like button that counts at once and rolls back if the post fails. The page is MPA, so the island
reads the new count from the action's result; on an SPA page `() => props.likes` is enough, as
`submit()` refreshes the props before it resolves:

```stsx check file=routes/likes/[id].stsx
// src/routes/likes/[id].stsx
import { actionData, optimistic, submit, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

let count = 3; // a database in a real app

export const actions = {
  like(_ctx: ActionContext<"/likes/[id]">) {
    count += 1;
    return { likes: count };
  },
};

export function LikeButton(props: { likes: number }) {
  const likes = optimistic(() => actionData<typeof actions>()?.likes ?? props.likes);
  return (
    <form
      method="post"
      action="?/like"
      onSubmit={(event) => likes.update((n) => n + 1, submit(event))}
    >
      <button>Like ({likes()})</button>
    </form>
  );
}

export default function Post() {
  return <LikeButton client:load likes={count} />;
}
```

Keeping the page's filters through a named action:

```stsx check file=routes/issues.stsx
// src/routes/issues.stsx: the list is filtered by ?status=; "Close" keeps the filter
import { redirect, url, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async close(ctx: ActionContext) {
    // await db.issues.close((await ctx.formData()).getAll("ids"));
    const back = new URL(ctx.url);
    back.searchParams.delete("/close"); // the action key; the filters stay
    redirect(back.pathname + back.search);
  },
};

export default function Issues() {
  const search = url().search; // "?status=open", or ""
  return (
    <form method="post" action={`${search === "" ? "?" : `${search}&`}/close`}>
      {/* rows with <input type="checkbox" name="ids" value={id} /> */}
      <button>Close selected</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Route loaders.** Lumiose has none. Await data in the page component; it is the same code on every
  route mode.
- **Calling server code from an island.** Import nothing from `*.server.ts` in island code
  (`LUM4003`); expose an endpoint and call it with `fetchJSON`.
- **`fetch()` instead of `fetchJSON()` inside islands.** A `Response` is not serializable
  (`LUM4007`).
- **Expecting `submit()` to reject on validation errors.** `fail()` resolves with
  `{ type: "failure" }`; only unexpected errors reject.
- **Calling `invalidate()` after a successful `submit()` on an SPA page.** `submit()` already did;
  a second call refreshes twice.
- **Reaching for a client cache library first.** `fetchJSON` and `query` already dedupe, cache and
  revalidate component awaits on the server and in the browser. Use
  [`@lumiose/query`](../reference/query.md) for client data that needs polling, refetching on focus,
  retries or per-query stale times.
- **Expecting an MPA page to refresh after `submit()`.** On MPA pages `submit()` never reloads.
  Update the island from the result (a toggle sets its own state, a list removes its own row), or
  call `invalidate()` explicitly if the page must show fresh server HTML.
- **Leaving an optimistic overlay up after the request.** Pass the promise to `set`/`update`
  rather than resetting by hand, and on MPA pages give the island a source that changes
  (`actionData()`, or an explicit `invalidate()`), or the value returns to the old one on success.
- **Forms without `method="post"`.** Actions only run for POST; `submit()` refuses a form that does
  not say `method="post"`, as the no-JS form would not post either.
- **Throwing for validation errors.** A thrown error renders `_error`. Return `fail(400, data)`.
- **Casting action data.** `actionData<{ errors: … }>()` is a type error: pass `typeof actions`.
  Annotating the export with `Action` (`export const action: Action = …`) hides what it returns,
  so annotate the parameter instead, or check it with `satisfies Action<"/x">`. Add
  `satisfies YourFailure` to `fail()` data whose string literals should stay literal.
- **Disabling the Origin check to make a cross-site form work.** Allow the specific origin instead
  (`csrf.allowedOrigins` in the request handler options).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Server](server.md), [Routing](routing.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: concepts/server.md -->

# Server

> Server code gets the request context everywhere: `ctx` in middleware, endpoints and actions, and `request()`, `url()`, `params()`, `route()`, `locals()`, `cookies()` and `response()` anywhere during a server render.

## Concept

**Request context.** Middleware, endpoints and actions receive
`ctx = { request, url, params, locals, cookies, env, platform }`. During a server render, the same values are
available through functions scoped to the current request (they work after `await` too):
`request()`, `url()`, `params()`, `route()` (the matched pattern), `locals()`, `cookies()`,
`response()` and `env(name)`.

**Platform.** `ctx.platform` is what the host adds to a request: `env` (the platform's bindings,
such as Cloudflare's KV or D1; `{}` elsewhere), `waitUntil(promise)` (work that continues after the
response) and `clientAddress` (the client's IP as the host sees it). Each has a fallback, so the
same code runs on every host ([server build](../reference/server-entry.md#platform)). Type the
bindings by augmenting `PlatformEnv`. A server component that needs them gets them from middleware,
through `locals`.

**Middleware.** `src/middleware.ts` default-exports `(ctx, next) => Promise<Response>` (or an array,
run in order). Use it for sessions, auth and headers. Put request data on `ctx.locals`, and type it
by augmenting `Locals`:

```ts
declare module "lumiose" {
  interface Locals {
    user: { id: string; name: string } | null;
  }
}
```

**Control flow.** `redirect(to, status?)`, `notFound()` and `error(status, message?)` throw; the
framework turns them into a redirect or the nearest `_404`/`_error` page. Without a status,
`redirect()` uses 302 for GET/HEAD and 303 for other methods.

**Cookies.** `cookies.get/getAll/set/delete`. Defaults: `path=/`, `httpOnly`, `sameSite=lax`, and
`secure` on HTTPS and in production. `signedCookie(name)` signs values with HMAC-SHA256 (secret:
`LUMIOSE_SECRET`, or rotate with an array of secrets); signing protects integrity, not
confidentiality. Secrets must be at least 32 bytes: a shorter one throws in production and warns
in development, unless you pass `{ allowWeakSecret: true }`. Generate one with
`openssl rand -base64 32`.

**Status and headers.** `response().setStatus()` and `setHeader()` change the page response, and
a page may export `headers(ctx)`. They are writable **until the shell is sent** (see
[Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md)); a change inside a streamed `<Suspense>` boundary is
`LUM5004`.

**Env.** `env("NAME")` reads server env variables (the adapter's env, else `process.env`) in
server-only code. Only `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` reaches client code (`@lumiose/vite` sets Vite's
`envPrefix` to `"PUBLIC_"` unless the config sets its own); `publicEnv()` returns that subset.

**Server-only code** lives in `*.server.ts` modules and under `src/server/`. Importing it from code
that reaches the browser is `LUM4003`, also through a web worker, `new URL("…", import.meta.url)`
or a `?raw`/`?url` import. `lumiose dev` does not serve these files over HTTP either: they are added
to Vite's `server.fs.deny` unless the config sets its own list (the server still loads them).

> **Status:** the request handler, middleware, endpoints, cookies, env and error pages are
> available, served by `lumiose dev` and by the build output (`lumiose preview`,
> [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md)).

## API

| API                                                                      | Use                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RequestContext<P>` (`ctx`)                                              | `{ request, url, params, locals, cookies, env, platform }`.            |
| `Middleware`                                                             | `(ctx, next) => Response \| Promise<Response>`.                        |
| `request()`, `url()`, `params<P>()`, `route()`, `locals()`, `cookies()`  | Request APIs during a server render.                                   |
| `response()`                                                             | `{ status, setStatus, getHeader, setHeader }` until the shell is sent. |
| `redirect(to, status?)`, `notFound(message?)`, `error(status, message?)` | Throw to stop rendering.                                               |
| `isRedirect(e)`, `isHttpError(e)`                                        | Recognize those when you catch errors.                                 |
| `signedCookie(name, options?)`                                           | `{ get(cookies), set(cookies, value), delete(cookies) }`.              |
| `env(name)`, `publicEnv(source?)`                                        | Server env; the `PUBLIC_*` subset.                                     |
| `Locals`                                                                 | Interface to augment with your request data.                           |
| `Platform`, `PlatformEnv`                                                | `ctx.platform`; the interface to augment with your bindings.           |

## Example

```ts check file=middleware.ts
// src/middleware.ts
import { signedCookie, type Middleware } from "lumiose";

const session = signedCookie("session");

declare module "lumiose" {
  interface Locals {
    userId: string | null;
  }
}

const middleware: Middleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.locals.userId = (await session.get(ctx.cookies)) ?? null;
  if (ctx.url.pathname.startsWith("/account") && ctx.locals.userId === null) {
    return Response.redirect(new URL("/login", ctx.url), 303);
  }
  const res = await next();
  res.headers.set("x-frame-options", "DENY");
  return res;
};

export default middleware;
```

```tsx check file=routes/account.tsx
// src/routes/account.tsx
import { locals, redirect, response } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

export default function Account() {
  const { userId } = locals();
  if (userId === null) redirect("/login");
  response().setHeader("cache-control", "private, no-store");

  return <h1>Signed in as {userId}</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading request APIs in a `static` route.** `cookies()`, `request()` and friends throw
  `LUM5001` while prerendering. Set `export const mode = "server"`.
- **Setting headers or status after the shell.** Inside a streamed `<Suspense>` boundary it is too
  late (`LUM5004`). Do it before the boundary, in the page body outside `<Suspense>`, in
  `headers(ctx)` or in middleware.
- **Reading secrets with `import.meta.env`.** Only `PUBLIC_*` values exist there. Use `env("NAME")`
  in server-only modules.
- **Catching `redirect()` by accident.** It throws. In a `try`/`catch`, rethrow when
  `isRedirect(error) || isHttpError(error)`.
