- **Storing request data in module-scope variables.** Modules are shared by every request. Use
  `locals`, context or component state (`LUM4008`).
- **Expecting signed cookies to hide data.** They are tamper-proof, not encrypted.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md), [Routing](routing.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: concepts/rendering-modes.md -->

# Rendering modes

> Each route picks a mode: `static` (built HTML, the default), `server` (rendered per request, shell first, then streamed `<Suspense>` boundaries) or `spa` (a client-routed subtree, rendered per request, prerendered at build time or in the browser). All three use the same components.

## Concept

| Mode               | HTML                                                                                                                | JS shipped        | Navigation                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `static` (default) | At build time, for each path from `staticPaths()`                                                                   | Islands only      | MPA (prefetch, opt-in View Transitions) |
| `server`           | Per request: the shell, then streamed boundaries                                                                    | Islands only      | MPA (prefetch, opt-in View Transitions) |
| `spa`              | Server-rendered (per request, or at build time with `prerender`) and hydrated, or a client shell with `ssr = false` | The whole subtree | Client router (`<Link prefetch>`)       |

A route sets `export const mode = "server"` (a string literal); pages inherit the mode of their
nearest layout that sets one, else the project default set in `vite.config.ts` with
`lumiose({ mode: "server" })` (`"static"` when unset). `export const ssr = false` applies to `spa`
routes: the build emits a static shell and the page renders in the browser. `lumiose({ ssr: false })`
makes that the default for every `spa` route, so `lumiose({ mode: "spa", ssr: false })` turns the
whole project into a client-rendered SPA built as static files. `export const prerender = true`
renders an `spa` page (or, in a layout, every `spa` page below it) at build time instead of per
request, and `lumiose({ prerender: true })` makes that the default for every `spa` page (see
[Prerendered SPA routes](#prerendered-spa-routes)).

**Shell first, then stream (server mode).**

1. **Shell.** The response starts once everything **outside** `<Suspense>` has resolved, including
   async components without a boundary. Until then you can still set the status, headers and
   cookies, call `redirect()`, `notFound()` or `error()`, and add `<Title>`/`<Meta>`/`<Head>`.
   A failure renders `_error` with the right status.
2. **Stream.** `<Suspense>` boundaries then stream in as they resolve, out of order, and replace
   their fallbacks (with native `<template for>` updates or a ~300 B `$swap` script). An error
   renders the boundary's `<ErrorBoundary>` in place. A head or status change inside a streamed
   boundary is `LUM5004`.
3. **SSG and prerender** resolve everything: no fallbacks and no swap scripts.

So: put slow, optional content inside `<Suspense>` to send the page sooner; leave essential
content (and anything that decides the status) outside.

**Hydration.** Only islands and SPA subtrees hydrate. The compiled code has a single DOM walk;
importing `lumiose/dom/hydrate` (done by the island loader and SPA entries) makes it claim existing
server nodes instead of creating them, so bundles without hydration carry no hydration code.
Markers are comments, used only for blocks, branches, text separators and async ranges.

**SPA mode.** An `spa` subtree starts at the outermost `spa` layout of a page (or at the page
itself) and renders as a single root island: layouts above it render on the server only. Its props
come from serializable route data; `request`, `cookies` and `locals` are not passed in. SPA code
calls endpoints instead. Pages with an SPA load the SPA entry (the client route table, a lazy
chunk per SPA layout and page, and the island loader) and navigate with
[`lumiose/router`](../reference/router.md). In a build, the page also modulepreloads the chunks of
its SPA layouts and page (and their imports), so a deep link fetches them alongside the entry
instead of after it has run. When nothing in a build hydrates (every SPA page is
`ssr = false` and the app has no islands), the SPA entry starts the router without the island
loader, and the build ships no hydration code.

- **`ssr` (the default):** the server renders the island and the browser hydrates it, replaying
  the server's awaited data.
- **`ssr = false`:** the server sends a shell (the document, the layouts above the SPA and an
  empty island) without loading the SPA's modules, so they may use browser APIs at module scope;
  the browser renders the island. Such pages cannot export `action` or `headers`: use endpoints.
- `_404` and `_error` pages below an `spa` layout render inside the SPA too.

### Prerendered SPA routes

`export const prerender = true` on an `spa` page renders it in the build's prerender step, as a
`static` page is rendered: the build writes real HTML for it, which the SPA entry hydrates, and later
navigation is client-side as usual. Search engines, link previews and visitors without JavaScript
see the content, and a static host can serve the page.

- **Opt in per page, per layout or for the project.** `export const prerender = true` on a page;
  on a layout, for every `spa` page below it; or `lumiose({ prerender: true })` for every `spa`
  page. It is inherited like `mode` and `ssr`: the page's own export wins, then the nearest layout
  that sets it, then the project default. A page opts out with `export const prerender = false`,
  and is then rendered per request; a layout's `prerender = false` turns the default off for its
  subtree. `prerender` must be a literal `true` or `false`. In an endpoint, or in a layout or page
  whose mode is `static` or `server`, it has no effect (a `LUM5002` warning).

  ```stsx
  // src/routes/_layout.stsx: every page below is prerendered…
  export const mode = "spa";
  export const prerender = true;
  ```

  ```stsx
  // src/routes/account.stsx: …except this one, which reads cookies per request
  export const prerender = false;
  ```

- **Params.** A page with params lists its paths with `staticPaths()`, as a `static` page does;
  without it the build stops. The build writes one HTML file per path. On a static host, any other
  URL gets `404.html`, which renders the root `_404` inside the SPA.
- **Deep links to paths that were not prerendered.** When `404.html` loads at the URL of an SPA page
  with params (a song saved in the browser, a record created after the build), the router renders
  that page in the browser instead of the `_404`. The page decides with the browser's data, and
  `notFound()` brings the `_404` back. A small inline script in `404.html` hides the document until
  the router has rendered, so the 404 does not flash (at most 8 s, should the SPA not start). A URL
  that matches no page keeps the `_404`, with status 404, and so does every URL without
  JavaScript. `lumiose dev` and a server build do the same when such a page calls `notFound()`
  while it renders on the server, which has no browser data. `ssr = false` pages with params
  behave the same way. This needs a root `_404` page: without one, `404.html` is a plain error
  page without the SPA.
- **No request.** The page renders at build time, so request APIs (`cookies()`, `request()`,
  `locals()`, `response()`, `url().searchParams`) stop the build with `LUM5001`. Read them in the
  browser, or call an endpoint.
- **Browser-only code.** The page, its `spa` layouts and everything they import now load on the
  server at build time, which an `ssr = false` page never did. Move browser APIs (`window`,
  `document`, `localStorage`, `AudioContext`, `requestAnimationFrame`) out of module scope and out
  of component setup: read them in `onMount()`, an effect or an event handler, which run only in
  the browser. Create browser objects lazily, on first use. The compiler warns about browser
  globals at module scope (`LUM4004`).
- **Not with `ssr = false`.** `ssr = false` renders the page only in the browser. A page whose
  `prerender = true` (its own or a layout's) meets `ssr = false` (its own, a layout's or the
  project's) is `LUM5006`: give a browser-only page under a prerendering layout
  `export const prerender = false`. `lumiose({ prerender: true, ssr: false })` is rejected. Under
  `lumiose({ prerender: true })` alone, a page with `ssr = false` stays a shell.

To move a client-rendered SPA (`ssr = false`) to prerendering: remove `ssr = false`, make its
modules safe to load on the server (above), add `staticPaths()` to pages with params, then set
`prerender = true` on the SPA's layout (or `lumiose({ prerender: true })`). `lumiose dev` renders the pages per request,
fully resolved as the build does, so hydration problems show up there first.

**Build (`lumiose build`).** 1. client build (islands, SPA, CSS, assets, `public/`), 2. server
build, 3. prerender of every `static` route and every `spa` page with `prerender` (each
`staticPaths()` entry for routes with params) and every static `GET` endpoint, in-process through the built handler and fully resolved (no fallbacks
or swap scripts), 4. precompression: a `.br` and a `.gz` copy next to every text file of
`dist/client` of at least 1 kB, which `@lumiose/adapter-node` (and most static hosts and CDNs) serve
to browsers that accept them. Output:

- `dist/client`: assets and prerendered files. Assets include those only server-rendered code
  imports (`import photo from "./photo.png"` in a route, a relative `<img src>` in a `.md`
  import), written once under `assets/` with the fingerprinted URL the HTML uses. Prerendered
  files are `path/index.html` (`path.html` with
  `lumiose({ trailingSlash: "never" })`, prerendered `spa` pages included), endpoint files such as
  `sitemap.xml`, the shell of each
  `ssr = false` page without params, and `404.html` from the root `_404` when the root scope is
  static or `spa`. In an `ssr = false` SPA, `404.html` is the shell: a static host that serves it
  for unknown URLs gets deep links to every route. Vite's `base` applies to URLs, not to file
  paths.
- `dist/server/entry.js`: `export default { fetch(request, platform?) }`, which serves the
  static files of `dist/client`, then the app ([server build](../reference/server-entry.md)), plus
  `createHandler({ env })` (the app alone) and `config`.
  The server output bundles your server code, linked workspace packages and the Lumiose runtime
  (npm dependencies stay external, as Vite does for SSR), minified with function and class names
  kept, so production stack traces still name the functions.

A route (`static`, or `spa` with `prerender`) that reads the request while it prerenders (`cookies()`, `locals()`, `request()`,
`response()`, `url().searchParams`) stops the build with [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md); a static
endpoint can only export `GET` ([LUM5005](../errors/LUM5005.md)). Middleware still runs. A form
post to a prerendered page reaches its `action` on the server. Serve the build with
`@lumiose/adapter-node` (`createServer({ port })`: `dist/client` with caching headers, then the
handler) or `lumiose preview`, or run `dist/server/entry.js` with Bun or Deno. A site whose every route is prerendered (no `server` route, no `spa`
route rendered per request, no form action; `ssr = false` routes with params need a `404.html`
shell) builds no `dist/server`: deploy `dist/client` to any static host, and `lumiose preview` serves
it without the adapter. Set response headers once with `lumiose({ headers })`
([@lumiose/vite](../reference/vite.md#lumiose)).

> **Status:** `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build`, prerendering,
> [`@lumiose/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md), CSS links in built pages, the island
> loader (hydration), SPA mode (one root island, `ssr = false` shells, prerendered pages) and the
> SPA router are available.

## API

| API                                                     | Use                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `export const mode = "static" \| "server" \| "spa"`     | The route's mode (inherited from layouts).                                                 |
| `export const ssr = false`                              | `spa` routes: render in the browser only.                                                  |
| `export const prerender = true`                         | `spa` pages: render at build time into HTML that hydrates (inherited from layouts).        |
| `lumiose({ mode, ssr, prerender })` in `vite.config.ts` | The project defaults for routes and layouts that do not set them.                          |
| `export async function staticPaths()`                   | `static` routes and prerendered `spa` pages with params: `[{ params: { slug: "a" } }, …]`. |
| `export function headers(ctx)`                          | Response headers for the page.                                                             |
| `<Suspense fallback>`                                   | Marks content that may stream after the shell.                                             |
| `renderToStream(root, options?)`                        | The server renderer behind it all; see [reference: server](../reference/server.md).        |

## Example

```stsx check file=routes/stats.stsx
// src/routes/stats.stsx: the shell (title, heading) is sent first; the slow chart streams in
import { Suspense, Title } from "lumiose";

export const mode = "server";

async function SlowChart() {
  const points = await new Promise<number[]>((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve([3, 1, 4]), 500));
  return <p>Points: {points.join(", ")}</p>;
}

export default function Stats() {
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>Stats</Title>
      <h1>Stats</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading chart…</p>}>
        <SlowChart />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/docs/[slug].tsx
// src/routes/docs/[slug].tsx: prerendered for each slug
import type { PageProps } from "lumiose";

const pages = { intro: "Introduction", setup: "Setup" } as const;

export async function staticPaths() {
  return Object.keys(pages).map((slug) => ({ params: { slug } }));
}

export default function Doc({ params }: PageProps<"/docs/[slug]">) {
  return <h1>{pages[params.slug as keyof typeof pages]}</h1>;
}
```

```stsx check file=routes/tracks/[id].stsx
// src/routes/tracks/[id].stsx: prerendered for each id, then hydrated into the SPA
import { onMount, signal } from "lumiose";
import { params } from "lumiose/router";

export const mode = "spa"; // or from a layout, or lumiose({ mode: "spa" })
export const prerender = true;

export function staticPaths() {
  return ["1", "2", "3"].map((id) => ({ params: { id } }));
}

export default function Track() {
  const volume = signal(1);
  // Browser-only: runs after hydration, never at build time.
  onMount(() => volume.set(Number(localStorage.getItem("volume") ?? 1)));
  return <h1>Track {params().id} (volume {volume()})</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Request APIs in a `static` route.** `cookies()`, `request()`, `locals()` and actions need
  `mode = "server"` (`LUM5001`).
- **Setting status or `<Title>` inside `<Suspense>`.** It arrives after the shell was sent
  (`LUM5004`). Decide them outside the boundary.
- **Wrapping the whole page in `<Suspense>`.** The shell is then just the fallback, and the status
  cannot change. Wrap only slow, optional parts.
- **Expecting `spa` routes to receive `cookies` or `locals` as props.** They are not serializable
  into the SPA (`LUM4002`); call an endpoint.
- **Computing `mode` at runtime.** `mode` must be a string literal (`LUM5002`).
- **Browser APIs at module scope or in component setup of a prerendered `spa` page.** The build
  renders it on the server; read them in `onMount()` or an event handler (`LUM4004`).
- **`prerender = true` on an `ssr = false` page.** The page cannot be both (`LUM5006`), also when
  one of them comes from a layout.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md): non-serializable island prop.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.
- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): invalid route file.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.
- [LUM5006](../errors/LUM5006.md): prerendered page that renders only in the browser.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.

See also: [Islands](islands.md), [Async components](async.md), [Head and document](head.md).

<!-- source: concepts/svg.md -->

# SVG imports

> `import Icon from "./icon.svg"` gives an inline SVG component: optimised at build time, styled with `currentColor` and props, labelled with `title`, the same on the server, the client and in islands. `?url` and `?raw` keep Vite's meaning.

## Concept

With the Lumiose Vite plugin, an `.svg` file in your project imports as a component. The build
optimises the file with [SVGO](https://svgo.dev) and compiles it into a static template, so
rendering an icon clones markup, on the server and in the browser alike. The icon is
**inline**: its paths are part of the page's HTML, CSS reaches them, and nothing is fetched.

- **Props override the file.** The file's root attributes (`width`, `height`, `viewBox`, `fill`,
  `stroke`, `class`, …) are defaults; any `<svg>` prop you pass replaces the matching one:
  `class`, `style`, `width`, `height`, `fill`, `aria-*`, events and `ref`. The defaults other
  than `class` and `style` stay in the cloned template, so rendering an icon only sets the props
  you pass.
- **Colour.** Icons drawn with `currentColor` follow the text colour (`color` in CSS). For icons
  with a hard-coded colour, set `lumiose({ svg: { currentColor: true } })` to replace every colour
  with `currentColor`, or pass `fill`/`stroke` props.
- **Accessibility.** Without `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, an icon is decorative
  and gets `aria-hidden="true"`. `title="Home"` renders `<title>` as the first child, with
  `role="img"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing at it. The id comes from the file and the title
  text, so the server and the client agree without a counter. The file's own `<title>` is
  dropped: the prop is the label.
- **What the build keeps.** An allowlist, whatever the SVGO config, so an icon file can never
  run script or act as HTML on your page:
  - **Elements**: the SVG ones, spelled as SVG spells them (`linearGradient`, not
    `lineargradient`): `svg`, `g`, `defs`, `symbol`, `use`, `switch`, `a`, `style`, the shapes
    (`path`, `rect`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`), text (`text`, `tspan`,
    `textPath`), `image`, paint servers, `clipPath`, `mask`, `marker`, `filter` and every `fe*`
    primitive, and the SMIL animations `animate`, `animateMotion`, `animateTransform`, `set` and
    `mpath`. Anything else is dropped with its content: `<script>`, `<foreignObject>` (and the
    HTML in it), editor elements (`sodipodi:*`, `<rdf>`), unknown or invalid names.
  - **Attributes**: the SVG presentation, geometry, link, text, gradient, filter and animation
    attributes, `id`, `class`, `style`, `role`, `tabindex`, `aria-*` and `data-*`, as plain string
    attributes. Event handlers (`onload`), DOM properties (`innerHTML`) and attributes of other
    namespaces are dropped; so are `javascript:` URLs.
  - **Animations** that target a link (`href`), a handler (`on…`) or `style`, in any letter case,
    or whose `values`/`from`/`to`/`by` hold a `javascript:` URL, are dropped.
  - **`<style>` text** keeps its CSS, with `<` and `&` written as CSS escapes (`\3c `, `\26 `):
    in a page, an inline SVG's `<style>` is parsed as markup, where they could open a tag.
  - Elements nested more than 128 levels deep make the file an error.

  Comments and editor metadata go too, and redundant markup when optimising. Ids get a per-file
  prefix, and so do the references to them (`href="#id"`, `url(#id)`, `<style>` selectors);
  class names get it too when the file has a `<style>`. Icons never clash with each other or with
  the page.

- **Optimisation.** By default SVGO runs its `preset-default` plus `convertStyleToAttrs` (fewer
  `style` attributes, for strict CSPs). Pass your own SVGO config as `optimize` to choose the
  plugins (`{ plugins: [...] }`, `multipass`, `floatPrecision`), or `false` to skip SVGO.
- **Query switches.** `./icon.svg` and `./icon.svg?inline` are the component. `?url` is Vite's
  asset URL (or a `data:` URL for small files) and `?raw` the file's text.
- **Dependencies.** `.svg` files under `node_modules` (the plugin's `exclude`) keep Vite's URL
  import, which is what a library importing an `.svg` expects. `lumiose({ svg: false })` leaves
  every `.svg` import to Vite.

Inline is a deliberate choice over sprites (`<use href="#id">`): with the compression every
server applies, a page of repeated inline icons transfers about as many bytes as a sprite, and
inline icons render faster and can be styled and animated part by part.

## API

| Import / option                            | Gives                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `import Icon from "./icon.svg"`            | `(props: JSX.SVGProps<SVGSVGElement> & { title?: string })` |
| `import Icon from "./icon.svg?inline"`     | The same component                                          |
| `import url from "./icon.svg?url"`         | The asset URL (`string`, Vite)                              |
| `import text from "./icon.svg?raw"`        | The file's text (`string`, Vite)                            |
| `lumiose({ svg: { optimize: config } })`   | Optimise with your SVGO config instead of Lumiose's         |
| `lumiose({ svg: { optimize: false } })`    | Skip SVGO (sanitising and id prefixes still run)            |
| `lumiose({ svg: { currentColor: true } })` | Replace every colour with `currentColor`                    |
| `lumiose({ svg: false })`                  | `.svg` imports stay Vite's URLs                             |

The types come with `lumiose/env` (`"types": ["lumiose/env"]` in `tsconfig.json`).

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts: your own SVGO plugins (optional)
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    lumiose({
      svg: { optimize: { multipass: true, plugins: ["preset-default", "removeDimensions"] } },
    }),
  ],
});
```

```tsx
// src/components/Nav.stsx
import Home from "../icons/home.svg";
import Search from "../icons/search.svg";
import logoUrl from "../icons/logo.svg?url";

export function Nav() {
  return (
    <nav>
      <img src={logoUrl} alt="Acme" width={96} height={24} />
      <a href="/" class="link">
        <Home class="icon" /> Home
      </a>
      <button type="button">
        <Search class="icon" title="Search" />
      </button>
    </nav>
  );
}

<style>
  .link { color: rebeccapurple; }
  .icon { width: 1.25em; height: 1.25em; vertical-align: -0.2em; }
  .link:hover .icon { color: crimson; }
</style>
```

The `Home` icon is decorative (its link has text); the search button has no text, so its icon
gets a `title`. Both follow the link or button colour through `currentColor`, and `class="icon"`
receives the file's scope, so the scoped `.icon` rule applies.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting a URL.** Before Lumiose, `import icon from "./icon.svg"` was a URL string in Vite.
  Use `./icon.svg?url` for `<img src>` and CSS, or `lumiose({ svg: false })` for the old behaviour
  everywhere.
- **Loading `vite/client` types first.** `vite/client` also declares `*.svg` (as a string), and
  whichever comes first in `"types"` wins: `Icon` then "cannot be used as a JSX component". List
  `lumiose/env` first, or drop `vite/client` (`lumiose/env` already types `import.meta.env`).
  Both type `*.svg` with a default export, a duplicate that TypeScript reports in the two `.d.ts`
  files unless `skipLibCheck` is on (the generated tsconfig sets it).
- **Styling inner paths from a scoped block.** The paths belong to the icon component, so only the
  root `<svg>` (through `class`) carries your component's scope. Use inherited properties
  (`color`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`) on the root, or `:deep(path)`.
- **Setting only `width`.** The file's `height` stays, and the drawing is centred in that box.
  Pass both, or size icons with CSS as above.
- **Labelling a decorative icon.** An icon next to visible text needs no `title`; a `title` there
  makes screen readers repeat the text.
- **Hard-coded colours in an icon set.** If icons stay black whatever `color` says, the files
  hard-code a colour: use `lumiose({ svg: { currentColor: true } })` for monochrome sets. It runs
  SVGO's `convertColors` before your own plugins, so with a custom config it still applies.
- **Expecting `<foreignObject>` content.** HTML inside an icon is dropped; render it with a
  component next to the icon.
- **Removing `viewBox` in a custom SVGO config.** Without `viewBox` an icon no longer scales with
  `width`/`height`; SVGO's `preset-default` keeps it, `removeViewBox` drops it.

## Related diagnostics

A file that is not well-formed SVG fails the build with its location
(`icon.svg: invalid SVG: … at 3:12`), as does a file whose root element is not `<svg>` and one
whose elements nest more than 128 levels deep.

See also: [Styles](styles.md), [JSX](jsx.md), [reference: `@lumiose/vite`](../reference/vite.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/content.md -->

# Markdown and HTML imports

> With `lumiose({ md: true, html: true })`, `import Post, { frontmatter, headings } from "./post.md"` and `import Card from "./card.html"` give static components, compiled at build time: CommonMark + GFM with heading ids, a headings list and YAML frontmatter, or HTML whose `<style>` is scoped to the file and whose `<script>` runs in the browser.

## Concept

Both are opt-in options of the Vite plugin. A `.md` or `.html` file in your project then imports
as a component that renders the file's content. The build compiles it into a static template,
like any `.stsx` markup, so it costs a clone in the browser and a string on the server. It works
the same in `static`, `server` and `spa` routes and inside islands.

**Markdown** is plain CommonMark with the GitHub extensions: tables, strikethrough, task lists,
autolinks (`www.example.com`, bare URLs) and footnotes. There is no MDX: Markdown cannot use
components or JS expressions. Raw HTML is allowed, since the file is part of your project, and
follows the HTML rules below, except for `<script>`: Markdown is content only, so a `<script>`
fails the build ([LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md)). Put scripts in an `.html` import or a
component.

- **Heading ids.** Each heading gets a GitHub-style id from its text: `## Hello, World!` becomes
  `id="hello-world"`, and repeats get `-1`, `-2`. A heading written as raw HTML with its own `id`
  keeps it.
- **Frontmatter.** A leading block between `---` lines is YAML (1.2 core schema: dates stay
  strings). The module exports it as `frontmatter`: plain data, `{}` without a block, typed
  `Frontmatter` (any keys, `unknown` values). Lumiose has no schema conventions. To validate or transform it at build time, pass a hook:
  `lumiose({ md: { frontmatter(data, { file }) { …; return data } } })`. What the hook returns is
  exported (returning `undefined` keeps `data`), and it may be async. A hook that throws fails the
  build with the file's name. Values may be JSON data, `Date`, `URL`, `Map`, `Set`, `BigInt`,
  `undefined` or `RegExp`.
- **Headings list.** The module also exports `headings`: each heading's `depth` (1 to 6), `text`
  and `id`, in document order, raw HTML headings included. The ids are the rendered anchors', so
  a table of contents links with `#${id}`. A heading whose text has no slug (`## !!!`) has no id
  and is not listed.
- **Code blocks** render as `<pre><code class="language-js">`, without highlighting.

**HTML** files are parsed the way a browser parses them.

- **Documents and fragments.** A full document (a doctype, or an `<html>`, `<head>` or `<body>`
  tag) contributes the content of its `<body>`, plus the `<style>` elements and scripts of its
  `<head>`. The rest of the head (`<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`) is dropped. Anything else is a
  fragment and is used as it is. The root `index.html` and other HTML entries of Vite, and files in
  `public/`, are never components.
- **Styles.** A top-level `<style>` is scoped to the file's content, like a top-level block in a
  `.stsx` file, and `<style global>` is not scoped. A `<style>` nested inside an element scopes to
  that element's subtree, as in `.stsx`. A `<style>` inside `<template>` (a web component's shadow
  DOM) or `<svg>` is left as it is. `$name` references are not available: there is no JS scope.
- **Scripts.** `<script>` and `<script type="module">` run as client modules: bundled by Vite and
  loaded in the browser wherever the component renders, the way an island's module is. Inline
  scripts and `src` files are both bundled. A relative `src` is resolved against the HTML file.
  Classic scripts become modules too, so they are deferred and strict. Scripts with other types
  (`application/ld+json`, `importmap`) stay in the markup.
- **Templates.** A `<template>`'s content stays verbatim, unscoped. So does the content of
  `<noscript>`. Comments and the doctype are dropped.
- **Attributes** are kept as written, including inline handlers (`onclick="…"`) and names JSX
  cannot write (`@click`, `x-on:click.prevent`), which are passed through a spread.
- **Asset URLs.** Relative URLs in `<img src>` and `srcset`, `<source src>` and `srcset`,
  `<video src>` and `poster`, `<audio src>`, `<track src>`, and `<a href>` to a file (an extension
  other than `.html` or `.md`) are bundled. They resolve against the `.md` or `.html` file, as
  `import url from "./photo.jpg?url"` does in a `.stsx` module: Vite serves them in dev and
  fingerprints them in builds (`/assets/photo-[hash].jpg`, or a data URL under its inline limit).
  Markdown images and links render as these elements, so their relative URLs are bundled too.
  Absolute paths (`/logo.svg`, from `public/`), URLs with a scheme or a query, fragments (`#top`)
  and links to pages (`./about`, `./next.md`) are kept as written. A missing file fails the
  build.

Raw `<style>` in Markdown follows the same rules. Raw `<script>` in Markdown is an error, with
the file and line ([LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md)); scripts belong in `.html` imports.

**How scripts load.** When a file has scripts, its component also renders an empty island with
`client:load`. On a server-rendered page, the island loader imports the island's module, which
imports the scripts, so they run once per page however many times the component renders. In a
client render, the scripts load with the component's module. An edit to such a file reloads the
page in dev, since scripts such as `customElements.define` cannot run twice.

> **Status:** available in `lumiose dev` and builds, with HMR: an edit re-renders the content and
> hot-updates its CSS.

## API

| Import / option                                       | Gives                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumiose({ md: true })`                               | Enables `.md` imports                                 |
| `lumiose({ md: { frontmatter(data, { file }) {} } })` | Enables them, with a build-time frontmatter hook      |
| `lumiose({ html: true })`                             | Enables `.html` imports                               |
| `import Post, { frontmatter } from "./post.md"`       | `Post: () => JSX.Element`; `frontmatter: Frontmatter` |
| `import { headings } from "./post.md"`                | `ReadonlyArray<{ depth; text; id }>`, document order  |
| `declare module "*.md" { interface Frontmatter {} }`  | Declares the fields your hook guarantees              |
| `import Card from "./card.html"`                      | `Card: () => JSX.Element`                             |
| `import.meta.glob("./posts/*.md", { eager: true })`   | Every post's module (component and frontmatter)       |

The types come with `lumiose/env` (`"types": ["lumiose/env"]` in `tsconfig.json`).

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts: Markdown with validated frontmatter, and HTML imports
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import * as z from "zod";

const Post = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  date: z.coerce.date(),
  draft: z.boolean().default(false),
});

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumiose({ md: { frontmatter: (data) => Post.parse(data) }, html: true })],
});
```

```ts
// src/content.d.ts: the fields the hook guarantees, merged into lumiose/env's `Frontmatter`
declare module "*.md" {
  interface Frontmatter {
    title: string;
    date: Date;
    draft: boolean;
  }
}
```

```stsx
// src/routes/blog/index.stsx: a list of posts and the latest one, with its table of contents
import type { Frontmatter, Heading } from "*.md";

type Post = {
  default: () => JSX.Element;
  frontmatter: Frontmatter;
  headings: ReadonlyArray<Heading>;
};
// `import.meta.glob` is Vite's (types from `vite/client`).
const posts = Object.values(import.meta.glob<Post>("../../posts/*.md", { eager: true })).toSorted(
  (a, b) => b.frontmatter.date.getTime() - a.frontmatter.date.getTime(),
);

export default function Blog() {
  const { default: Latest, headings } = posts[0]!;
  return (
    <main>
      <ul>
        {posts.map((post) => (
          <li>{post.frontmatter.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <nav aria-label="On this page">
        {headings
          .filter((heading) => heading.depth === 2)
          .map((heading) => (
            <a href={`#${heading.id}`}>{heading.text}</a>
          ))}
      </nav>
      <article class="post">
        <Latest />
      </article>
      <style>
        .post :deep(h2) { margin-top: 2rem; }
      </style>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```html
<!-- src/components/user-card.html: a web component in one file -->
<template id="user-card">
  <style>
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  </style>
  <slot></slot>
</template>
<user-card>Ada Lovelace</user-card>
<script type="module">
  customElements.define(
    "user-card",
    class extends HTMLElement {
      connectedCallback() {
        const template = document.getElementById("user-card");
        this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" }).append(template.content.cloneNode(true));
      }
    },
  );
</script>
<style>
  user-card {
    margin-block: 1rem;
  }
</style>
```

The Markdown's elements belong to the post's component, so the route styles them with
`:deep()` under its own `.post` element. The web component's shadow styles stay in its template;
its light-DOM rule is scoped to the file.

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting the option.** `.md` and `.html` imports are off by default; without
  `lumiose({ md: true })` Vite tries to read the file as JavaScript.
- **Trusting frontmatter types without a check.** `frontmatter` has `unknown` values. Declare
  fields in `Frontmatter` (as above) only when the hook validates the data.
- **Styling Markdown from a scoped block without `:deep()`.** The rendered elements belong to the
  Markdown component. Use `:deep()`, a class on a wrapper plus `:deep()`, or a `<style>` in the
  `.md` file itself.
- **Targeting `body` or `html` from an HTML file's `<style>`.** Its top-level styles are scoped
  to the file's content (`LUM3005`: the selector matches no element). Use `<style global>`.
- **A `<script>` in Markdown.** It fails with [LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md). Move the markup
  and script to an `.html` file and import that, or render the Markdown next to an island.
- **Expecting a script per use.** A file's scripts run once per page, not once per rendered
  component. Query the elements they work on (`document.querySelectorAll`) or use a custom
  element, which runs its code for every instance.
- **Linking to a file that is not there.** A relative asset URL (`<img src="./photo.jpg">`) is an import:
  a typo or a missing file fails the build. Files meant to be served as they are belong in
  `public/`, with an absolute URL (`/downloads/app.zip`).
- **Relative links between pages.** A Markdown link to `./next-post` is kept as written, so it resolves
  against the page's URL, not the file's. Link to the route's URL instead (`/blog/next-post`).

## Related diagnostics

The generated component compiles like a `.stsx` file, so style diagnostics apply to its blocks,
for example [LUM3005](../errors/LUM3005.md) for a selector that matches nothing.
[LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md) reports a `<script>` in a Markdown file. A frontmatter
block that is not a mapping, or a hook that throws, fails the build with the file's name.

See also: [Styles](styles.md), [Islands](islands.md), [SVG imports](svg.md), [reference: `@lumiose/vite`](../reference/vite.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/head.md -->

# Head and document

> Set head content with `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` from any component. Lumiose renders `<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>` for you; `src/document.stsx` customizes them.

## Concept

**Head components.** `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` can be used in any component, layout or page.
There is no `meta` export: these components are the one way to set head content.

- `<Title>`: the deepest one wins, so a page overrides its layouts and the document.
- `<Meta name="…" content="…" />`: attributes as in HTML. Metas with the same `charset`, `name`,
  `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop` dedupe: the deepest one wins, and the previous value comes
  back when it is removed.
- `<Head>`: any other head elements (`<link>`, `<script>`). Elements already in `<head>` are not
  duplicated.

**On the server** they are collected while the shell renders and flushed into `<head>`. Inside a
streamed `<Suspense>` boundary they are too late (`LUM5004`). **In the browser** (islands, SPA)
they update `document.title` and `<head>` live, and are removed with their component.

**Document.** By default Lumiose renders the HTML document. `src/document.stsx` takes over
`<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>`: it receives `{ head, body }` and must render each once. It renders
like any component, so it can provide context to pages. `{props.head}` also carries the page's
stylesheets, preload hints and island loader. `{props.body}` is followed by the page's island records
and its streamed `<Suspense>` content, so the whole page stays inside `<body>` with either document.

**Head defaults.** The `<title>` and `<meta>` tags the document writes in its `<head>` are defaults,
the shallowest level of the head: a `<Title>` replaces the title, and a `<Meta>` replaces the tag
with the same `charset`, `name`, `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop`, where the document put it.
Each page gets one of each, in complete and streamed responses. The default document's `charset` and
`viewport` tags work the same way. The document renders on the server only, so after an SPA
navigation a default that a page replaced does not come back: defaults that SPA pages fall back to
belong in their outermost `spa` layout, as `<Title>`/`<Meta>`.

> **Status:** available on the server (`renderToStream`) and in the browser; the default and custom
> documents are rendered by the request handler.

## API

| API                     | Use                                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Title>{text}</Title>` | The document title; the deepest wins, over the document's `<title>`.                |
| `<Meta … />`            | A `<meta>` tag, keyed by `charset`, `name`, `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop`. |
| `<Head>…</Head>`        | Other head elements.                                                                |
| `DocumentProps`         | `{ head, body }`: props of `src/document.stsx`.                                     |

## Example

```stsx check file=document.stsx
// src/document.stsx: the title and description are defaults that pages replace
import type { DocumentProps } from "lumiose";

export default function Document(props: DocumentProps) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
        <title>A Lumiose site</title>
        <meta name="description" content="A Lumiose site" />
        {props.head}
      </head>
      <body>{props.body}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/about.tsx
// src/routes/about.tsx
import { Head, Meta, Title } from "lumiose";

export default function About() {
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>About us</Title>
      <Meta name="description" content="Who we are" />
      <Head>
        <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/about" />
      </Head>
      <h1>About us</h1>
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **A `meta` or `title` export.** There is none; render `<Title>` and `<Meta>`.
- **`<Title>` inside `<Suspense>`** on a server route: the head was already sent (`LUM5004`). Set
  it in the page body outside the boundary.
- **Rendering `props.head` or `props.body` twice** in `document.stsx`. Render each exactly once.
- **Writing `<title>` or `<meta>` elements directly in a page.** They land in the body. Use the
  components.
- **Setting `document.title` in an effect.** It fights with `<Title>`; use the component.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/compiler.md -->

# Compiler and diagnostics

> A Rust compiler (OXC and Lightning CSS) turns `.stsx` and `.tsx` into fine-grained client code or string-concatenating server code. Every rule it enforces has a stable `LUMxxxx` code with a docs page.

## Concept

**Pipeline.** For each `.stsx`/`.tsx` module the Vite plugin calls the compiler, which:

1. **scans** the file for `<style>` blocks and masks them (replaces them with spaces, keeping every
   offset), so the rest is valid TSX;
2. parses and analyses the TSX: components, props, compiled idioms, `await` sites, islands and
   `$name` references;
3. compiles the CSS (scoping by placement, `$name` substitution, constant math folding, targets,
   minification);
4. generates JS for the **client** (cloned templates, bindings, delegated events) or the **server**
   (string concatenation with escaping), with source maps. Types are stripped.

Vite's own JSX transform is disabled for Lumiose files, and `node_modules` is excluded.

**The masking invariant.** Masked TSX parses as valid TSX with identical offsets. Tools rely on it:
TypeScript type-checks _shadow files_ (`.lumiose/shadow/<path>.stsx.tsx`, the masked text), so
errors map back to the same line and column of the `.stsx`. `$name` references stay in place as
real TS expressions (`$radius.lg` becomes `{radius.lg}` inside JSX, `;radius.lg;` at top level), so
TypeScript checks them too.

**Scanner rules.**

- `<style` must be followed by whitespace or `>`; it is recognised wherever a JSX element can
  start. Inside JSX text, quotes (as in `Don't`) do not start strings.
- The only attribute is `global`; content runs to the first `</style>`.
- A `<style>` inside `<svg>` is native SVG CSS: emitted verbatim and unscoped.

**Diagnostics.** Every diagnostic has the shape
`{ code, severity, message, span, labels, help, fix?, docs }`. Codes are stable forever and never
reused; the compiler's registry is the source of truth, and the [error pages](../errors/README.md)
are generated from it. They appear in the Vite overlay, in `lumiose check`, in the editor and in
`--format json` output.

| Range | Area                                                                        |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1xxx  | File format: syntax, scanner, `<style>` blocks                              |
| 2xxx  | Reactivity: stale values, writes during render, early returns               |
| 3xxx  | Styles: placement, `$name` references, unused CSS                           |
| 4xxx  | Islands and boundaries: exports, serialization, server-only code, hydration |
| 5xxx  | Routing and server: route files, prerender, streaming                       |

**Tooling on top.** `lumiose check` (typegen, shadow files, `tsc --noEmit`, scanner and compiler
diagnostics), `lumiose lint` (oxlint on shadows, optional stylelint on blocks), `lumiose fmt` (oxfmt
plus each block's CSS), and the language server (a TypeScript LSP proxy plus CSS features in
blocks, the compiler's diagnostics as you type and each JSX expression's execution contract in
hovers) all share the one scanner. TypeScript plugins
are not used.

## API

| API                                   | Use                                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumiose check [--format json]`       | Type-check and report diagnostics; exit 1 on errors. |
| `lumiose explain <code>`              | Print a diagnostic's explanation.                    |
| `lumiose docs <topic>`                | Print or search these docs.                          |
| `@lumiose/vite`                       | The plugin that runs the compiler in Vite.           |
| `.lumiose/shadow/`, `.lumiose/types/` | Generated shadow TSX and route types (git-ignored).  |

## Example

```stsx check
// The masked view TypeScript sees: the block becomes spaces, `$pad` stays as `{pad}`.
export function Box() {
  const pad = "1rem";
  return (
    <div class="box">
      Content
      <style>
        .box { padding: $pad; }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```sh
$ lumiose check --format json
{ "command": "check", "ok": true, "diagnostics": [], "summary": { "errors": 0, "warnings": 0, "hints": 0, "files": 0 } }
$ lumiose explain LUM3010
```

## Common mistakes

- **Running bare `tsc` without shadow files.** `import "./X.stsx"` only resolves after shadows
  exist. Run `lumiose check` (or `lumiose typegen`), or keep the dev server or editor running.
- **A `tsconfig.json` that neither extends `.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json` nor sets `rootDirs`
  and `.lumiose/shadow`.** `lumiose check` reports the missing options (`LUM6001`); extend the
  generated file ([tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md#tsconfigjson)).
- **Importing `.stsx` across `src/` or from a workspace package with a standalone tsconfig.** Its
  `rootDirs` only pair `src`. Extend `.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json` instead
  ([tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md#imports-outside-src-and-stsx-from-other-packages)).
- **Ignoring a code because the message is short.** Run `lumiose explain <code>` for the cause and
  the fix.
- **Expecting TypeScript plugins.** Lumiose uses stock `tsc` and a language server; there is no TS
  plugin to configure.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1001](../errors/LUM1001.md): syntax error.
- [LUM1002](../errors/LUM1002.md): unsupported by this compiler version.
- [LUM1003](../errors/LUM1003.md): scanner ambiguity.
- [All diagnostics](../errors/README.md).

See also: [Styles](styles.md), [reference: CLI](../reference/cli.md).

<!-- source: concepts/testing.md -->

# Testing

> Test components with Vitest through the Lumiose Vite plugin: render into a DOM environment, interact, call `flush()`, assert. Test server rendering with `renderToString`.

## Concept

Vitest uses your Vite config, so `lumiose()` compiles `.stsx` and `.tsx` test subjects the same way
as the app. Two things matter for component tests:

- **A DOM environment.** Use `happy-dom` (or `jsdom`), per file with
  `// @vitest-environment happy-dom` or for all tests with `test.environment`.
- **The browser build of `lumiose`.** `lumiose` has a browser entry (signals, the DOM renderer) and a
  `node` entry (server rendering, where signals are plain values and effects never run). Vitest
  resolves Node conditions, but `lumiose()` gives tests in a DOM environment the browser entry of
  `lumiose`, so rendered components update. Tests without a DOM environment keep the `node` entry.

Updates are batched: after a write or an event outside a delegated handler, call `flush()`
before asserting. Delegated events (`onClick`) need the element to be attached to `document`.

Server rendering is tested with `renderToString(() => <Page />)` under the `node` entry: a test
file without a DOM environment, in the same project.

**Scoped state is fresh in each test.** `lumiose()` adds a Vitest setup file that resets
`defineState` instances before each test, so one test's cart never leaks into the next. In server
tests, a state's accessor called outside a render (to seed or inspect it) uses one instance per
test, which `renderToString` then shares.

> **Status:** `@lumiose/testing` (a `render()` helper and Testing Library integration) is planned.
> Until then, use `render` from `lumiose/dom` as shown here.

## API

| API                                                   | Use                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `render(() => <App />, container)` from `lumiose/dom` | Render into a DOM node; returns a disposer. |
| `flush()`                                             | Run pending bindings and effects now.       |
| `renderToString(() => <App />)`                       | Server-render to a string (node entry).     |

## Example

```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumiose()],
  test: { environment: "happy-dom" },
});
```

```tsx check file=Counter.test.tsx
// src/Counter.test.tsx
import { flush } from "lumiose";
import { render } from "lumiose/dom";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { Counter } from "./Counter.stsx";

it("counts clicks", () => {
  const container = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"));
  const dispose = render(() => <Counter start={2} />, container);

  const button = container.querySelector("button")!;
  button.click();
  flush();

  expect(button.textContent).toContain("Clicked 3 times");
  dispose();
  container.remove();
});
```

## Common mistakes

- **No DOM environment.** Without `happy-dom` (or `jsdom`) there is no `document`, and `lumiose`
  resolves to its `node` entry, which has no reactive graph: set the environment for component
  tests.
- **Asserting right after a write.** Effects and bindings run in a microtask; call `flush()`
  first.
- **Clicking a detached element.** Delegated handlers listen at `document`; append the container
  to `document.body`.
- **Not disposing.** Call the disposer returned by `render` so effects and listeners from one test
  do not leak into the next.
- **Testing server components in a DOM environment.** Async server components that use
  `request()`, `cookies()` or `*.server.ts` modules belong in server-side tests with
  `renderToString`.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph (also `renderToString` called with the browser entry).
- [LUM4004](../errors/LUM4004.md): browser API at module scope.

See also: [Getting started](../getting-started.md), [reference: `lumiose/dom`](../reference/dom.md), [reference: server](../reference/server.md).

<!-- source: concepts/security.md -->

# Security

> `lumiose({ csp: "strict" })` sends a strict Content Security Policy: a fresh nonce on every inline script and style Lumiose writes and on those you write in JSX, `cspNonce()` for markup you build yourself, and hashes for prerendered pages. Form actions are also checked against cross-site posts.

## Concept

**Strict Content Security Policy.** A strict CSP lets the browser run only the scripts and apply
only the styles the page meant to include, so injected markup cannot run code. With
`lumiose({ csp: "strict" })`:

- **Pages rendered per request** (`server` routes, `spa` routes that reach the server) get a new
  random nonce for each response. Every inline `<script>` and `<style>` Lumiose writes carries it:
  the page's stylesheets that are inlined (see [Styles](styles.md)), the island loader, the
  streamed `<Suspense>` swaps, the speculation rules, the View Transitions opt-in and module
  preloads. The response gets this header:

  ```
  Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'
  ```

  `'strict-dynamic'` lets the scripts the page loads import their own modules (islands, SPA
  routes). Stylesheets from your own origin are allowed; inline styles need the nonce. These
  responses also get `Cache-Control: private, no-store` unless the page sets its own: a nonce is
  only secret while no shared cache hands the same HTML to someone else.

- **Prerendered pages** (`static` routes, the shells of `spa` pages) are files that every visitor
  gets as they are, so a nonce would be the same for everyone. Each one gets the policy as
  `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">`, first in `<head>`, with the SHA-256 hash of each
  inline script and style that Lumiose or your JSX wrote (the same ones that get a nonce per
  request) and `'self'` for scripts and stylesheets of your origin. It works on any static host.
- **`style` props** render as rules of a nonce'd (or hashed) `<style>` that target a `data-l-v`
  attribute, instead of `style="…"` attributes, which a strict policy refuses. In the browser,
  styles are set through the CSSOM, which the policy allows.
- **Your own inline scripts and styles** written in JSX get the nonce automatically: a
  `<script innerHTML={…}>` in the document, a JSON-LD block, an SVG `<style>`. An explicit `nonce`
  prop wins. Strings rendered as text are escaped and never become elements, and raw HTML strings
  (`innerHTML` of another element) never get a nonce, nor a hash on prerendered pages: a script
  injected through such a string is blocked either way.
- **Static `style="…"` strings** (in JSX, and in `.md`/`.html` imports) are applied like `style`
  props: a nonce'd rule on the server, the CSSOM in the browser.
- **`cspNonce()`** returns the response's nonce during a server render (the document included) and
  in middleware, and `undefined` without strict CSP or while prerendering. Use it for markup you
  build yourself: a third-party snippet as a string, a custom `Content-Security-Policy` header, a
  script you create at runtime. In the browser it reads `<meta property="csp-nonce">`.
- **Your own policy wins.** A `Content-Security-Policy` header from `lumiose({ headers })` for the
  path, or one set with `response().setHeader()` or by middleware, replaces Lumiose's; with `headers`,
  the path's prerendered pages get no `<meta>` policy either. `lumiose dev` puts nonces on the page but sends no policy,
  because Vite injects styles of its own for hot updates.

Elements that the client creates later (a `<style>` inside an `<svg>` rendered after a client
navigation) take the nonce from `<meta property="csp-nonce">`. A prerendered page has no nonce,
so such an element is refused there unless it was in the prerendered HTML: put its rules in the
file's `<style>` block.

**Client navigation.** `navigate()` and the redirects of enhanced form actions only
follow `http:` and `https:` URLs (relative ones included); a `javascript:` or `data:` location
throws a `TypeError` instead of running in the page. Spread props drop lowercase `on*` keys
(`{...{ onclick: "…" }}`): an inline handler attribute is a script sink, so handlers are only
functions in `onClick`.

**Unsafe URLs.** A dynamic value for a URL attribute (`href`, `src`, `action`, `formaction`,
`xlink:href`, `poster`, `data`, …) whose scheme is `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:text/html`
renders as `about:blank#blocked`, on the server and in the browser, with a
[LUM4009](../errors/LUM4009.md) warning in development. Case, leading spaces and control
characters, and tabs or newlines inside the scheme do not get past it. String literals in your JSX
are left as written.

**Error details.** In production server rendering, `<ErrorBoundary>` fallbacks receive a generic
error with a short `digest`, and the original error is logged with the same digest
([ErrorBoundary](../reference/components.md#errorboundary)).

**Redirects.** `redirect()` accepts paths and `http(s)` URLs only; a `javascript:` or `data:`
location throws. For a user-supplied target (`?next=`), accept only same-origin paths, or the user
lands wherever a link sends them:

```ts
// A `next` parameter as a path of this site, else the fallback.
function safeNext(next: string | null, fallback = "/"): string {
  if (next === null || !next.startsWith("/") || next.startsWith("//") || next.startsWith("/\\")) {
    return fallback;
  }
  return next;
}
redirect(safeNext(url.searchParams.get("next")));
```

Trailing-slash redirects (`lumiose({ trailingSlash })`) always stay on your site, also for a
request path such as `//evil.com/`. `href()` refuses `.` and `..` as param values, which a browser
would resolve into another route.

**Files from elsewhere.** Icon sets, Markdown and HTML often come from outside the project. The
compiler treats them as untrusted input:

- **SVG imports** keep an allowlist of SVG elements and attributes: no scripts, handlers,
  `<foreignObject>` HTML, `javascript:` URLs or animations of links, and `<style>` text cannot
  open a tag ([SVG imports](svg.md)).
- **`$` constants** in style blocks cannot end their declaration or the `<style>` element
  ([LUM3021](../errors/LUM3021.md)), so data in a constant cannot add CSS outside its scope.
- **Frontmatter** keys such as `__proto__` stay plain data.
- **Depth limits** turn absurdly nested files into errors instead of crashes or stalls: CSS
  blocks past 64 levels and parentheses past 16 ([LUM3014](../errors/LUM3014.md)), SVG elements past 128,
  Markdown and HTML past 512 ([LUM1009](../errors/LUM1009.md)).

**Cross-site form posts.** Form actions and form-encoded posts to endpoints are checked against
the `Origin` header (on by default, `lumiose({ csrf })`); see [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).

**Request URLs.** `lumiose dev`, `lumiose preview` and `@lumiose/adapter-node` build each request's URL
from the server's origin (`ORIGIN`, else the socket's protocol and the `Host` header) plus the
request target's path, appended as is: a request for `//attacker.test/reset` stays on your origin
with that path, so `ctx.url`, `url()`, the cross-site check and `fetchJSON()`'s same-origin test
never see another host. Targets that are not a path (`http://other/x`, or `*` other than with
`OPTIONS`) and invalid `Host` headers get `400 Bad Request`. Behind a proxy that rewrites the
host, set `ORIGIN` (or the adapter's `origin`) so a client cannot choose the origin through `Host`.

**Request body limits.** Every request body is bounded (decision-29): URL-encoded forms, JSON and
other bodies at 1 MB, `multipart/form-data` (uploads) at 10 MB. A larger request gets `413 Payload
Too Large`, refused before reading when its `Content-Length` says so, else as soon as the bytes
read pass the limit; nothing buffers an unbounded body. The limits hold for form actions
(`ctx.formData()`), endpoints (`request.formData()`, `json()`, `text()`, `arrayBuffer()` read the
bounded body) and middleware alike, in every deployment. Raise or lower them for the app with
`lumiose({ limits: { body: "2mb", upload: "50mb" } })`, and for one route with
`export const limits = { upload: "200mb" }` in its page or endpoint file.

**Default response headers.** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (no MIME sniffing of uploads and
JSON) and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` (no full URLs to other sites) go on
every response; override them in `lumiose({ headers })`, or remove one with `""`.

**Server-only code** (`*.server.*` files, `src/server/`) never reaches the browser: imports from
client code fail `lumiose dev`/`lumiose build` (`LUM4003`), `lumiose dev` refuses to serve the files
(`server.fs.deny`), and only `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` variables reach client code (`envPrefix`).
See [Server](server.md).

**What the page sends.** Island props, values awaited inside islands and the scoped state islands
use (`defineState`) are serialized into the page as plain data (JSON in
`<script type="application/json">`, escaped so it cannot end the element): anyone who loads the
page can read them. Never pass a secret there; keep it in server-only modules.

**Secrets.** `signedCookie()` needs a secret of at least 32 bytes in production
(`LUMIOSE_SECRET`); a shorter one throws when the cookie is used (in development it warns).
`{ allowWeakSecret: true }` opts out.

**Compression.** `@lumiose/adapter-node` compresses responses; for pages that render a secret next
to reflected input, see BREACH in the [adapter reference](../reference/adapter-node.md).

## API

| Option / export                   | Meaning                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumiose({ csp: "strict" })`      | Nonces per response, the policy header, hash policies for prerendered pages |
| `cspNonce(): string \| undefined` | The response's nonce (from `lumiose`), for markup the app builds itself     |
| `<meta property="csp-nonce">`     | Written by Lumiose with the nonce; the client's preload helper reads it     |

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";

export default { plugins: [lumiose({ csp: "strict" })] };
```

```tsx
// src/document.tsx: an inline script that runs before the first paint
import type { DocumentProps } from "lumiose";

const THEME = `document.documentElement.dataset.theme = localStorage.getItem("theme") ?? "auto"`;

export default function Document(props: DocumentProps) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8" />
        <script innerHTML={THEME} />
        {props.head}
      </head>
      <body>{props.body}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

On a server-rendered page Lumiose gives the script the response's nonce; on a prerendered page the
page's policy lists the script's hash.

## Common mistakes

- **An inline script built as a string** (`<div innerHTML={'<script>…</script>'}>`, a snippet
  added at runtime). Lumiose only nonces elements written in JSX: the browser refuses it and logs a
  CSP violation. Write it as a JSX `<script>`, add `nonce={cspNonce()}` to the markup you build,
  or load the code as a module.
- **A `<style>` inside an `<svg>` that only the client renders, on a prerendered page.** No nonce
  exists there. Put the rules in the file's `<style>` block.
- **Expecting the policy in `lumiose dev`.** Dev sends none; check with `lumiose build` and
  `lumiose preview` or your server.
- **Adding `'unsafe-inline'` to make an error go away.** It disables the protection for every
  inline script. Find the element in the console message and give it the nonce instead.

## Related diagnostics

A CSP violation shows in the browser console, with the refused element. For files:
[LUM1009](../errors/LUM1009.md) (content nested too deeply), [LUM3014](../errors/LUM3014.md) (CSS
nested too deeply), [LUM3021](../errors/LUM3021.md) (a `$` constant that would break out of its
value).

See also: [Head and document](head.md), [Styles](styles.md), [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: `@lumiose/vite`](../reference/vite.md), [reference: app APIs](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: deploy/README.md -->

# Deploy

> Run a Lumiose build in production: what `lumiose build` writes, the settings a server needs, a guide per target, and what each guide was verified on.

## What to deploy

`lumiose build` writes `dist/` ([Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md)):

- `dist/client`: the browser assets (content-hashed, under `assets/`), the files of `public/`, and
  the prerendered pages, with `.br` and `.gz` copies of every text file of 1 kB or more.
- `dist/server/entry.js`: the request handler for server-rendered pages, endpoints and form
  actions. It bundles your server code and the Lumiose runtime; other npm packages stay imports,
  so production needs the app's `dependencies` installed.

A site whose every route is prerendered builds no `dist/server`: any static host serves
`dist/client`. Anything else runs on a server: `@lumiose/adapter-node` serves both directories with
Node, from the `server.ts` that `create-lumiose --template ssr` writes
([reference](../reference/adapter-node.md)).

## Production settings

The Node adapter and the request handler read these environment variables:

| Variable         | Set it to                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NODE_ENV`       | `production`. The adapter sets it when it is unset, before the build loads.                                                                                    |
| `PORT`           | The port to listen on. Default: `3000`.                                                                                                                         |
| `HOST`           | The address to listen on. Default: every address, which a container needs. Behind a proxy on the same machine, `127.0.0.1`.                                     |
| `ORIGIN`         | The public origin, such as `https://example.com`, behind a proxy that terminates TLS or rewrites the host. Request URLs (`url()`, `ctx.url`) are built from it. |
| `LUMIOSE_SECRET` | When the app signs cookies (`signedCookie()`): a random secret of at least 32 bytes (`openssl rand -base64 32`). Never commit it or bake it into an image.      |

## Guides

- [Docker](docker.md): A multi-stage Dockerfile: `node:24-alpine`, production dependencies only, a non-root user and a health check.
- [VPS](vps.md): The Node adapter under systemd or pm2, behind Caddy or nginx, and what the adapter already does for compression and caching.
- [Coolify](coolify.md): Deploy from the Dockerfile with Coolify's Dockerfile build pack.

## Verification

Each target's status says how far its guide has been checked:

- **Verified on the platform**: deployed to the real service by hand, on the date given.
- **Tested locally**: run on a development machine in the target's own runtime (a container, the
  platform's emulator), by the script named or by hand; not on the real service.
- **Not tested**: written from the platform's documentation only.
- **Planned**: no guide yet.

     also places it in the website's navigation and llms.txt), and a row below. -->

| Target                    | Guide                              | Status         | Checked    | What was checked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docker                    | [Docker](docker.md)                | Tested locally | 2026-10-12 | The Dockerfile on the page, on a `create-lumiose@0.2.0 --template ssr` project with packages from npm: builds, healthy, serves pages (brotli) and `immutable` assets, runs as `node`, stops in under a second. Docker 29.8, linux/arm64. The npm variant is not tested.                                                              |

| nginx                     | [VPS](vps.md#nginx)                | Tested locally | 2026-10-12 | The config on the page (nginx 1.31, a self-signed certificate in place of certbot's) in front of the bookshelf container: `nginx -t`, the same checks as Caddy (with `gzip on` too), and streaming with `proxy_buffering` on and off.                                                                                               |

<!-- source: deploy/docker.md -->

# Docker

> A multi-stage Dockerfile for a Lumiose app served by `@lumiose/adapter-node`: built with every dependency, run on `node:24-alpine` with production dependencies only, as a non-root user, with a health check.

This page is for an app with server routes and the `server.ts` that `create-lumiose --template ssr`
writes (`@lumiose/adapter-node`'s `createServer()`). The same image runs on any host that runs
containers: a [VPS](vps.md) with Docker, [Coolify](coolify.md), Kubernetes, a container platform.

## The Dockerfile

Put it at the root of the project, next to `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
ARG NODE_VERSION=24

# Build: all dependencies, then `lumiose build`. Debian (glibc): the compiler ships native
# binaries for Linux x64 and arm64 on glibc, and for x64 only on musl (Alpine).
FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-slim AS build
ENV PNPM_HOME=/pnpm CI=true
RUN npm install --global pnpm@11
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml* ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm,target=/pnpm/store pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
COPY . .
RUN pnpm build

# Production dependencies only, on the runtime's base image (native packages match its C library).
FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS prod-deps
ENV PNPM_HOME=/pnpm CI=true
RUN npm install --global pnpm@11
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml* ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm,target=/pnpm/store pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod

# Runtime: Node, the build output and production dependencies, as the unprivileged `node` user.
FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine
# tini passes `docker stop`'s SIGTERM on to Node, which ignores it as PID 1.
RUN apk add --no-cache tini
ENV NODE_ENV=production PORT=3000 HEALTHCHECK_PATH=/
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=prod-deps /app/node_modules node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/dist dist
COPY package.json server.ts ./
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=30s --start-interval=2s --retries=3 \
  CMD ["node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:' + process.env.PORT + process.env.HEALTHCHECK_PATH).then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
ENTRYPOINT ["/sbin/tini", "--"]
CMD ["node", "server.ts"]
```

And a `.dockerignore`, so the build context leaves out what the image builds itself:

```text
node_modules
dist
.lumiose
.git
.env*
*.log
```

Build and run it:

```sh
docker build -t my-app .
docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -e LUMIOSE_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" my-app
```

`LUMIOSE_SECRET` is only needed when the app signs cookies (`signedCookie()`); pass every secret
at run time like this, never as a build argument or an `ENV` line, which stay in the image. The
other settings (`ORIGIN` behind a proxy, `PORT`, `HOST`) are in
[Production settings](README.md#production-settings).

## How it works

- **Three stages.** `build` installs everything and runs `lumiose build`. `prod-deps` installs only
  `dependencies`, so Vite, the compiler and the CLI never reach the image. The last stage copies
  `dist/`, those `node_modules` and `server.ts` onto a fresh `node:24-alpine`. The server build
  bundles your server code and the Lumiose runtime; other npm packages stay imports, which is why
  production dependencies are installed.
- **Debian to build, Alpine to run.** `lumiose build` loads the compiler's native binary, published
  for Linux x64 and arm64 on glibc but only x64 on musl, so the build stage is `node:24-slim`,
  which builds on both architectures (an arm64 laptop or server included). The build output is
  JavaScript and static files, so it runs on Alpine. `prod-deps` uses the runtime's image so that a
  dependency with a native addon is built for musl.
- **Non-root.** The app runs as `node` (uid 1000), and the files it runs are owned by root, so it
  cannot change them. A directory it writes to, such as a SQLite database's, must be created for
  it before `USER node` and mounted as a volume:
  `RUN mkdir /data && chown node:node /data`, then `docker run -v my-app-data:/data …`.
- **Health check.** `HEALTHCHECK` fetches `HEALTHCHECK_PATH` (default `/`) with Node, since Alpine
  has no curl; any `2xx` answer is healthy. Point it at a cheap URL, such as a `GET` endpoint
  that returns `ok` without rendering a page: `docker run -e HEALTHCHECK_PATH=/healthz …`.
  `--start-interval` (Docker Engine 25 or later) checks every 2 s while the container starts.
- **Signals.** Node as PID 1 ignores `SIGTERM`, so `docker stop` would wait 10 s and kill it.
  [tini](https://github.com/krallin/tini) passes the signal on, and Node exits at once.
- **pnpm.** `npm install --global pnpm@11` installs pnpm; when `package.json` has a
  `packageManager` field (`pnpm@11.x.y`), pnpm switches to that version. The cache mounts keep
  the package store between builds. `pnpm-workspace.yaml*` copies the file when it exists
  (pnpm 11 keeps settings there).

**With npm** instead of pnpm: drop the `npm install --global pnpm@11` lines, the `PNPM_HOME`
variable and the cache mounts, copy `package-lock.json` instead of `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and run
`npm ci`, `npm run build` and `npm ci --omit=dev`. This variant has not been tested.

## The bookshelf sample

The repository's [bookshelf sample](https://github.com/itsjavi/lumiose/tree/main/examples/ssr-bookshelf)
has a Dockerfile of the same shape, built from the monorepo instead of from npm:

- The build context is the repository root (`docker build -f examples/ssr-bookshelf/Dockerfile .`).
  Its ignore file is `examples/ssr-bookshelf/Dockerfile.dockerignore`: BuildKit reads the ignore
  file named after the Dockerfile before the one at the context root. It allows only the
  workspace packages the sample uses.
- A first stage compiles the compiler's native binary from the Rust sources, because the
  monorepo has no Linux binaries (npm installs them as `@lumiose/compiler-linux-*`).
- pnpm installs with `--filter "@lumiose-examples/ssr-bookshelf..."`, and the production install
  with `--filter-prod`, which leaves out the workspace's dev dependencies.
- The build seeds a throwaway database, because the genre pages are prerendered from it. The
  container seeds `/data/bookshelf.db` on its first start, and the health check calls `/api/me`.

```sh
docker build -f examples/ssr-bookshelf/Dockerfile -t lumiose-bookshelf .
docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -e LUMIOSE_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \
  -v bookshelf-data:/data lumiose-bookshelf
```

`node examples/ssr-bookshelf/e2e/docker-smoke.ts` builds the image and checks a running container:
health, a server-rendered page compressed with brotli, a database query, prerendered pages, the
`immutable` caching of hashed assets and their precompressed copies, the `node` user, no dev
dependency in the image, and a prompt stop. It needs Docker, skips itself in CI, and is never run
by CI: a cold build compiles the Rust compiler (about 1 minute on an 8-core arm64 machine).

<!-- source: deploy/vps.md -->

# VPS

> Run a Lumiose app on your own server: `@lumiose/adapter-node` under systemd or pm2, with Caddy or nginx in front for TLS. The adapter already compresses responses and caches hashed assets, so the proxy needs no rules for either.

This page covers an app with server routes and the `server.ts` that `create-lumiose --template ssr`
writes. The examples call the app `my-app`, serve it as `example.com`, and keep it in
`/srv/my-app`. To run it in Docker on the server instead, see [Docker](docker.md).

## Build and install

The server needs Node 24 or later. Build where the dependencies are installed, on the server or
in CI:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
```

To ship production dependencies only, build in CI (or with the [Docker](docker.md) image's
`build` stage), copy `dist/`, `server.ts`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` (if any) to `/srv/my-app`, and run
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod` there. Then start it with `node server.ts`, which serves
`dist/` on `PORT` (3000).

## What the adapter already does

`createServer()` serves `dist/client` first, then the app ([`@lumiose/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md)):

- **Compression.** Static files are sent from the `.br` and `.gz` copies that `lumiose build`
  writes next to every text file of 1 kB or more (brotli 11, gzip 9), at no CPU cost per request.
  Pages and endpoints with a text content type are compressed as they stream: brotli quality 4,
  else gzip 6. Every compressible response gets `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.
- **Caching.** Content-hashed files under `assets/` (`loader-BzIcWyn5.js`) get
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; a new build changes their names. Every
  other file, prerendered pages included, gets `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` with an `ETag`
  and `Last-Modified`, answered with `304` when unchanged. Pages rendered per request send what
  the app sets (`response().setHeader("cache-control", …)`).
- **Headers.** `lumiose({ headers })` and the default `X-Content-Type-Options` and
  `Referrer-Policy` go on static files and pages alike.

So the proxy only adds TLS, HTTP/2 and connection limits. Proxy every request to Node: a proxy
that serves `dist/client` itself would have to repeat the caching rules and the headers above.
With compression on in both, the proxy leaves the already encoded responses alone; or pass
`compress: false` to `createServer()` and let the proxy compress.

## The process

### systemd

Create a system user that owns nothing it runs:

```sh
sudo useradd --system --home-dir /srv/my-app --shell /usr/sbin/nologin my-app
```

Put the secrets in `/etc/my-app.env`, one `KEY=value` per line, readable by root only
(`sudo chmod 600 /etc/my-app.env`):

