```sh
LUMIOSE_SECRET=paste-the-output-of-openssl-rand-base64-32
```

`/etc/systemd/system/my-app.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=my-app (Lumiose)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=my-app
Group=my-app
WorkingDirectory=/srv/my-app
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.ts
Environment=NODE_ENV=production HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=3000 ORIGIN=https://example.com
# Secrets as KEY=value lines (LUMIOSE_SECRET=…), readable by root only.
EnvironmentFile=/etc/my-app.env
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2
# The app can read /srv/my-app and write only its state directory, /var/lib/my-app.
StateDirectory=my-app
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```sh
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now my-app
journalctl -u my-app -f                # logs
sudo systemctl restart my-app          # after deploying a new build
```

Set `ExecStart` to the path `command -v node` prints. `HOST=127.0.0.1` keeps the app off the
public network: only the proxy reaches it. Point file databases and uploads at `/var/lib/my-app`
(the `StateDirectory`): with `ProtectSystem=strict`, it and a private `/tmp` are the only places
the app can write.

### pm2

`ecosystem.config.cjs`, next to `server.ts`:

```js
module.exports = {
  apps: [
    {
      name: "my-app",
      cwd: "/srv/my-app",
      script: "server.ts",
      // Node runs server.ts itself; pm2 6 would start .ts files with Bun.
      interpreter: "node",
      env: {
        NODE_ENV: "production",
        HOST: "127.0.0.1",
        PORT: "3000",
        ORIGIN: "https://example.com",
      },
    },
  ],
};
```

```sh
LUMIOSE_SECRET=… pm2 start ecosystem.config.cjs   # the app inherits this shell's variables
pm2 save && pm2 startup                           # restart it on boot
pm2 logs my-app
```

`pm2 save` writes the process list with its environment, the secret included, to
`~/.pm2/dump.pm2`, which `pm2 resurrect` (run at boot by the script `pm2 startup` installs)
restores. This runs one process (pm2's fork mode); pm2's cluster mode has not been tested with
Lumiose.

## The proxy

Set `ORIGIN` to the public origin (`https://example.com`), as in the configs above. The app
then builds request URLs (`url()`, `ctx.url`) with `https:` and your host, not the `http:` it
receives from the proxy. Without `ORIGIN`, the URL comes from the `Host` header, which the proxy
must pass through. The cross-site check of form posts compares the browser's `Origin` host with
that URL's host. Behind a proxy, the app's `clientAddress` is the proxy's: read
`X-Forwarded-For`, which both configs set, in middleware.

### Caddy

`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:

```caddy
example.com {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}
```

Caddy gets and renews the certificate, redirects HTTP to HTTPS, passes `Host` and sets
`X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto`. It flushes streamed responses as they arrive, so
`<Suspense>` chunks are not held back. It needs no `encode` directive: responses arrive
compressed.

### nginx

`/etc/nginx/sites-available/my-app` (linked into `sites-enabled`), with a certificate from
certbot:

```nginx
upstream my_app {
    server 127.0.0.1:3000;
    keepalive 16;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    listen [::]:80;
    server_name example.com;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    listen [::]:443 ssl;
    http2 on;
    server_name example.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

    # The app accepts uploads up to 10 MB (lumiose({ limits })); nginx's default is 1 MB.
    client_max_body_size 10m;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://my_app;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Connection "";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        # Send each streamed chunk (a <Suspense> boundary) to the browser as it arrives.
        proxy_buffering off;
    }
}
```

`proxy_set_header Host $host` matters: nginx sends the upstream's name (`my_app`) as `Host`
otherwise. `http2 on` needs nginx 1.25.1 or later; on older versions, write `listen 443 ssl http2`.
`proxy_http_version 1.1` with an empty `Connection` header reuses connections to Node
(`keepalive`). `client_max_body_size` should match the largest body the app accepts
([Security](../concepts/security.md)), or nginx answers `413` first.

<!-- source: deploy/coolify.md -->

# Coolify

> Deploy a Lumiose app to Coolify with the Dockerfile build pack: the Dockerfile from the Docker guide, the exposed port, a domain, `ORIGIN` and runtime-only secrets, the image's health check, and a volume for data.

[Coolify](https://coolify.io) builds the app's Dockerfile on your server and runs the image behind
its proxy, which terminates TLS for the domain. Lumiose needs nothing Coolify-specific: the image
is the one from [Docker](docker.md). The field names below follow Coolify v4's documentation; this
guide has not been run on a Coolify instance yet (see the [verification table](README.md#verification)).

## 1. Add the Dockerfile

Commit the [Dockerfile and `.dockerignore`](docker.md#the-dockerfile) at the root of the
repository. Check that it builds locally (`docker build -t my-app .`): Coolify runs the same build.

## 2. Create the application

In Coolify, **+ New**, pick the project and environment, connect the repository (a public URL, a
Git App or a deploy key) and choose the **Dockerfile** build pack. Then, under **General**:

| Field                   | Value                                                             |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Base Directory**      | `/`, the build context (the directory with `package.json`)        |
| **Dockerfile Location** | `/Dockerfile`, relative to the base directory                     |
| **Ports Exposes**       | `3000`, the image's `PORT`                                        |
| **Domains**             | `https://example.com`; Coolify's proxy gets the TLS certificate   |

Coolify sets `PORT` to the first exposed port and `HOST` to `0.0.0.0` when they are not set,
which is what `createServer()` reads.

## 3. Environment variables

Under **Environment Variables**:

| Variable         | Value                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ORIGIN`         | The domain, `https://example.com`. The proxy speaks plain HTTP to the container, so request URLs (`url()`) need it.        |
| `LUMIOSE_SECRET` | When the app signs cookies: `openssl rand -base64 32`. Set **Build time** to **Not available during build**.              |
| Your own secrets | Database URLs, API keys: also **Not available during build**, since only the running server reads them.                   |

New variables are available during the build by default; a secret that reaches the build can end
up in the image's layers. Restart or redeploy after changing them.

## 4. Health check

The image's `HEALTHCHECK` fetches `HEALTHCHECK_PATH` (`/` by default) inside the container. For a
Dockerfile application, Coolify uses an image's `HEALTHCHECK` instead of the one in its
**Healthcheck** settings, waits for the new container to be healthy before it replaces the old
one, and its default proxy (Traefik) stops routing to a container that turns unhealthy. To check a cheaper URL than the home
page, add a `GET` endpoint such as `/healthz` and set `HEALTHCHECK_PATH=/healthz` as a variable.
A health check configured in Coolify's dashboard instead runs `curl` or `wget` in the container;
Alpine has `wget`.

## 5. Persistent storage

Files the app writes at run time (a SQLite database, uploads) are lost when Coolify replaces the
container, unless they live on a volume. Create the directory for the `node` user in the
Dockerfile, before `USER node`:

```dockerfile
RUN mkdir /data && chown node:node /data
```

Then **Configuration**, **Persistent Storage**, **Add**, **Volume Mount**, with `/data` as the
**Destination Path**, and point the app at it (`DATABASE_PATH=/data/app.db`, or whatever your app
reads). Redeploy, and back the volume up outside the server.

## 6. Deploy

**Deploy**, then read the build log (the three Dockerfile stages) and the runtime logs (the
`Listening on …` line of `server.ts`). Pushes to the branch redeploy when automatic deployments
are on.

## A monorepo

Set **Base Directory** to the directory the Dockerfile's `COPY` lines are relative to, and
**Dockerfile Location** to the Dockerfile's path from there. The bookshelf sample, for example,
builds from the repository root with `/examples/ssr-bookshelf/Dockerfile`
([its notes](docker.md#the-bookshelf-sample)).

<!-- source: reference/reactivity.md -->

# `lumiose`: reactivity

> Signatures and behavior of the reactive core exported by `lumiose`: signals, computeds, effects, stores, owners, context, ids (`useId`), scoped state and in-flight state.

All of these are exported by `lumiose` in the browser and on the server. On the server (the `node`
entry) signals are plain cells, computeds evaluate once per request, and `effect`/`onMount` never
run. Concepts: [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md).

## signal

```ts
function signal<T>(value: T, options?: SignalOptions<T>): Signal<T>;

interface Signal<T> {
  (): T; // read (tracked)
  set(value: T): void;
  update(fn: (value: T) => T): void;
  peek(): T; // read without tracking
}
interface SignalOptions<T> {
  /** When a write counts as a change. Default Object.is; false: every write is a change. */
  equals?: false | ((a: T, b: T) => boolean);
}
```

## computed

```ts
function computed<T>(fn: (previous: T | undefined) => T, options?: SignalOptions<T>): Computed<T>;
type Computed<T> = () => T;
```

Lazy (runs on first read), cached, glitch-free. `fn` must be pure: no signal writes (`LUM2002`).
An unobserved computed unlinks itself from its sources.

## effect

```ts
function effect(fn: EffectFn): () => void;
type EffectFn = () => void | (() => void);
```

Runs `fn` after the DOM updates, then again whenever a signal it read changes. A returned function
is a cleanup, run before the next run and on disposal. Returns a disposer. Owned by the current
owner, so it is disposed with the component.

## onMount

```ts
function onMount(fn: EffectFn): void;
```

Runs `fn` once, untracked, after the current owner's DOM is mounted. It may return a cleanup.

## onCleanup

```ts
function onCleanup(fn: () => void): void;
```

Registers `fn` on the current owner: it runs when the owner is disposed (or, for an effect, before
its next run).

## getAbortSignal

```ts
function getAbortSignal(): AbortSignal;
```

An `AbortSignal` for the current owner. Aborted when the owner is disposed, when an effect re-runs,
or when an async component run is superseded. On the server it is the request's signal. Throws
outside an owner (with a message in development). Svelte has the same function.

## untrack

```ts
function untrack<T>(fn: () => T): T;
```

Runs `fn` without subscribing the current scope to the signals it reads.

## batch

```ts
function batch<T>(fn: () => T): T;
```

Defers dependents until `fn` returns, so they run once. Delegated event handlers are batched
automatically.

## flush

```ts
function flush(): void;
```

Runs pending computeds, DOM bindings and effects now, instead of in the next microtask.

## store

```ts
function store<T extends object>(value: T): T;
```

Wraps a plain object or array in a deep, **mutable** reactive proxy, like Valtio's `proxy`, Vue's
`reactive` or Solid's `createMutable`: you write to it directly (`state.count++`,
`state.items.push(item)`), with no setter. Reads track per property, writes notify only on change,
array methods work. Class instances, `Map`s, `Set`s and frozen objects are returned as is.

## snapshot

```ts
function snapshot<T>(value: T): T;
```

A deep plain copy of a store, of a value inside one (`snapshot(state.items)`), or of plain data
that holds stores. Plain objects and arrays are copied; other values (`Date`s, `Map`s, class
instances) are kept as they are, and shared or circular references stay shared. Use it where a
proxy does not work: `structuredClone()` and `postMessage()` (to a worker or an AudioWorklet)
throw on proxies, and a copy does not change when the store does (saving, undo history). Reads
are not tracked: in an effect, read the properties it should react to. On the server it copies the
plain object.

```ts
const song = store({ title: "Demo", rows: [] as number[][] });
worker.postMessage({ type: "song", song: snapshot(song) });
```

## reconcile

```ts
function reconcile<T extends object>(target: T, data: T, options?: ReconcileOptions): void;

interface ReconcileOptions {
  key?: string; // identifies array items, default "id"
}
```

Patches fresh `data` (a fetch result, a server payload) into a store, or into an object or array
inside one (`reconcile(state.books, fresh)`), in place, with Solid's `reconcile` semantics:

- Array items are matched by reference, or by `key` when the new item has it. Items without the
  key are merged into the item at the same index when that item has no key either; unmatched
  items are inserted as new values, and leftovers are removed. Keys should be unique: new items
  that share a key end up as the same store item.
- Matched objects are merged deeply; an object whose `key` differs from the old one is replaced.
- Keys missing from `data` are deleted. Primitives and other values (`Date`s, `Map`s, class
  instances) are replaced.

Unchanged items keep their identity, so keyed list rows, their DOM and their local state survive,
and only properties whose value changed notify, all in one batch. Reads are not tracked, so it is
safe in an effect. `target` and `data` must be the same kind (both arrays or both plain objects),
otherwise it throws a `TypeError` in development. Pass the store, not plain data: a plain object is patched
without notifying anything (that is what happens on the server, where stores are plain objects).

```ts
const books = store<Book[]>([]);
reconcile(books, (await (await fetch("/api/books")).json()) as Book[]);

const page = store({ rows: [{ slug: "intro", views: 1 }] });
reconcile(page.rows, [{ slug: "intro", views: 2 }], { key: "slug" });
```

## createContext, useContext

```ts
function createContext<T>(defaultValue: T): Context<T>;
function createContext<T>(): Context<T | undefined>;
function useContext<T>(context: Context<T>): T;
interface Context<T> {
  (props: { value: T; children?: JSX.Element }): JSX.Element; // the provider component
  readonly id: symbol;
  readonly defaultValue: T;
}
```

A context is also its provider component, as in React 19 and Solid 2: `<Theme value="dark">…</Theme>`
provides `value` to everything rendered inside it, including content rendered later (conditionals,
lists). `useContext` returns the value of the nearest provider above, or the default. A nested
provider of the same context shadows the outer one for its subtree. Context survives `await` in
async components. Islands start a new root ([LUM4010](../errors/LUM4010.md)).

The provider reads `value` once, when it renders, like Solid's provider and like every component
prop read in a component body: components run once. To share state that changes, provide a signal,
a store or an object with getters, and read it where it is used.

```tsx
const Theme = createContext("light");
const Count = createContext(signal(0));

<Theme value="dark">
  <Count value={signal(5)}>
    <Toolbar /> {/* useContext(Theme) is "dark"; useContext(Count)() is reactive */}
  </Count>
</Theme>;
```

## useId

```ts
function useId(): string;
```

Returns an id that is unique in the page, for `id`/`for`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`,
`aria-controls` and the like. Call it in a component's setup, once per id you need; each call returns
the instance's next id. The id is a valid HTML id and CSS identifier (`l0-0-1-0`, `ls3`, `lc7`), so
it also works in selectors and as a `view-transition-name`. Do not parse it: the format may change.

- **Server and hydration.** Inside an island (and an SPA, which is one), the server builds the id
  from the island's id and the component instance's position in it, and hydration computes the same
  id, so the server's `for`/`id` pairs stay as they are. Outside islands, server ids follow the
  render tree, so the same page renders the same ids whatever order its async content resolves in.
- **Browser only.** Content rendered in the browser after hydration, or by
  [`render()`](dom.md#render), gets ids from a counter.
- **Several apps on one page.** Give each a prefix: `render(code, container, { idPrefix: "cart-" })`,
  or `renderToStream(root, { idPrefix })` on the server, which the page's islands reuse when they
  hydrate. Ids then start with the prefix.
- **Async components.** Each run of an async component runs its body again, so a re-run after a
  signal it read changed gets new ids, as its other locals are new too.

```tsx check
import { useId } from "lumiose";

export function EmailField(props: { label: string; hint: string }) {
  const id = useId();
  const hintId = useId();
  return (
    <p>
      <label for={id}>{props.label}</label>
      <input id={id} type="email" aria-describedby={hintId} />
      <small id={hintId}>{props.hint}</small>
    </p>
  );
}

export function SignUp() {
  const title = useId();
  return (
    <form aria-labelledby={title}>
      <h2 id={title}>Sign up</h2>
      <EmailField label="Email" hint="We never share it." />
      <EmailField label="Backup email" hint="Optional." />
    </form>
  );
}
```

## defineState

```ts
function defineState<T>(factory: () => T): () => T;
```

Scoped state: returns an accessor whose `factory` runs on the first call, once per scope, and
returns the same instance after that.

| Scope          | One instance per                                                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Browser        | page: shared by every island and the SPA tree                                          |
| Server         | request: middleware, endpoints, actions and the render share it; never across requests |
| Tests (Vitest) | test: `@lumiose/vite` resets scoped state before each test                             |

The factory runs outside the component tree: it sees no context and its reads are not tracked; in
the browser its effects live as long as the page. On the server it may read request APIs
(`cookies()`, `locals()`, …), which do not exist in the browser: guard them with
[`isServer`](#isserver). Calling an accessor on the server outside a request or render (at module
scope) throws.

**Sent to the browser.** When islands or SPA routes import the state, a page that created it
sends what the factory returned that the browser cannot rebuild: the returned signal or store
itself, or the top-level signals and stores of the returned object. Computeds and functions are
not sent; the factory runs again in the browser and the server values replace its signals and
stores before any island reads them, so hydration matches. Values go once per page, in the chunk
(shell or streamed boundary) where the state was first used, and must be plain data like island
props ([LUM4011](../errors/LUM4011.md)). States that only server code imports are never sent.
Everything a sent state holds is public: never put secrets in it.

Define states at module scope with `export const x = defineState(…)` (or export the binding):
`@lumiose/vite` names each one after its module and export, the way it names islands. States
created elsewhere (inside a function) are never sent.

```ts
import { computed, cookies, defineState, isServer, signal } from "lumiose";

export const prefs = defineState(() => {
  const theme = signal(isServer ? (cookies().get("theme") ?? "light") : "light");
  return { theme, dark: computed(() => theme() === "dark") };
});
// prefs().theme(), prefs().dark(), prefs().theme.set("dark")
```

## isServer

```ts
const isServer: boolean;
```

`true` in the server entry of `lumiose` (the `node` condition), `false` in the browser entry
(Solid's name). Use it to guard code that runs on both sides, such as a `defineState` factory that
reads request APIs: `signal(isServer ? locals().user : null)`. The guard stays explicit: request
APIs called in the browser still throw [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md).

It is a constant, so production client builds fold it: `if (isServer) { … }` and
`isServer ? a : b` lose their server branch, and server-only strings in it never reach the
bundle. The server branch must still type-check and import only what client code may import;
server-only modules stay out of client graphs ([LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md)).

## isPending

```ts
function isPending(): boolean;
```

Inside an async component (its body or its UI): whether a **re-run** is in flight. The first load is
not a re-run (`<Suspense>` covers it). Reading it in the body does not re-run the component.
Always `false` on the server.

## isBusy

```ts
function isBusy(): boolean;
```

App-wide: whether anything is in flight: an async component run, a `<Suspense>` showing its
fallback, a form submission (`submit()`), an SPA navigation or a request of the async cache
(`fetchJSON`, `query`), background refetches included. Reactive. Always `false` on the
server.

## resource

```ts
function resource<T>(fetcher: (signal: AbortSignal) => T | PromiseLike<T>): Resource<T>;

interface Resource<T> {
  (): T | undefined; // latest value, tracked
  loading(): boolean;
  error(): unknown;
  refetch(): void; // aborts a load in flight and loads again
}
```

Low-level on-demand loading. `fetcher` runs now and whenever a signal it read synchronously
changes; its `AbortSignal` aborts when superseded or disposed. The first load counts as pending
for the nearest `<Suspense>`. Errors are not thrown: read `error()`. Browser only: on the server it
stays loading. Prefer [async components](../concepts/async.md).

## optimistic

```ts
function optimistic<T>(source: () => T): Optimistic<T>;

interface Optimistic<T> {
  (): T; // source() with the pending overlays applied in order, tracked
  set(value: T, promise: PromiseLike<unknown>): void;
  update(fn: (value: T) => T, promise: PromiseLike<unknown>): void;
}
```

A value that follows `source` (a getter such as `() => props.likes`, or a signal), plus overlays
held while their promises are pending. Each `set`/`update` applies at once and drops when its own
promise settles, either way: on success the (refreshed) source shows, on failure the value rolls
back. Concurrent overlays apply in call order over the latest source value, so an `update` is
re-applied when the source changes. A rejection is not re-thrown; await the promise itself to
handle it. Writes stop when the owner is disposed. On the server it reads `source()` and `set`/`update`
do nothing. See [optimistic updates](../concepts/data-and-actions.md) in Data and actions.

## Example

```tsx check
import { batch, effect, getAbortSignal, onCleanup, resource, signal, untrack } from "lumiose";

export function Clock() {
  const now = signal(new Date());
  const timer = setInterval(() => now.set(new Date()), 1000);
  onCleanup(() => clearInterval(timer));

  const first = signal("Ada");
  const last = signal("Lovelace");
  const rename = () =>
    batch(() => {
      first.set("Grace");
      last.set("Hopper");
    });

  effect(() => {
    console.log(`${first()} ${last()} at`, untrack(now).toISOString());
  });

  const user = resource((signal) =>
    fetch(`/api/users/${first()}`, { signal }).then((res) => res.json() as Promise<{ id: string }>),
  );

  return (
    <p onClick={rename}>
      {now().toLocaleTimeString()} · {user.loading() ? "…" : user()?.id}
      {String(getAbortSignal().aborted)}
    </p>
  );
}
```

<!-- source: reference/components.md -->

# `lumiose`: components

> Signatures and behavior of the built-in components and element helpers exported by `lumiose`: `Suspense`, `ErrorBoundary`, `Portal`, `Dynamic`, `ref`, `Head`, `Title` and `Meta`.

All are exported by `lumiose` in the browser and on the server. Concepts:
[Components](../concepts/components.md), [Async components](../concepts/async.md),
[Head and document](../concepts/head.md).

## Suspense

```ts
function Suspense(props: SuspenseProps): JSX.Element;
interface SuspenseProps {
  /** Shown while new content below is pending. */
  fallback?: JSX.Element;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}
```

Shows `fallback` while **new** async content below it is pending: the first load, and async
components or resources that a branch mounts later. Re-runs of revealed content keep their stale UI
(`isPending()` tells them apart). Hidden content stays alive. A shown fallback counts for `isBusy()`.
On the server, a boundary marks content that streams after the shell; with prerendering it is
resolved inline.

## ErrorBoundary

```ts
function ErrorBoundary(props: ErrorBoundaryProps): JSX.Element;
interface ErrorBoundaryProps {
  /** Rendered instead of the children after an error. */
  fallback?: JSX.Element | ((error: unknown, reset: () => void) => JSX.Element);
  children?: JSX.Element;
}
```

Renders `fallback` when its children throw while rendering, an effect below throws, or an async
component below rejects. `reset()` disposes the fallback and renders the children again. On the
server, an error in a streamed boundary renders the nearest `ErrorBoundary` in place.

In production server rendering, a fallback receives a generic `Error` with a short `digest`
(`An error occurred while rendering this part of the page (digest 1a2b3c4d).`) instead of an
error that is not an `HttpError`, which could reveal a database message or a file path. The
original error goes to the server log (the request handler's `onError`) with the same `digest`
property, so a user's report can be matched to the log entry. `HttpError`s (`notFound()`,
`error(403, …)`) reach the fallback as they are, development keeps the raw error, and boundaries
that catch in the browser get the error itself (decision-29).

## Portal

```ts
function Portal(props: PortalProps): JSX.Element;
interface PortalProps {
  /** Where the content goes. Default: document.body. */
  mount?: Node;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}
```

Renders `children` into a `<div>` appended to `mount`, removed with the owner. Delegated events
from the portal's content continue at the portal's position in the component tree.

## Dynamic

```ts
function Dynamic(props: DynamicProps): JSX.Element;
interface DynamicProps {
  /** A component or an intrinsic tag name. Nothing renders while it is nullish or false. */
  component: Component | string | null | undefined | false;
  [prop: string]: unknown;
}
```

Renders `component` with the other props, re-creating it only when `component` changes.

## ref

```ts
function ref<T extends Element>(): JSX.Ref<T>;
```

A callback for the `ref` prop that can also be read like a signal: `input()` is `undefined` until
the element exists. Pass it as `ref={input}`.

## Title

```ts
function Title(props: { children?: JSX.Element }): JSX.Element;
```

Sets the document title. The deepest `<Title>` wins, so a page overrides its layouts. It replaces
the `<title>` that `src/document.stsx` writes in `<head>`.

## Meta

```ts
function Meta(props: Record<string, unknown>): JSX.Element;
```

Adds or updates a `<meta>` in `<head>`, with the given attributes. Metas with the same `charset`,
`name`, `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop` dedupe: the deepest wins, and the previous one comes
back when it is removed. A `<Meta>` replaces the `<meta>` with the same key that the document writes
in `<head>` (`src/document.stsx`, or the default document's `charset` and `viewport`).

## Head

```ts
function Head(props: { children?: JSX.Element }): JSX.Element;
```

Appends its children to `<head>` and removes them on disposal. Elements equal to one already in
`<head>` (for example rendered by the server) are skipped.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Dynamic, ErrorBoundary, Portal, Suspense, ref, signal } from "lumiose";

function Info() {
  return <p>Info</p>;
}

export function Dialog() {
  const open = signal(false);
  const kind = signal<"h2" | "h3">("h2");
  const button = ref<HTMLButtonElement>();

  return (
    <ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => <button onClick={reset}>{String(error)}</button>}>
      <button ref={button} onClick={() => open.set(true)}>
        Open
      </button>
      {open() && (
        <Portal>
          <div role="dialog">
            <Dynamic component={kind()}>Title</Dynamic>
            <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
              <Dynamic component={Info} />
            </Suspense>
            <button onClick={() => (open.set(false), button()?.focus())}>Close</button>
          </div>
        </Portal>
      )}
    </ErrorBoundary>
  );
}
```

<!-- source: reference/app.md -->

# `lumiose`: app layer

> Signatures of the app-layer exports of `lumiose`: data fetching, form actions, routing helpers, control flow, request APIs, cookies, env and the request-context types.

`lumiose` exposes the same names in the browser and on the server. Server-only APIs exist in the
browser build as stubs that throw `LUM4003` with a hint; browser-only APIs reject on the server.
Concepts: [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md), [Server](../concepts/server.md),
[Routing](../concepts/routing.md).

## Data

### fetchJSON

```ts
function fetchJSON<T = unknown>(input: string | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T>;
```

Fetches and parses JSON (`Accept: application/json` unless `init` sets it); an empty body is
`undefined`. Non-2xx responses throw a `FetchError`. During SSR, same-origin URLs are served
in-process through the request handler, with the page request's cookies and headers. Returns plain
data, so awaited results stay serializable in islands.

Awaited in an async component, a GET is **cached by its absolute URL** (see [query](#query) for the
cache's behaviour): components awaiting the same URL share one request. The first caller's `init`
(headers, credentials) makes the request. Inside an async component the signal defaults to
`getAbortSignal()`: a superseded run stops waiting, and the request is cancelled once no component
waits for it. Elsewhere (event handlers, middleware, endpoints, actions) and for other methods it is
a plain request.

`fetchJSON(url, { cache: "no-store" })` opts a component-level GET out of the cache: a plain
request, not deduped with other components, not kept, and not sent with the page payload (inside an
island, its value is still recorded for hydration like any other await). Other `cache` values keep
the default behaviour; `init` always reaches `fetch` as given.

### query

```ts
function query<T, const TKey extends readonly unknown[]>(
  key: TKey,
  fn: (context: QueryFunctionContext<TKey>) => T | PromiseLike<T>,
): Promise<T>;

interface QueryFunctionContext<TKey extends readonly unknown[] = readonly unknown[]> {
  signal: AbortSignal; // the shared request's signal
  queryKey: TKey; // `key`
}
```

Awaited in an async component, caches what `fn` resolves to under `key`, an array of
JSON-serializable values hashed stably (object key order does not matter), as TanStack Query's
`queryKey`. Use it for data that does not come from `fetchJSON`: a database call in a server
component, a third-party SDK. `fn` receives `{ signal, queryKey }`, TanStack Query's
`QueryFunctionContext`: `fn` runs outside the component, so `signal` is the shared request's
(the same one `getAbortSignal()` returns inside `fn`), aborted once no component waits for it.
Pass it on to `fetch` or an SDK: `query(["user", id], ({ signal }) => sdk.getUser(id, { signal }))`.
Outside an async component it calls `fn` without caching, with the current owner's signal (one that
never aborts when there is no owner).

The cache behind `fetchJSON` and `query`:

- **Scope:** one per request on the server; one per page in the browser, shared by every island and
  the SPA tree and kept across client navigations.
- **Deduplication:** components awaiting the same entry share one request.
- **Stale-while-revalidate:** in the browser, an entry with data returns it at once (a new
  component shows it without a `<Suspense>` fallback) and refetches in the background; when the
  data changed, the components that awaited it re-run. Defaults follow TanStack Query: `staleTime`
  0, `gcTime` 5 minutes after the last component that awaited it is gone.
- **Invalidation:** [`invalidate(target)`](#invalidate) re-runs only the components that awaited the
  matching entries; their re-runs wait for the refetch, keeping their UI meanwhile.
- **Islands:** entries awaited inside an island (or an SPA page) during SSR are sent once with the
  page, so the browser cache starts with them and islands hydrate without fetching. Their values
  must be plain data (`LUM4007`); entries only server components awaited are never sent.
- **Errors** are never cached: the next await fetches again. A failed background refetch keeps the
  old data.
- Cached data is shared, not copied: treat it as read-only.

### FetchError, isFetchError

```ts
interface FetchError extends HttpError {
  readonly status: number; // 0 for network failures
  readonly url: string;
  /** Parsed JSON body for JSON responses, else text; undefined when empty. */
  readonly data: unknown;
}
function isFetchError(value: unknown): value is FetchError;
```

Thrown by `fetchJSON()` and by `submit()` for unexpected errors. An `HttpError`, so if a server
component lets it escape, the page renders `_error` (or `_404`) with the same status.

## Form actions

### submit

```ts
function submit(target: SubmitTarget, options?: SubmitOptions): Promise<ActionResult>;
// Typed by the action it posts to: submit<typeof actions.save>(event)
function submit<A extends ActionsExport>(
  target: SubmitTarget,
  options?: SubmitOptions,
): Promise<ActionResult<ActionSuccessData<A>, ActionFailureData<A>>>;

type SubmitTarget =
  | HTMLFormElement
  | Event // a submit event: onSubmit={submit}
  | FormData
  | URLSearchParams
  | Record<string, string | Blob | readonly (string | Blob)[]>;

interface SubmitOptions {
  /** A URL, or "?/name" for a named action. Default: the submitter's formaction, else the
   *  form's action, else the current URL. */
  action?: string;
  /** Default POST. A form must say method="post". */
  method?: string;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** After a success: true (default) refreshes the whole page with invalidate() on client-routed
   *  (SPA) pages, false keeps the page, and a list of targets (URLs, query() keys) refetches only
   *  those, on SPA and MPA pages. MPA pages never refresh as a whole on their own. */
  invalidate?: boolean | readonly (string | readonly unknown[])[];
}

type ActionResult<Data = unknown, Failure = unknown> =
  | { type: "success"; status: number; data: Data }
  | { type: "failure"; status: number; data: Failure }
  | { type: "redirect"; status: number; location: string };
```

Posts without a page load. `success` and `failure` set `actionData()`; `redirect` navigates.
On client-routed (SPA) pages, after a `success`, `submit()` runs [`invalidate()`](#invalidate) and
resolves once the page's data is fresh (decision-20); `{ invalidate: false }` skips it, and
`{ invalidate: ["/api/books/1", ["stats"]] }` refetches only those targets instead, on SPA and MPA
pages alike. On MPA pages it never reloads: the island updates itself from the result, refetches
targets, or calls `invalidate()` explicitly.
Failures, redirects and errors do not invalidate. Rejects only for unexpected errors (the action throws, an error response, a network
failure) with a `FetchError`, and with a `TypeError` for a redirect to a URL that is not `http(s)`
(a `javascript:` location never runs). Browser only: rejects on the server.

### isSubmitting

```ts
function isSubmitting(name?: string): boolean;
```

Whether a `submit()` is in flight; with a name, one to that named action (`?/name`). Reactive.
`false` on the server.

### actionData

```ts
function actionData(): unknown;
// Typed by the page's actions: actionData<typeof actions>() or actionData<typeof action>()
function actionData<A extends ActionsExport>(): ActionData<A> | undefined;
type ActionData<A extends ActionsExport> =
  | ActionSuccessData<A> // what the actions return (not fail() or a Response); void → undefined
  | ActionFailureData<A>; // the data they pass to fail()
// typeof action, typeof actions or typeof actions.name
type ActionsExport =
  | ((ctx: never) => unknown)
  | { readonly [name: string]: (ctx: never) => unknown };
```

The data of the last action result: what the action returned, or its `fail()` data. The type
argument is the actions export itself, never a data type: the result types are inferred from it.
`ActionData<typeof actions>` names the same type, for the props of a component that receives it
(`failed: ActionData<typeof action> | undefined`). Success and failure data are told apart by
their shape, as with React Router's `useActionData` and SvelteKit's `form`. Reactive in
the browser; after a no-JS form post it starts with the data the page was rendered with. On the
server: the current request's action result while the page re-renders after a post.

### fail, ActionFailure

```ts
function fail(status: number): ActionFailure<undefined>;
function fail<Data>(status: number, data: Data): ActionFailure<Data>;
```

A failed action result, usually for validation errors: `return fail(400, { errors })`. Without
JavaScript the page re-renders with `status`; `submit()` resolves with `{ type: "failure" }`.

### invalidate

```ts
function invalidate(...targets: (string | readonly unknown[])[]): Promise<void>;
```

With targets, refetches only the matching [cache](#query) entries and re-runs the async components
that awaited them, on SPA and MPA pages alike; their UI stays until the new data arrives. A string
is a URL (resolved against the page) and matches the `fetchJSON()` entry of that exact URL; an
array matches the `query()` entries whose key starts with it, as TanStack Query's
`invalidateQueries`: `invalidate(["books"])` matches `["books"]`, `["books", 1]` and
`["books", { page: 2 }]`. In development, a string that does not look like a URL (`/…`, `./…`,
`../…`, `http(s):…`) logs a warning: `invalidate("stats")` was probably meant as
`invalidate(["stats"])`.

Without targets, refreshes the whole page after a mutation: re-runs the page's async components in
SPA routes, refetching every cache entry (their UI stays until the new data arrives), and reloads
the page otherwise (that promise never settles, as the page is going away). A successful `submit()`
calls it for you on SPA pages only; on MPA pages call it yourself when the page needs fresh server
HTML.

Resolves once nothing is in flight anymore (`isBusy()` is false). Browser only: rejects on the
server.

## Routing

### href

```ts
function href<P extends Routes>(pattern: P, ...args: HrefArgs<P>): string;
```

Builds a path from a route pattern, encoding each param; `params` is required when the pattern has
params. A `[...rest]` param keeps its `/` separators and may be empty. Throws on a missing or empty
`[param]`.

The path is below Vite's `base` and follows `lumiose({ trailingSlash })`, on the server and in the
browser alike (`lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and prerendering):

| `base`  | `trailingSlash` | `href("/")` | `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug: "a" })` | `href("/feed.xml")` |
| ------- | --------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `/`     | `"ignore"`      | `/`         | `/blog/a`                             | `/feed.xml`         |
| `/sub/` | `"never"`       | `/sub/`     | `/sub/blog/a`                         | `/sub/feed.xml`     |
| `/sub/` | `"always"`      | `/sub/`     | `/sub/blog/a/`                        | `/sub/feed.xml`     |

With `"always"`, a pattern whose last segment has a dot (an endpoint such as `/feed.xml`) gets no
trailing slash. A relative `base` (`./`) counts as `/`. Outside Vite (plain Node) the path is
root-relative.

### Route types

```ts
interface RouteMap {}                  // augmented by .lumiose/types/routes.d.ts (typegen)
interface LayoutMap {}                 // the same, for layouts (by the URL scope of their folder)
type Routes = /* every route pattern, or string before typegen */;
type RouteParams<P extends Routes>;    // { slug: string } for "/blog/[slug]"
interface PageProps<P extends /* a page pattern */> { params: RouteParams<P> }
interface LayoutProps<P extends /* a layout pattern */> {
  params: /* the params of the layout's scope */;
  children: JSX.Element;
}
```

## Control flow

```ts
function redirect(location: string | URL, status?: 301 | 302 | 303 | 307 | 308): never;
function notFound(message?: string): never;
function error(status: number, message?: string): never; // 400-599
function isRedirect(value: unknown): value is Redirect;
function isHttpError(value: unknown): value is HttpError;
```

They throw; the framework renders a redirect, the nearest `_404` (404) or the nearest `_error`.
Without a status, `redirect()` uses 302 for GET/HEAD and 303 otherwise. `HttpError` is an `Error`
with a `status`.

## Request APIs (server)

```ts
function request(): Request;
function url(): URL;
function params<P extends Routes = never>(): RouteParams<P>; // Record<string, string> without P
function route(): Routes | undefined; // the matched pattern, "/blog/[slug]"; undefined if none
function locals(): Locals;
function cookies(): Cookies;
function response(): ResponseContext;
function env(name: string): string | undefined;
function publicEnv(source?: ServerEnv): Record<string, string>;
function cspNonce(): string | undefined; // lumiose({ csp: "strict" }): the response's nonce
```

`cspNonce()` is `undefined` without strict CSP, outside a request and while prerendering (the
page's hash policy covers its inline elements); in the browser it reads
`<meta property="csp-nonce">`. See [Security](../concepts/security.md).

Available anywhere during a server render (also after `await`), scoped to the current request. In
the browser they throw `LUM4003`. `url()`, `params()` and `route()` also exist in
[`lumiose/router`](router.md): those are reactive, follow client navigations and also work during
server rendering, so use them in code that runs in the browser (SPA routes, islands). `env()` reads the adapter's env, else `process.env`;
`publicEnv()` returns the `PUBLIC_*` subset.

```ts
interface ResponseContext {
  readonly status: number;
  setStatus(status: number): void;
  getHeader(name: string): string | null;
  setHeader(name: string, value: string): void;
}
```

Writable until the shell is sent; later writes throw `LUM5004`.

## Cookies

```ts
interface Cookies {
  get(name: string): string | undefined;
  getAll(): Array<{ name: string; value: string }>;
  set(name: string, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): void;
  delete(name: string, options?: CookieDeleteOptions): void;
}
interface CookieOptions {
  path?: string; // default "/"
  domain?: string;
  maxAge?: number; // seconds
  expires?: Date;
  httpOnly?: boolean; // default true
  secure?: boolean; // default: true in production and on https
  sameSite?: "lax" | "strict" | "none"; // default "lax"; "none" forces secure
  partitioned?: boolean; // CHIPS; forces secure
}
type CookieDeleteOptions = Pick<CookieOptions, "path" | "domain" | "secure" | "sameSite">;

function signedCookie(name: string, options?: SignedCookieOptions): SignedCookie;
interface SignedCookieOptions extends CookieOptions {
  /** HMAC secret; an array rotates keys (the first signs). Default: env LUMIOSE_SECRET. */
  secret?: string | readonly string[];
  /** Accept secrets under 32 bytes (else they throw in production, warn in dev). */
  allowWeakSecret?: boolean;
}
interface SignedCookie {
  readonly name: string;
  get(cookies: Cookies): Promise<string | undefined>; // undefined when the signature is invalid
  set(cookies: Cookies, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): Promise<void>;
  delete(cookies: Cookies, options?: CookieDeleteOptions): void;
}
```

## Context types

```ts
// P is a route pattern ("/books/[isbn]"); without one, params is Record<string, string>.
interface RequestContext<P extends Routes = never> {
  request: Request;
  url: URL;
  params: RouteParams<P>;
  locals: Locals;
  cookies: Cookies;
  env: ServerEnv; // Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>
  platform: Platform; // what the host adds: bindings, waitUntil, client address
}
interface Platform {
  readonly env: PlatformEnv; // the platform's bindings; {} where there are none
  waitUntil(promise: Promise<unknown>): void; // fallback: runs it, reports a rejection
  readonly clientAddress: string | undefined;
}
interface ActionContext<P extends /* a page pattern */ = never> extends RequestContext<P> {
  formData(): Promise<FormData>; // parsed once; 400 if the body is not a form
}
type Middleware = (
  ctx: RequestContext,
  next: () => Promise<Response>,
) => Response | Promise<Response>;
type Endpoint<P extends /* an endpoint pattern */ = never> = (
  ctx: RequestContext<P>,
) => Response | Promise<Response>;
// Annotating with Action hides the result from actionData<typeof action>(): type the parameter
// with ActionContext<P> instead, or use `satisfies Action<P>`.
type Action<P extends /* a page pattern */ = never, Result = unknown> = (
  ctx: ActionContext<P>,
) => Result | Promise<Result>;
type HttpMethod = "GET" | "HEAD" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE" | "OPTIONS";
interface ErrorPageProps {
  status: number;
  error: Error & { status?: number };
}
interface DocumentProps {
  head: JSX.Element;
  body: JSX.Element;
}
interface Locals {} // augment: declare module "lumiose" { interface Locals { … } }
interface PlatformEnv {} // augment: declare module "lumiose" { interface PlatformEnv { … } }
```

## Example

```ts check file=routes/api/session.ts
// src/routes/api/session.ts
import { isHttpError, type Endpoint } from "lumiose";

// Per request: it reads cookies and accepts POST, so it cannot be prerendered (LUM5005).
export const mode = "server";

export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/session"> = ({ cookies }) =>
  Response.json({ theme: cookies.get("theme") ?? "light" });

export const POST: Endpoint<"/api/session"> = async ({ request, cookies }) => {
  try {
    const { theme } = (await request.json()) as { theme: string };
    cookies.set("theme", theme, { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 });
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (isHttpError(error)) throw error;
    return Response.json({ error: "Invalid JSON" }, { status: 400 });
  }
};
```

<!-- source: reference/server.md -->

# `lumiose`: server rendering

> `renderToStream` and `renderToString` render components to HTML under the `node` entry of `lumiose`; `lumiose/server` is the server half of the compiler-runtime contract.

Most apps never call these directly: the request handler (and `lumiose dev` / `lumiose build`) does.
Use them for custom servers, tests and tools. Concepts:
[Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md).

## renderToStream

```ts
function renderToStream(
  root: () => unknown,
  options?: RenderToStreamOptions,
): Promise<RenderedShell>;

interface RenderToStreamOptions {
  /** Aborts the render: rejects a pending shell, ends the stream and aborts getAbortSignal(). */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** SSG/prerender: render every Suspense boundary into the shell; no fallbacks, no stream. */
  resolveAll?: boolean;
  /** CSP nonce for the $swap scripts and strict-mode <style> rules. */
  nonce?: string;
  /** CSP strict mode: style props become nonce'd <style> rules. */
  strictStyles?: boolean;
  /** Maps an island module specifier to its URL for modulepreload hints. */
  islandUrl?: (specifier: string) => string;
  /**
   * URL of the island loader (lumiose/dom/loader). A page with islands gets it once, as
   * <script type="module" async>: in `head` when the shell has islands, else in the first
   * streamed chunk with island records. Default: none (islands render but do not hydrate).
   */
  loaderUrl?: string;
  /** Errors of streamed boundaries that no ErrorBoundary handled. Default: console.error. */
  onError?: (error: unknown) => void;
  /**
   * Prepended to every useId() of the render, its islands included (they reuse it when they
   * hydrate). Keeps the ids of several renders or apps on one page apart. Default: "".
   */
  idPrefix?: string;
}

interface RenderedShell {
  /** Collected <Title>/<Meta>/<Head> HTML, modulepreload hints and strict-mode styles. */
  head: string;
  /** The shell HTML, followed by the shell's island records. */
  body: string;
  /** Streamed boundary chunks to append inside <body>; null when nothing is pending. */
  stream: ReadableStream<string> | null;
}
```

Renders `root` shell-first (decision-19): resolves once everything outside `<Suspense>` is ready,
and rejects with the first error thrown while rendering the shell (so the caller can render an
error page with the right status). The stream then delivers each boundary as it resolves, out of
order.

## renderToString

```ts
function renderToString(
  root: () => unknown,
  options?: Omit<RenderToStreamOptions, "resolveAll">,
): Promise<string>;
```

Renders everything resolved (no fallbacks, no stream) and returns the body HTML. Used for
prerendering and tests.

Both are server-only: in the browser build of `lumiose` they throw `LUM4003`. With `idPrefix`, the
island records carry the prefix, so [`useId()`](reactivity.md#useid) returns the same ids after
hydration.

## `lumiose/server`

The server runtime that compiled server code imports (`ssr`, `escape`, `insert`, `list`, `branch`,
`branchArm`, `createComponent`, `island`, `$await`, …). It is the compiler-runtime contract, not an
application API: its members may change between versions without notice. It also re-exports
`renderToStream` and `renderToString`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { renderToStream } from "lumiose";

function App() {
  return <h1>Hello</h1>;
}

export async function handle(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const { head, body, stream } = await renderToStream(() => <App />, { signal: request.signal });
  const encoder = new TextEncoderStream();
  const writer = encoder.writable.getWriter();
  void (async () => {
    await writer.write(`<!doctype html><html><head>${head}</head><body>${body}`);
    if (stream) for await (const chunk of stream) await writer.write(chunk);
    await writer.write("</body></html>");
    await writer.close();
  })();
  return new Response(encoder.readable, {
    headers: { "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" },
  });
}
```

<!-- source: reference/dom.md -->

# `lumiose/dom`

> `render` renders a component tree into a DOM element. The rest of `lumiose/dom` is the client half of the compiler-runtime contract that compiled code imports.

## render

```ts
function render(code: () => JSX.Element, container: Element, options?: RenderOptions): () => void;

interface RenderOptions {
  /** Prepended to every useId() of the app: keeps the ids of several apps on one page apart. */
  idPrefix?: string;
}
```

Renders `code()` into `container` (appended after its existing content) under a new root owner, and
marks the container as a delegation boundary. Returns a disposer that disposes the owner and
removes the rendered nodes. With the Vite plugin, an entry module that imports `render` re-renders
the app on hot updates. Solid's `render` has the same signature, without `options`.
[`useId()`](reactivity.md#useid) in the app returns `idPrefix` followed by a counter.

## Compiler-runtime contract

`template`, `bind`, `insert`, `insertText`, `branch`, `list`, `selector`, `createComponent`, `mergeProps`,
`restProps`, `spread`, `delegateEvents`, `listen`, `attach`, `bindValue`, `bindChecked`,
`useRef`, `$async`, `$await`, `$leave` and friends are what the compiler emits calls to. They are
not an application API and may change between versions; write JSX instead.

## `lumiose/dom/hydrate`

```ts
function hydrate<P extends object>(
  component: Component<P>,
  props: P,
  start: Node,
  end: Node,
  awaits?: Record<string, unknown>,
  slots?: readonly string[],
  fresh?: boolean,
  idPrefix?: string,
): () => void;
```

Hydrates the server-rendered range between the comments `start` and `end` (an island's
`<!--l:ID-->` and `<!--/l:ID-->`): it renders `component` with `props`, and the compiled code
claims the server's nodes instead of creating new ones, so element identity, focus and text
selections survive. Returns a disposer.

- **Awaits are replayed.** `awaits` maps each first-run `await` of an async component to the value
  the server recorded (`"instancePath:site:occurrence"` keys), so hydration does not fetch again.
  The awaited expression still runs for tracking, with its fetch held off: when a signal it reads
  changes later, the component re-runs and fetches as usual.
- **Slots** (`slots`, the names of children and JSX props) become props holding the server's HTML:
  the nodes rendered inline (`<!--l:s:NAME-->…<!--/l:s-->`) are adopted where the island renders
  the slot; a slot the server did not render comes from its `<template data-l-slot="NAME">` when
  the island renders it later.
- **Mismatch.** When the client renders a different structure than the server's (another branch,
  element or list length), the island is disposed, its range cleared and rendered on the client;
  in dev, [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md) is logged. A missing await record makes the client await
  again (also LUM4006 in dev).
- `fresh` (`client:only`) renders on the client without claiming.
- **Ids.** [`useId()`](reactivity.md#useid) returns the server's ids while the island hydrates: they
  come from the island id (in `start`) and each component's position. `idPrefix` is the server
  render's (the island record's `idPrefix`).

Importing `lumiose/dom/hydrate` also installs the hydration cursor that the compiled walk uses. Only
the island loader and hydrating entries import it; bundles that never hydrate do not include it.

## `lumiose/dom/loader`

The island loader: a client entry, with no exports, that `lumiose dev` and `lumiose build` add to every
page that renders an island (`<script type="module" async>`, see [Islands](../concepts/islands.md));
with your own server, pass its URL as `renderToStream(root, { loaderUrl })`. It imports the app's
island manifest (`virtual:lumiose/islands`, from `@lumiose/vite`), and:

- reads the island records (`<script type="application/json" data-l-islands>`) as each streamed
  chunk arrives, and finds each island's range;
- arms its trigger: `client:load` and `client:only` at once, `client:idle` on
  `requestIdleCallback` with a 2 s timeout (a busy main thread cannot leave the island inert), `client:visible` when the range's first element intersects the viewport
  (the value is the `rootMargin`), `client:media` when the query matches;
- waits for an island whose range still holds a streamed `<Suspense>` fallback until its content
  (and the await records sent with it) arrives;
- imports the island's module and calls `hydrate()`;
- catches `click`, `input`, `submit` and `keydown` on an island that is not hydrated yet: it
  hydrates that island at once and dispatches the events again on their targets afterwards (an
  `input` restores the value typed meanwhile).

Islands inside slots that an island inserts later are hydrated when they appear.

## Example

```tsx check
import { signal } from "lumiose";
import { render } from "lumiose/dom";

function App() {
  const name = signal("world");
  return <input bind:value={name} placeholder={`Hello, ${name()}`} />;
}

render(() => <App />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

<!-- source: reference/router.md -->

# `lumiose/router`

> The client router for `spa` routes, built on the Navigation API: `<Link>`, `navigate()`, reactive `params()`, `route()`, `searchParams()`, `url()` and `isNavigating()`, persistent layouts, transitions that hold the old page, scroll and focus restoration, and a client-side `_404`.

`lumiose/router` works inside `spa` routes (`export const mode = "spa"`, or `lumiose({ mode: "spa" })`
for the whole project); `<Link>` works on MPA pages too (see [Link](#link)). Pages and layouts of an SPA import it like any module; on the server
(`ssr` pages, rendered per request or prerendered at build time) the same names read the request: `params()`, `route()`, `url()` and `searchParams()` return the
request's values, `<Link>` renders its `<a>`, `isNavigating()` is `false`, and `navigate()` and
`searchParams.set()` throw (call them from event handlers and effects). Concepts:
[Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md).

## Components

### Link

```ts
function Link(props: LinkProps): JSX.Element;

type LinkProps = Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "children"> & {
  href: string;
  /** Default "hover" in spa pages; on MPA pages, lumiose({ prefetch }). */
  prefetch?: "hover" | "viewport" | "none";
  children?: JSX.Element;
};
```

An `<a href>` with every attribute and event of `<a>`. The router navigates plain `<a>` links too;
`<Link>` adds:

- **Prefetch.** It loads the target route's modules ahead of the click: when the pointer enters
  the link or it gets focus (`hover`), when it enters the viewport (`viewport`), or not (`none`).
  Data still loads when the page renders. `spa` pages get no speculation rules, so this is the
  prefetch of their links.
- **On MPA pages** (static and server routes) there is no router: `<Link>` renders a plain `<a>`,
  outside islands without any JavaScript, and `prefetch` sets how the page's speculation rules from
  `lumiose({ prefetch })` treat it ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)). The `<a>` gets
  `data-l-prefetch="<level>"`; the rules skip `none` links, prefetch `viewport` links with `eager`
  and `hover` links with `moderate` eagerness, and give unmarked links (`<Link>` without
  `prefetch`, plain `<a>`) the project default. With `lumiose({ prefetch: "none" })`, only pages that
  have `hover` or `viewport` links get rules. Browsers prefetch URLs: a `none` link to a URL that
  another link on the page prefetches does not stop it.
- **`aria-current="page"`** while its path is the current URL's path (style it with
  `a[aria-current="page"]`).

Build `href` with [`href()`](app.md#href) so the route and its params type-check.

## Navigation

### navigate

```ts
function navigate(href: string | URL, options?: NavigateOptions): Promise<void>;

interface NavigateOptions {
  /** Replace the current history entry instead of adding one. */
  replace?: boolean;
}
```

Navigates on the client when `href` belongs to the current SPA, else loads the document. Resolves
once the new page is on screen (its async content ready), or when another navigation supersedes
it. Browser only. Only `http:` and `https:` URLs (relative ones included) navigate: any other
scheme, such as `javascript:`, throws a `TypeError`.

### isNavigating

```ts
function isNavigating(): boolean;
```

Whether a navigation is in flight: from the click until the new page is on screen. Reactive, and
counted by [`isBusy()`](reactivity.md) (decision-20).

## Route state

### params

```ts
function params<P extends Routes = never>(): RouteParams<P>; // untyped: Record<string, string>
```

The current route's params, reactive: `params<"/songs/[id]">().id`. Pages also receive them as
`props.params`.

### route

```ts
function route(): Routes | undefined;
```

The matched route pattern, reactive: `route() === "/songs/[id]"`. Compare patterns instead of
matching `url().pathname`; typegen makes an unknown pattern a type error. `undefined` on a `_404`
page for an unknown URL (a matched route that throws `notFound()` keeps its pattern).

### url

```ts
function url(): URL;
```

The current URL, reactive. Do not mutate it.

### searchParams

```ts
interface SearchParams {
  (): URLSearchParams;
  set(
    next: SearchParamsInit | ((current: URLSearchParams) => SearchParamsInit),
    options?: NavigateOptions,
  ): Promise<void>;
}
const searchParams: SearchParams;

type SearchParamsInit =
  | URLSearchParams
  | string
  | Record<string, string | number | boolean | readonly string[] | null | undefined>;
```

`searchParams()` is the current URL's query, reactive (a new object per change). `searchParams.set()`
navigates to the current path with a new query, keeping the scroll position; `null` and
`undefined` values are left out. It adds a history entry unless `{ replace: true }`.

While a page is still loading during a navigation, `params()`, `route()`, `url()` and `searchParams()` called in it
(and its props) already describe the page it is loading; everything else keeps the shown URL until
the new page is on screen.

## Behaviour

- **Interception.** The router handles same-document navigations to URLs of its SPA: link clicks,
  `navigate()`, back/forward and (with the Navigation API) `GET` form submissions. URLs of other
  routes (`static` or `server` pages, endpoints, other SPAs) load the document. Without the
  Navigation API, a History API fallback intercepts link clicks and `popstate`; it is a chunk of its
  own that only those browsers load, shortly after the SPA starts (a click before it loads is a
  document navigation).
- **Persistent layouts.** A layout's `children` is the outlet. Layouts the old and the new page
  share stay mounted with their state; the first level that differs (another file, or other
  values of the params in its path, such as `songs/[id].stsx` for another song) is replaced. A
  navigation that only changes the query keeps every level and updates `searchParams()`.
- **Transitions.** The new page is created off-screen. The old page stays until the new page's
  async content (async components and resources outside a `<Suspense>` of the new page) is ready;
  then the URL signals change and the pages swap in one step. A `<Suspense>` inside the new page
  shows its fallback instead.
- **Scroll and focus.** After a navigation the page scrolls to the top (or to the URL's `#hash`)
  and focus moves to the document (or the first `[autofocus]` element); back/forward restore the
  scroll position. `searchParams.set()` keeps both.
- **Errors.** `notFound()` and unknown URLs render the nearest `_404` page of the SPA; other errors
  its `_error` page (`{ status, error }` props), with the layouts kept. A thrown `redirect()`
  navigates. Without such a page, a minimal built-in error page replaces the SPA. A `_404` that
  the server rendered at the URL of a prerendered page with params (`404.html` on a static host)
  renders that page instead: see
  [Prerendered SPA routes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#prerendered-spa-routes).
- **`invalidate()`** from `lumiose` re-runs the SPA's async components and resources (they keep
  their UI meanwhile) and resolves once they settled. `submit()` redirects navigate through the
  router, and a successful `submit()` invalidates (on MPA pages it does not: that would reload).
- **Stale modules.** A page module that fails to load (an old chunk after a deploy) loads the URL
  as a document instead.

## Example

```tsx check file=routes/music/_layout.tsx
// src/routes/music/_layout.tsx: an SPA under /music, with a persistent layout
import { href, type LayoutProps } from "lumiose";
import { Link, isNavigating } from "lumiose/router";

export const mode = "spa";

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/music">) {
  return (
    <div class="app">
      <nav>
        <Link href={href("/music")}>Songs</Link>
        <Link href={href("/music/settings")} prefetch="viewport">
          Settings
        </Link>
      </nav>
      {isNavigating() && <progress />}
      <main>{props.children}</main>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/music/index.tsx
// src/routes/music/index.tsx: a filter kept in the query
import { searchParams } from "lumiose/router";

export default function Songs() {
  const query = () => searchParams().get("q") ?? "";
  return (
    <input
      type="search"
      value={query()}
      onInput={(event) =>
        searchParams.set({ q: event.currentTarget.value || null }, { replace: true })
      }
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/music/settings.tsx
// src/routes/music/settings.tsx
import { href } from "lumiose";
import { navigate } from "lumiose/router";

export default function Settings() {
  return <button onClick={() => navigate(href("/music"), { replace: true })}>Done</button>;
}
```

See also: [Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md),
[`lumiose`: app layer](app.md).

<!-- source: reference/vite.md -->

# `@lumiose/vite`

> The Vite 8 plugin: compiles `.stsx` and `.tsx` with the Lumiose compiler, picks the `lumiose` entry per Vite environment, reports diagnostics in the overlay and reloads on edit.

Install it next to `lumiose` and Vite: `pnpm add -D @lumiose/vite vite`.

## lumiose()

```ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";

function lumiose(options?: LumioseOptions): Plugin[];

interface LumioseOptions {
  /** Modules compiled by Lumiose. Default: .stsx and .tsx files. */
  include?: RegExp;
  /** Modules left to Vite. Default: anything in node_modules. */
  exclude?: RegExp;
  /** The project's default route mode; a layout's or route's `export const mode` overrides it. */
  mode?: "static" | "server" | "spa"; // default "static"
  /** Whether spa routes render their content on the server (false: the shell only). */
  ssr?: boolean; // default true
  /** Whether spa pages that render on the server are prerendered at build time; a layout's or page's `export const prerender` overrides it. */
  prerender?: boolean; // default false, and not with ssr: false
  /** Trailing slashes of page URLs: "always"/"never" redirect to the canonical form. */
  trailingSlash?: "ignore" | "always" | "never"; // default "ignore"
  /** The origin check of form posts (on by default); false turns it off. */
  csrf?: false | { allowedOrigins?: readonly string[] };
  /** `.svg` imports as inline components; false leaves them to Vite (URLs). */
  svg?: boolean | { optimize?: boolean | SvgoConfig; currentColor?: boolean }; // default true
  /** `.md` imports as components; the hook validates or transforms each file's frontmatter. */
  md?: boolean | { frontmatter?(data: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: { file: string }): unknown }; // default false
  /** `.html` imports as components. */
  html?: boolean; // default false
  /** Cross-document View Transitions between MPA pages (not under reduced motion). */
  viewTransitions?: boolean; // default false
  /** Speculation rules that prefetch the same-origin links of MPA pages. */
  prefetch?: "hover" | "viewport" | "none"; // default "hover"
  /** A strict Content Security Policy: nonces per response, hashes for prerendered pages. */
  csp?: "strict";
  /** Response headers: a record for every response, or rules by path (below base). */
  headers?: Record<string, string> | { path: string; headers: Record<string, string> }[];
  /** Request body limits, in bytes or "512kb"/"1mb": larger requests get 413. */
  limits?: { body?: number | string; upload?: number | string }; // default { body: "1mb", upload: "10mb" }
}
```

The project options (`mode`, `ssr`, `prerender`, `trailingSlash`, `csrf`, `viewTransitions`,
`prefetch`, `headers`, `limits`) are
read by `lumiose dev`, `lumiose build` and `lumiose routes`/`check` from the plugin's `api.options`.
Invalid values and unknown option names throw when the config loads, as does `prerender: true`
with `ssr: false` ([prerendered SPA routes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md#prerendered-spa-routes)). `csp: "strict"` is
described in [Security](../concepts/security.md): nonces on every inline script and style Lumiose
writes and on those written in JSX, static `style` strings as nonce'd rules, a `Content-Security-Policy` header for pages rendered per request, and a hash policy
`<meta>` in prerendered pages. `allowedOrigins` takes full
origins such as `"https://app.example.com"`, without a path or trailing slash.

**Response headers** (`headers`). Declare them once: a record applies to every response; rules
apply to the paths they match, below Vite's `base` (`*` matches one segment, `**` any number,
later rules win for the same header). `lumiose dev`, `lumiose preview` and `@lumiose/adapter-node` send
them on every response, static files included, and `lumiose build` writes them to
`dist/client/_headers`, the file Netlify and Cloudflare Pages read (`**` becomes `*`, a `*`
segment a `:name` placeholder). Headers that middleware, endpoints or `response().setHeader()` set
win. Two headers are sent by default, as Rails and Django do: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; give them another value in `headers`, or `""`
to remove one (`_headers` gets `! name`).

**Body limits** (`limits`). `body` caps URL-encoded forms, JSON and any other non-multipart
request body (default `"1mb"`), `upload` caps `multipart/form-data` bodies (default `"10mb"`). A
route's `export const limits = { upload: "100mb" }` overrides them for its requests. See
[Security](../concepts/security.md).

```ts
lumiose({
  headers: [
    { path: "/**", headers: { "cross-origin-opener-policy": "same-origin" } },
    { path: "/admin/**", headers: { "x-robots-tag": "noindex" } },
  ],
});
```

| Deployment                       | Where the headers come from                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumiose dev`, `lumiose preview` | `lumiose({ headers })`                                                              |
| `@lumiose/adapter-node`          | `lumiose({ headers })`, from the build (`config.headers` of `dist/server/entry.js`) |
| Netlify, Cloudflare Pages        | `lumiose({ headers })`, as `dist/client/_headers`                                   |
| Other static hosts and CDNs      | The host's own header configuration, copied from `lumiose({ headers })`             |

Per-response headers that depend on the request belong in middleware or `response().setHeader()`.

MPA navigation ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)): the page documents that `lumiose dev` and
`lumiose build` render get, in `<head>`:

- `viewTransitions: true`:
  `<style>@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){@view-transition{navigation:auto}}</style>`,
  on every page, `spa` pages included (their client navigations are not cross-document).
- `prefetch`: a `<script type="speculationrules">` on every page except `spa` pages, whose
  `<Link prefetch>` prefetches instead. It matches the links below Vite's `base` (`href_matches`),
  except the URLs of endpoints, with `moderate` eagerness for `"hover"` (the pointer rests on the
  link, or it is pressed) and `eager` for `"viewport"` (as soon as the browser sees fit: desktop
  Chromium on a brief hover, mobile Chromium as links enter the viewport); `"none"` emits nothing.
  On a page with `<Link prefetch>` links (marked `data-l-prefetch`), the rules give each level its
  own `selector_matches` rule, and the default's rule skips links marked otherwise; with `"none"`,
  only such pages get rules ([`lumiose/router`](router.md#link)).

Both are inline elements: a Content-Security-Policy you set without `'unsafe-inline'` needs
`'inline-speculation-rules'` in `script-src` for the rules, and the hash of the `<style>` in
`style-src`.

What it does:

- Compiles Lumiose modules before Vite's own transform, which is told to skip them. Server consumers
  (SSR) get `lumiose/server` code; everything else gets `lumiose/dom` code.
- Resolves `lumiose` to its `browser` entry in client environments and its `node` entry in server
  environments, and keeps every `lumiose` entry out of dependency pre-bundling, so compiled code and
  the runtime share one module instance. Under Vitest, tests in a DOM environment (`happy-dom`,
  `jsdom`) get the `browser` entry too (see [Testing](../concepts/testing.md)).
- Turns compiler diagnostics into Vite warnings and errors with code frames (the dev overlay).
- Names scoped state: each module-scope `defineState()` binding imported from `lumiose` gets an id
  after its module and export (`/src/lib/cart.ts#cart`), as island refs do, where client code
  (islands, SPA routes) reaches it; pages send only those states' values
  ([`defineState`](reactivity.md#definestate)). Under Vitest it adds a setup file that resets
  scoped state before each test.
- Loads project `.svg` files (`./icon.svg`, `./icon.svg?inline`) as inline components for the
  environment's target, optimised with SVGO (`optimize`: `true` for Lumiose's defaults,
  `preset-default` plus `convertStyleToAttrs`; your SVGO config; or `false`). Scripts, event
  handlers and `javascript:` URLs are always removed and ids prefixed per file. `currentColor:
  true` replaces every colour with `currentColor` (SVGO's `convertColors`, before other
  plugins). `?url` and `?raw` stay Vite's, and `.svg` files in `exclude` (node_modules) keep
  Vite's URL import. See [SVG imports](../concepts/svg.md).
- With `md`/`html`, loads project `.md` and `.html` files as static components: their source
  becomes the Lumiose module `<file>.md.stsx` (`.html.stsx`), compiled like any `.stsx` file, with
  `frontmatter` from `<file>.md?lumiose-frontmatter`, `headings`, relative asset URLs as `?url`
  imports, and client scripts loaded by an island from `<file>.html?lumiose-script`. HTML entries (`index.html`, HTML build inputs) and `public/` files
  stay Vite's. See [Markdown and HTML imports](../concepts/content.md).
- Hot updates: an edited component re-renders in place, in every instance, and the rest of the page
  keeps its DOM and state (`lumiose dev` registers each named component of client code with
  `lumiose/dom/hot`). Only the components whose code changed re-render; an edit outside every
  component of the file (a constant, a helper) re-renders all of the file's components. Components
  hydrated in an island or on the SPA's first page update the same way once hydrated. A module
  whose exports are not all such components (a constant or signal export, a changed export list,
  an async or anonymous default component) falls back to the app entry: a client module that imports `render` from `lumiose/dom` accepts
  updates of every module it reaches and re-renders the app into the same container (component
  state resets; module-level signals of unchanged modules survive), else the page reloads.
- Style blocks become `<file>?lumiose&type=style&lang.css` modules handled by Vite's CSS pipeline.
  Modules that `$` references import constants from are tracked as dependencies of that CSS module.
  A style-only edit, or an edit to such a constants module, hot-updates the CSS without remounting.

> **Status:** compilation, environments, diagnostics, HMR, style-block CSS, `.svg`, `.md` and `.html` imports and the
> project options above are available. The designed options `adapter` and `css` are not.

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumiose from "@lumiose/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumiose({ mode: "server", exclude: /[\\/](node_modules|legacy)[\\/]/ })],
});
```

<!-- source: reference/jsx.md -->

# JSX types and tsconfig

> `lumiose/jsx-runtime` types JSX for `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"`; `lumiose/env` declares the global `JSX` namespace, `import.meta.env` and `Locals`. This page lists the type rules and the tsconfig.

## tsconfig.json

A Lumiose project's `tsconfig.json` extends the tsconfig that Lumiose generates (decision-25). This is
what `create-lumiose` writes, what `lumiose agents init` writes when the file is missing, and what
`lumiose check` prints when there is none:

```jsonc
{
  // Lumiose's compiler options, shadow TSX and route types. lumiose dev, build, check and typegen
  // write the generated file; add your own options below.
  "extends": "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json",
}
```

Add your own `compilerOptions` next to `extends`; they override the generated ones. `lumiose check`,
`lumiose typegen`, `lumiose dev`/`build`, `@lumiose/vite` and the language server write
`.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json`, so it follows the installed Lumiose version and the workspace
layout. `.lumiose/` is not committed: in a fresh clone, run `lumiose typegen` (or `lumiose check`) before
a bare `tsc`.

The generated file, with paths relative to `.lumiose/`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "lumiose",
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "rootDirs": ["..", "./shadow"],
    "types": ["lumiose/env"]
  },
  "include": ["../src", "./shadow", "./types"]
}
```

| Option                                          | Why                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `jsx: "preserve"`, `jsxImportSource: "lumiose"` | The Lumiose compiler transforms JSX; TypeScript only checks it against Lumiose's types.   |
| `rootDirs` with `.lumiose/shadow`               | `import "./X.stsx"` resolves to the shadow file `X.stsx.tsx`.                             |
| `include` `.lumiose/shadow`, `.lumiose/types`   | Shadow files and generated route types are part of the program.                           |
| `types: ["lumiose/env"]`                        | The global `JSX` namespace, `import.meta.env`, `Locals` and `.svg`/`.md`/`.html` modules. |
| `allowImportingTsExtensions`                    | Imports name their extension: `./Card.stsx`, `./tokens.ts`.                               |
| `skipLibCheck`                                  | `lumiose/env` and `vite/client` can both be loaded: their `*.svg` declarations collide.   |

If you set `include` or `types` yourself, they replace the generated lists: keep `src`,
`.lumiose/shadow` and `.lumiose/types` in `include`, and `lumiose/env` in `types`. An array `extends`
keeps a shared base: `["../../tsconfig.base.json", "./.lumiose/tsconfig.generated.json"]` (later
entries win). `lumiose check` reports missing options (`LUM6001`).

### Imports outside `src/` and `.stsx` from other packages

The generated `rootDirs` pair a _mirror base_ with `.lumiose/shadow`. The mirror base is the nearest
directory that contains the project and the Lumiose packages it uses. These are the linked
dependencies that list `lumiose` as a dependency, plus the enclosing package of a project without its
own `package.json`. For a standalone project, it is the project root (`..` above).

Shadows mirror the paths below that base. For example, `apps/web/.lumiose/shadow/apps/web/src/` holds
the app's own shadows and `apps/web/.lumiose/shadow/packages/ui/src/` holds a package's. So a `.stsx`
